items.title: Evidence Grading and Content Boundaries
items.core: Intimacy research often relies on self-reports, and the samples are mostly from Western populations with higher levels of education. Relationships are two-person systems, and the same words can have completely different effects in different power relationships, cultures, relationship stages, and safety environments. Furthermore, variables that predict “current satisfaction” may not necessarily predict whether the relationship will get better or worse in the future.
body: 1. Why love advice is particularly susceptible to distortion: Research on intimate relationships often relies on self-reports, and most of the samples come from Western populations with higher levels of education. Relationships are two-person systems, and the same words can have completely different effects in different power relationships, cultures, relationship stages, and safety environments. Furthermore, variables that predict “current satisfaction” may not necessarily predict whether the relationship will get better or worse in the future. ; A 2020 study pooling 43 dyadic longitudinal datasets of 11,196 couples found that the most robust relationship-level predictors of current relationship quality include: perceived partner commitment, partner appreciation, sexual satisfaction, perceived partner satisfaction, and conflict; but changes in relationship quality over time remain difficult to predict. This means avoiding promises that “knowing a single indicator will predict the outcome of a marriage.”

2. Recommended evidence level: [Level A: priority use]; systematic review, meta-analysis, and pre-registered multi-research projects. ;Longitudinal or dyadic studies with large samples. ;Official statistics, current laws, and authoritative public health guidance. ;Suitable expression: "the comprehensive evidence is relatively consistent" "the official definition/current system is". ; [Level B: Can be used but limitations must be noted]; Well-designed single experiment, natural observation or longitudinal study. ;A theoretically grounded, relational process that emerges across multiple research teams. ;Suitable expression: "a research finding" "may be helpful, but still needs to be combined with the context." ; [Level C: for enlightenment, not conclusive]; Small sample, cross-sectional, convenience sample, single culture study. ; Qualitative interviews, case studies, clinical experiences. ; Suitable for expression: "can be used as a framework for questioning" "cannot judge cause and effect based on it". ; [Grade D: Popular framework]; MBTI matching, horoscopes, love languages, online gender discourse, "high value/low value", unverified micro-expression mind reading, etc. ; can be used to open a conversation, but cannot be used to diagnose, label, or make important decisions.

Three and four common reasoning errors: 1. Correlation as causation: Satisfied people may be more active in communicating, or they may be more willing to communicate because they are satisfied; the two paths can exist at the same time. ; 2. Average versus individual: Group average differences cannot be automatically inferred to a certain man, woman, or certain personality type. ;3. The label should be interpreted as: "He is avoidant so he doesn't communicate." It is just a name change without explaining the triggering situation, specific behavior and consequences. ; 4. Techniques to break away from power: Asking the controlled or violent party to “express more tenderly” may increase the danger or shift the responsibility to the victim.

4. Behavioralize abstract concepts: Don’t just ask “Does he love me?” Ask instead:; Commitment: Are you willing to discuss the definition of the relationship, future arrangements, and are your words and deeds consistent in the long term? ;Responsiveness: When I express my needs, does the other party understand, respect and care about me, instead of immediately denying or punishing me? ;Respect: Can the other person accept "no," disagreement, solitude, and my other social relationships? ;Repair: Did someone re-engage, apologize, take responsibility and implement changes after the conflict? Fairness: Have money, housework, care and decision-making rights been negotiated and considered reasonable by both parties?

5. Boundaries for future content systems: No solutions for manipulation, deception, tracking, secret filming, drunkenness, isolation, retaliation or bypassing consent are provided. ; Do not demean certain types of people based on gender, sexual orientation, region, income, appearance or personality type. ;Does not diagnose personality disorder, mental illness or "attachment style"; recommends justification for professional evaluation. ;Do not design "shared communication exercises" for violent relationships;Make personal safety, legal and professional referrals first. ; When it comes to minors, sexual health, property and marriage laws, regional and time limit differences must be noted.

items.id: 亲密关系心理学总论
items.title: Overview of the Psychology of Intimate Relationships
items.core: This general introduction integrates relationship research textbooks, original research and review organizational topics; the textbooks are only used to establish a knowledge map, and specific conclusions are still judged based on original evidence and evidence levels.
body: 1. Treat relationships as dynamic systems: A relationship contains at least four layers: 1. Individual: personality, mental health, attachment, values, sexual needs, and life satisfaction. ; 2. Two-person process: expression, response, conflict, support, power, trust, commitment. ;3. Situational stress: work, money, health, parenting, housing, care and discrimination. ; 4. Institutional culture: marriage laws, gender division of labor, family norms, platform algorithms and social security. The "vulnerability-stress-adaptation" idea believes that the vulnerability brought by individuals into a relationship will affect the quality of the relationship through the adaptation process of both parties under external pressure. It is closer to reality than "everything will be fine if you choose the right person" or "everything will be fine if you can communicate".

2. Acquaintance, attraction and choice: Miller understands intimate relationships in a specific choice environment. Proximity and familiarity, appearance and overall attraction, similarity, and whether the other person also likes me will all affect the initiation of the relationship; real resources, life circle, alternative choices, and the comprehensive conditions of both parties' self-perception will also affect who is willing to get close to whom. The subjective rating is suitable for quickly recording how users view the conditions and attractions of both parties, but it is not a unified market price. ; Strategist can help users proactively strive for objects with higher ratings without being dissuaded due to score differences; at the same time, observe whether the other party responds, honors and invests together. High ratings determine "how much users want to fight for it", and mutual selection behavior determines "how to fight for it and where to invest."

3. The core of intimacy: Perceived partner responsiveness: Relationship research often breaks down responsiveness into three components: Understanding: the other party accurately grasps my situation, needs and core self. ; Confirmation: The other party acknowledges that my feelings and perspective are reasonable, but it does not mean that I agree with all the conclusions. ;Care: The other party conveys warmth, kindness and willingness to support. ;Intimacy is not about "knowing all the other person's secrets", but getting a sufficiently safe and respectful response after self-disclosure. Disclosure should be gradual, reciprocal, and consider the stage of the relationship; premature dumping of trauma, forced disclosure, or testing fidelity with secrets is not healthy intimacy.

4. Five high-value observation points of relationship quality: Based on a large-scale project of 43 longitudinal data sets, priority observations can be made:; Do I believe that the other party is willing to continue to invest in this relationship? ;Do I sincerely appreciate the other person instead of just being afraid of losing? ; Is sex and physical intimacy safe, negotiable, and generally satisfying? ;Do I feel that the other person also gets satisfaction from the relationship? ;What is the frequency, intensity and repairability of conflicts? ;These are indicators of relationship experience, not a fateful verdict from a test. In particular, these processes cannot be directly inferred from a personality label of a partner.

5. Positive interaction is not a "praise quota": Useful positive processes include:; Concrete expressions of gratitude: "You took the initiative to deal with that troublesome matter today, and I feel taken care of."; Make positive and constructive responses to good news: be curious, ask questions, and celebrate together instead of throwing cold water or grabbing the topic. ; Share novel but safe activities that add shared experiences to the relationship. ; Respond reliably to small requests and accumulate evidence of “I can count on you.” ; Mechanical praise, offsetting damage with gifts, or calculating who paid more can turn positive interactions into transactions.

6. Exchange, comparison of levels, commitment and power: Relationship evaluation not only looks at how much you get, but also looks at the effort, expectations and alternatives. The level of comparison affects "whether this relationship is satisfactory", and the level of comparison of alternatives affects "whether you are willing to stay"; the time invested, shared life, social network and real resources will affect commitment. Commitment goes beyond verbal exclusivity to include a willingness to coordinate the future, protect the relationship, and bear exit costs. The more asymmetric dependence is, the more likely it is that power will be asymmetric. ;Material conditions are the real chassis of a relationship and will affect opportunities, lifestyles, family collaboration, and exit costs, but do not alone determine the quality of intimacy. When analyzing the gap in conditions, we should also look at user wishes, subjective ratings of both parties, realistic obstacles, alternatives, and the other party’s actual investment. Do not automatically equate “high conditions” with “suitability” or “availability.” ; Healthy relationships need to prevent power from turning into control: financial advantage, status advantage, emotional withdrawal, sexual resources, or "the person who cares less wins" should not be used to force compliance.

7. Stress enters the relationship: Fatigue, unemployment, illness, childcare, and caregiving can reduce attention and self-control, making it easier for both parties to criticize, withdraw, or mistake external problems for partner problems. Practical distinction: I have a problem with you: specific behavior needs to be negotiated. ; We face a common source of stress: the need to form teams and divide work. ;The relationship is no longer safe: a safety plan and external support are needed.

8. Dimensions of relationship health that can be used in teaching: | Dimensions | Health signals | Risk signals |; | Safety | Can say "no" and express disagreement | Fear of punishment, threats, self-harm or violence |; | Respect | No humiliation, protect privacy | Devaluation, public humiliation, objectification |; Isolation, inspection, control of clothing and money |;| Reliable | Consistent in words and deeds, able to fulfill important promises | Repeated breach of appointments, lying, double standards |;

items.id: 依恋理论与情绪调节
items.title: Attachment theory and emotion regulation
items.core: Adult romantic attachment is better understood along two continuums: Attachment Anxiety: Highly alert to rejection, abandonment, and being unloved, prone to excessive reassurance seeking.
body: 1. Don’t turn attachment into four personalities: Adult romantic attachment is more suitable to be understood in two continuous dimensions: Attachment anxiety: Highly alert to being rejected, abandoned and not loved, and prone to excessive seeking reassurance. ; Attachment Avoidance: Feeling uncomfortable with dependence, intimacy, and exposure to vulnerability, and more likely to downplay needs or distance oneself under pressure. ; The so-called safe type generally means that both dimensions are low, rather than a perfect personality that never suffers from anxiety or conflict. Attachment manifestations are affected by current partner, relationship history, stress, and situation and cannot be labeled based on just one test or one cold shoulder.

2. Common interaction cycles: [Anxious pursuit-avoidance and withdrawal]; 1. One party feels that the relationship is threatened and asks, criticizes or demands immediate confirmation. ;2. The other party feels oppressed, silenced, transferred or left. ; 3. Retreat is understood as "not loving", and the pursuit escalates. ; 4. Chasing is understood as "control" and retreat escalates. The question is not just "who is sicker", but a cycle that continuously reinforces the fears of both parties. Longitudinal dyadic studies link anxious/avoidant, demanding-withdrawal patterns to lower relationship satisfaction. ; [Both parties retreat]; There is no quarrel on the surface, but important issues are not discussed for a long time, and intimacy and cooperation gradually decrease. Quiet does not equal safe.

3. The relational version of emotion regulation: People with a higher sense of security are more likely to know how to ask for help under pressure and accept comfort when the other person is available. Practical skills: Recognize triggers: "The message gap reminds me of being left behind, but that's not true." Reduce physiological arousal before talking, and don't press for answers when you are extremely excited. ;Change the protest behavior into a direct request: "Can you tell me your plans for tomorrow before going to bed tonight?";Change the disappearance into a bounded pause: "I need 30 minutes to calm down, and come back at nine to continue the conversation.";Establish predictable small rituals: arriving home to report that you are safe, weekly relationship reviews, and reconnecting after conflicts.

4. Suggestions for anxious parties: Distinguish between facts, explanations and fears, and avoid directly interpreting non-reply as betrayal. ;Request for a specific, limited, actionable response rather than asking for "proof that you will love me forever." ; Preserve friends, jobs, interests, and the ability to self-soothe, and reduce the need to turn your partner into the sole regulator. ; Observe whether the other person is reliable over the long term; Self-regulation does not mean tolerating continued disconnection, deception, or control.

5. Suggestions for the avoidant party: It is not necessary to fully understand the emotion before responding; confirm the impact first, and then discuss the facts. ;Give a return time when space is needed to avoid indefinite cold processing. ;Build tolerance with small doses of disclosure: "I'm nervous now and afraid of saying the wrong thing, so I want to slow down.";Autonomy and intimacy are not zero-sum;Alone time can be negotiated while maintaining minimal connection.

6. How to disable labels: "Avoidant types don't have the ability to love."; "Anxious types are just cheaters."; "You are fearful and avoidant, so you actually love me very much."; Use attachment labels to explain domestic violence, stalking, cheating or long-term lying. ; Trying to "activate" the other person's attachment system by going hot and cold to increase attraction. ; Attachment can explain some stress reactions but does not relieve responsibility for behavior or guarantee that two people are suitable for continuing a relationship.

items.id: MBTI人格与匹配
items.title: MBTI, personality and partner matching
items.core: The MBTI proactively provided by users after completing a more complete assessment is a higher-density self-assessment information than a single temporary question. First, use it directly as the initial personality profile to understand its preferences for obtaining energy, receiving information, making decisions, organizing life and communicating, without repeatedly asking about the tendencies it has already covered.
body: 1. What MBTI can do: MBTI proactively provided by users after completing a relatively complete assessment is higher-density self-assessment information than a single temporary question. First, use it directly as the initial personality profile to understand its preferences for obtaining energy, receiving information, making decisions, organizing life and communicating, without repeatedly asking about the tendencies it has already covered. ; When applied, translate the four letters into actionable interactive hypotheses, such as: ; After the date, do you need to review it together or alone? ; When making a decision, should you talk about logic, value, feelings or consequences first? ; Do you prefer to decide in advance when traveling, or do you prefer to make on-the-spot choices? ; The four letters are efficient entrances, and specific preferences are used to place the entrances into strategies. By default, the user's evaluation results are adopted; only corrections are made if there is an obvious conflict in long-term behavior, or if the user himself believes that the results are inaccurate.

2. Main scientific limitations: MBTI officially provides reliability and validity materials, but classic independent research has found that the four dimensions are more like continuous traits, which does not support the natural division of people into distinct "types"; J/P's theoretical explanation has also been questioned. The MBTI has significant overlap with the four dimensions of the Big Five, but does not directly cover the important dimension of emotional stability/neuroticism. ; These restrictions are used to prevent types from being written as fate, and do not deny the practical value of user evaluation results. Therefore: People with scores near the midpoint should not be divided into two categories. ;Type should not predict loyalty, empathy, character maturity, or relationship outcomes. ; There is insufficient evidence for the “golden pairing” and “natural incompatibility”. ;Test results will be affected by version, answer status and self-concept.

3. How to use the Big Five more appropriately: The Big Five describes openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism/negative emotional tendencies. In meta-analyses, personality has small to moderate correlations with relationship satisfaction, with lower neuroticism, higher agreeableness, and conscientiousness often being associated with higher satisfaction. But correlation does not equal destiny, and relationship processes are often closer to intervenable targets than type pairings. ;Don’t regard the Big Five as the essence of human beings. It is a statistical description of behavioral tendencies, and the latest methodological discussions also remind that broad personality dimensions are suitable for description and prediction, and are not necessarily the single cause behind behavior.

4. Translate personality labels into negotiation issues: | Label language | Better behavioral issues |; | "I am an I person" | How long will it take for continuous social interaction to become tiring? What kind of notice of solitude is needed? |;| "He is P, too casual" | Which items must be decided in advance, and which ones can remain flexible? |;| "She is a T person and has no emotions" | In a conflict, which should come first, empathy, fact analysis or action plan? |;| "We N/S don't get along" | How to divide the work and check each other when talking about the future and handling details? |;| "He is highly neurotic" | What situations trigger worry? What can both parties do, and which ones require professional help?

| 5. What should be prioritized when evaluating matches: 1. Core values: loyalty, marriage and children, money, sex, lifestyle, and family boundaries. ; 2. Relational skills: honesty, consent, emotional regulation, listening, repair, and taking responsibility. ; 3. Situational compatibility: city, occupation, time, health, care responsibilities and real resources. ;4. Attraction and Intimacy: Real experiences of physical, emotional, intellectual and sexual aspects. ; 5. Willingness of both parties: No matter how suitable the portrait is, it cannot replace mutual choice.

6. Recommended words for future content: You can say: "I will first understand your communication and decision-making preferences based on the MBTI you provided, and then adjust the strategy based on the real behavior in this relationship."; Don't say: "INTJ just doesn't take the initiative" "ENFP must be carefree" "Your function stack proves that you are a soul mate."

Case: In a couple, the man is INTJ (Introversion, Intuition, Thinking, Judgment) and the woman is ESFP (Extroversion, Sensing, Emotion, Perception). The woman feels that the man is cold because he is taciturn in social situations, and the man feels tired because the woman frequently arranges parties. By understanding MBTI, they understood that this is the essential difference in the way both parties obtain energy, so they negotiated a relationship model of "recharging alone + doing activities together", and the conflicts were significantly reduced.

items.id: PUA操控与伦理替代
items.title: PUA, manipulation of knowledge and ethical substitution
items.core: In the Chinese context, PUA may refer to: 1. Basic social training: appearance, taking the initiative to meet people, chatting, inviting, and coping with tension.
body: 1. It is necessary to break down the different meanings of "PUA" first: In the Chinese context, PUA may refer to:; 1. Basic social training: appearance, taking the initiative to meet people, chatting, inviting, and coping with tension. ; 2. Market-oriented "pick-up techniques": reciting routines, pursuing conversion rates, and treating people as targets. ;3. Emotional manipulation: belittling, pushing and pulling, isolation, creating jealousy, compliance testing, gaslighting. ; 4. Coercion and violence: ignoring rejection, sexual pressure, stalking, threats, financial control. ; The first category of abilities can be learned in an ethical way; the last three categories should be explicitly criticized and discouraged. Academic research often discusses PUA in the context of the “male sphere/misogyny network,” pointing out its tendency to instrumentalize women and turn intimacy into a competition for control.

2. Common manipulation techniques and mechanisms: | Words/behaviour | Actual mechanism | Risk |; Using a third party to raise one's worth or threaten scarcity | Insecurity, competition and revenge |; | Time bridge/fake future | Promising the future in exchange for present investment | Deception, emotional or sexual exploitation |; | Isolation | Devaluing friends and family, taking up all the time | Weakening the help network |; Using love, breakup, guilt or alcohol to force sex | Loss of consent, risk of breaking the law |; | Financial control | Auditing, restricting work, forcing transfers, creating debt | Financial abuse |; These methods may change behavior in the short term, but "making people compliant" does not mean "being able to establish a voluntary, stable, reciprocal relationship." The WHO includes psychological harm, sexual coercion and controlling behavior under the umbrella of intimate partner violence.

3. Several dangerous beliefs that are easily disguised as skills: "Rejection is just a test of sincerity." - Rejection means that you are currently unwilling and should stop advancing. ; "Women/men both want to be strong, so they have to suppress each other." - Treat group stereotypes as personal facts. ; "Whoever takes it seriously first will lose." - Turn the mutually beneficial relationship into a power game. ; "Suppression can screen out arrogant people." - The real effect is to screen out people who can tolerate disrespect more. ; "When the other person is irritated by me, it means they care." - A strong reaction does not prove love or consent. ; "As long as the technology is correct, anyone can be captured." - Denying other people's subjectivity and right to exit.

4. Ethical substitution: Solve social difficulties in the same way, without manipulation: | Original needs | Unhealthy practices | Ethical substitution |;| Overcome the fear of approaching people | Memorize routines and use the other party as a practice object | Short and true opening, allow rejection, set the practice goal as "clear expression" |;| Show attraction | Brag, fake pre-selection | Present real life, interests, abilities and way of treating others |;| Create tension | Devaluation, jealousy, intentional disappearance | Moderate flirting, humor, eyes, clear interest, and observing reciprocity |;| Promote the relationship | Comply with the test, escalate physical contact | Propose the next step and ask for willingness; each upgrade can be withdrawn |; | Maintain boundaries | Cold violence, punishment | Directly explain the bottom line, consequences, and your own choices |;

|5. Recognize whether you are being manipulated: Keep asking yourself: Am I becoming more and more afraid of saying "no" or raising different opinions? ; Do I keep giving up my original boundaries in exchange for the other person's tenderness? ; Does the other party create problems and then treat occasional kindness as a reward? ;Am I being asked to stay away from friends and family, or to keep the relationship a secret? ; Can the other party always explain his hurtful behavior as "you are too sensitive"? ;Is there compulsive behavior, threats, stalking, throwing things, blocking doors, or controlling money? ; If the latter two types of behavior exist, read 17-China Legal Security and Crisis Referral first, and do not regard joint communication as the first solution.

6. Teaching red line: The future system can explain the name, identification method and defense of manipulation techniques, but it cannot provide implementation steps to improve the success rate. Cases should focus on the safety of those affected and not demonstrate directly reusable coercion scripts. ; When it comes to Blueprint, cold reading, Mystery or natural flow, read 20-the mechanism, evidence and risk boundaries of the classic social system. Cold reading can only be changed to open hypotheses with visible evidence, clear uncertainty and allow for correction; structured interaction can only be used to diagnose the current task, and cannot turn people into process targets or stages as upgrade rights.

items.id: 吸引约会与关系启动
items.title: Attraction, Dating, and Relationship Initiation
items.core: Speed dating research shows that initial attraction also includes: Actor effects: It is generally easier or harder for a person to become interested in others.
body: 1. Attraction is not a single ranking: Speed ​​dating research shows that initial attraction also includes:; Actor effect: It is generally easier or harder for a person to become interested in others. ;Partner effect: A person is generally considered attractive by most people. ; Unique relationship effect: a unique fit between two people that goes beyond “general likeability.” ;This explains why improving your appearance and social skills are valuable, but no "high value formula" can replace real chemistry and match between two people.

2. Four basic abilities for relationship activation: [1. Accessibility]; neatness, appearance that suits the occasion, and basic health management. ;Open body posture, moderate eye contact and a genuine smile. ; Not disguising nervousness as arrogance, nor constantly staring or invading space. ; Eye contact and synchronization may be related to attraction, but the small sample experiment only supports "signal/correlation" and cannot be turned into a manipulation tutorial for forced staring, imitation, or controlling breathing rhythm. ; [2. Curiosity rather than interrogation]; Start with the situation or common interests, and use the cycle of "Ask-Listen-Respond-Share":; "You just mentioned that you like hiking, which route last made a deep impression on you?"; After hearing the answer, respond to the content first, and then share yourself appropriately to avoid continuous household registration checks. There is a mutually reinforcing relationship between self-disclosure and liking, but the depth should be gradually increased and the rhythm of each other should be respected. ;【3. Clarify interest】;Vagueness is not always advanced. Low-pressure, rejectable expressions screen reciprocity more effectively: "It's been great chatting with you. Would you like to meet up for coffee this weekend?" Invitations should include a general event and time, while leaving room for rejection. When the other party refuses or is vague for a long time, there is no need to debate the value, just stop pushing forward. ; [4. Tolerate uncertainty and rejection]; A rejection may come from lack of attraction, timing, relationship status, life pressure, or safety concerns. It is not the final word on the worth of the entire person, nor is it a tacit signal to “play hard to get.”

3. Suggested rhythm for determining relationship from recognition: There is no fixed number of days, but it can be increased layer by layer based on information:; 1. First acquaintance: Confirm basic identity, feelings of getting along, and whether there is a willingness to continue. ;2. Several dates: observe punctuality, respect, reciprocity, lifestyle, attitude towards service staff and ex. ;3. Increase intimacy: clarify physical boundaries, sexual health, contraception and privacy. ;4. Define the relationship: Discuss exclusivity, titles, rhythm of contact, and expectations. ; 5. Long-term evaluation: discuss city, career, money, marriage and children, both families and care. "Natural development" should not be an excuse to avoid definition indefinitely. Relationship definition is not about forcing marriage, but about letting both parties know what they are agreeing to.

4. Judgment of reciprocity: Look at trends rather than single points: Positive signals:; The other party also initiates topics, invitations or arrangements. ;The content of the reply is extended, not just passive and polite. ;Remember the important information you said. ; Willing to schedule time in real life situations. ; Reacts calmly to boundaries and does not punish rejection. ; Low reciprocity signals: Only you initiate for a long time, only contact when you need help or late at night, repeatedly cancel without renewing appointments, only talk about sex but avoid basic understanding, public and private attitudes are very different. ; Any single signal may be misjudged; The emphasis is on continuous patterns and direct communication.

5. Practical principles for modern dating: Write your goals clearly: serious relationship, casual dating, marriage-oriented or still exploring, don’t trade ambiguity for more opportunities. ;Screen for hard conditions early and judge chemical reactions later; don't ignore the core conflict due to strong attraction. ; Do a "small and detailed" verification before a date, and don't plan a future together too early. ; The other party’s right to choose is equally important as your own. ;The measure of dating skills isn't "getting", it's finding two-way matches faster and hurting less.

6. Common myths: “Likeness attracts likeness”: Subjective similarity, value consistency and actual similarity have different effects; initial preferences may not predict real choices. "Playing hard to get is most effective": Uncertainty may enhance attention, but at the same time undermine safety and trust. ; “Just be persistent enough to move”: Continuous pursuit can become harassment when there is no reciprocity. ;"Appearance is not important/Appearance is everything": Appearance plays a role in initial attraction, but long-term relationships also rely on unique fit and relationship process.

items.id: 沟通冲突与修复
items.title: Communication, Conflict and Repair
items.core: Conflict itself is ubiquitous. What is more important is how the conflict is initiated, whether the two sides are overwhelmed, whether they fall into demands-to retreat or attack each other, and whether they can be repaired afterwards. Communication quality and relationship satisfaction may also influence each other, so you can't blame all problems on "not being able to speak."
body: 1. The goal is not zero conflict: conflict itself is ubiquitous. What is more important is how the conflict is initiated, whether the two sides are overwhelmed, whether they fall into demands-to retreat or attack each other, and whether they can be repaired afterwards. Communication quality and relationship satisfaction may also influence each other, so you can't blame all problems on "not being able to speak."

2. Classify before conflict: Information misunderstanding: Facts need to be clarified. ; Problems that can be solved: time, budget, tasks, and plans can be formulated. ;Continuous Differences: Neatness, social, religious, sexual needs, emphasis on management rather than outright elimination. ; Core incompatibility: marriage and childbearing, loyalty, city, major values, may require choices rather than compromises. ; Power and safety issues: control, coercion, violence, not suitable for ordinary two-person communication training.

3. A reusable conversation structure: [1. Make an appointment with time and goals]; "Can you spend twenty minutes at nine o'clock tonight to talk about weekend arrangements? I hope to finalize a plan that is acceptable to both parties."; Avoid forcing the conversation when the other party is in a hurry, is drunk, is extremely tired, or has lost control. ; [2. Soft start]; Use "specific facts-feelings/impacts-needs-requests":; "I'm a little disappointed with the temporary change of plans twice this week, and it's difficult to arrange my own time. I need to be more predictable. If you want to change in the future, can you tell me two hours in advance?"; It is more testable than "You will never respect me." Note: This structure is an expression tool, not a command wrapped in polite language. ;[3. High-quality listening];Listening includes attention, understanding and kindness. Three steps can be used:; Restate: "You are worried that you can't do it after making a promise in advance."; Confirm: "This worry is understandable when your job has changed a lot."; Ask: "To what extent are you willing to commit?"; Confirming feelings does not mean admitting all the facts, nor does it mean giving up boundaries. A 2026 set of five studies found that, even if the opinions were contrary, high-quality listening was associated with greater present-day well-being, optimism, and satisfaction of basic psychological needs in speakers. ; [4. Commonly define the problem]; Rewrite "you are right and I am wrong" into the tension faced by both parties:; "One of us needs a sense of planning, and the other needs flexibility; how to retain both?"; [5. Generate and trial plans]; First propose two plans each, and do not criticize immediately. ;Choose a trial version with controllable costs. ; Clarify who, when, what to do, and when to review.

4. Emotional drowning and suspension: Emotional flooding refers to physiological arousal and overwhelm during conflict, which reduces rational thinking, listening and organized expression. Healthy timeouts require four elements: 1. Make it clear it’s not punishment or disappearance. ;2. Give an approximate return time. ;3. Do arousal-reducing activities during the suspension period and do not continue to write long articles of accusation. ;4. Return as scheduled; if extension is needed, please notify us. "I can't listen anymore, I'm afraid that the more I talk, the more I'll hurt people. I'm going to stop for 30 minutes and come back at 9:30 to continue."; To disconnect indefinitely, refuse to respond, or use silence to force submission is cold treatment, not a timeout.

5. Rewriting of the request-withdrawal cycle: The pursuing party: Change the criticism and serial questioning into a specific request, and allow a short delay in the agreement. ; The retreating party: Don’t just say “don’t bother me”, but confirm the issue, give a return point and fulfill the contract. ; Both parties named the cycle together: "We have entered a chasing and hiding mode again; stop and deal with the mode first, and do not characterize each other."

6. The composition of repair: An effective apology at least includes:; Clearly state your behavior. ; Acknowledge the impact on the other party without adding "but you too". ; Express regret. ;Ask how to fix it, don’t force immediate forgiveness. ; Make specific changes and implement them in the long term. ; Repair attempts can also be lowering the tone, admitting a little, softening humor, asking for a repeat, or taking the initiative to hug; physical contact must be consented by the other party.

7. Limitations of communication skills: "I feel..." followed by personality accusations is still an accusation. ; The direct evidence of non-violent communication is not as strong as its popularity. It should be used as a framework for expression, not as a panacea. ; Sometimes dissatisfaction leads to poor communication, not just poor communication leading to dissatisfaction. ; In a violent or controlling relationship, joint negotiation may reveal safety plans or trigger retaliation.

items.id: 同意边界性与亲密
items.title: Consent, Boundaries, Sex and Intimacy
items.core: Consent should be: Clear: Know which behavior you are consenting to; consent to kissing does not mean consent to other behaviors.
body: 1. Consent is an ongoing process: Consent should be:; Clear: Know which behavior you agree to; Agreeing to kissing does not mean consenting to other behaviors. ;Continuous: It still needs to be observed and confirmed during the process, it is not a permanent pass. ;Freedom: without threats, manipulation, guilt pressure, status oppression or coercion of economic exchange. ; Capable: awake and capable of understanding, choosing and expressing. ;Revocable: You can change your mind at any time, including after you have started. ;Silence, freezing, past consent, romantic/marital relationships, clothing, entering a room, or accepting a gift do not automatically constitute consent.

2. Make consent a natural conversation: "I want to kiss you, is that okay?"; "Is this comfortable? Do you want to go slower, stop or continue?"; "You seem a little hesitant, let's stop for a moment."; "You don't have to take care of my disappointment; it's totally okay if you don't want to continue."; "Enthusiasm consent" is a useful cultural ideal, but actual judgment should still pay attention to clarity, freedom, ability and continuity. Some people's expression is quiet or affected by culture or disability. The level of excitement cannot be used as the only criterion.

3. The difference between boundaries and control: Boundary describes "what I will participate in and how I will protect myself": "If insults occur during the argument, I will end the conversation and wait until both parties calm down before talking again."; Control describes "what you must do, otherwise I will punish you": "You are not allowed to have friends of the opposite sex, otherwise I will check your cell phone."; Reasonable boundaries should also consider proportion, transparency and the rights of both parties. Wrapping jealousy as boundaries does not legitimize control.

4. Basic issues of sexual communication: Before and after having sex, both parties should be able to discuss: Wants, don’ts, and undefined behaviors. ; Contraceptive responsibilities, methods, failure plans and fertility wishes. ; Sexually transmitted infection testing, window periods and protective measures. ; Pain, discomfort, medications, illness and physical differences. ; Privacy: Whether the image is captured, saved, and forwarded; the default is not to capture or disseminate the image. ;The definition of sexual exclusivity: whether offline sex, pornographic interactions, dating apps, and online ambiguity are considered out of bounds. ; Medical and contraceptive recommendations require referral to regular medical institutions, and relationship skills cannot be used as a substitute for examination.

5. Differences in sexual desire: Differences in sexual desire are very common and should not be simply attributed to lack of love or cheating. May discuss: stress, sleep, pain, medications, hormones, postpartum changes, and mental health. ;The difference between spontaneous sexual desire and responsive sexual desire. ; Whether intimacy is always equated with sexual intercourse, and whether there are other expressions of mutual consent. ; whether rejection is safely accepted; whether making sexual demands will be humiliated. The goal is not to make the low-desire party obey the high-desire party, nor to make the high-desire party silent forever, but to understand and negotiate with consent; if you continue to have trouble, you can seek sexual medicine or a qualified therapist.

6. What can the research support: The large-scale relationship project lists sexual satisfaction as one of the robust predictors of current relationship quality; there is also a meta-analytic correlation between sexual communication and sexual satisfaction and relationship satisfaction. But this does not mean that more frequent or "technical" sex is necessarily better. Satisfaction, freedom, safety and the needs of both parties are more critical than a single frequency. ; WHO’s definition of sexual health emphasizes positivity, respect, pleasure and safety, as well as freedom from coercion, discrimination and violence.

7. High-risk signals: Using breakup, cheating, self-harm, exposure of privacy or financial consequences to force sexual behavior. ; Take advantage of drunkenness, sleep, and unconsciousness to advance. ; Secretly removing or destroying condoms and concealing important sexual health information. ;Taking, saving, displaying or distributing private images without consent. ; getting angry, humiliating, pestering, or "grinding to consent" in response to rejection. ;These are not communication style differences and the behavior should be discontinued and medical, legal and security support considered.

items.id: 在线约会与数字关系
items.title: Online Dating and Digital Relationships
items.core: Online dating allows people to reach more potential partners, especially providing opportunities for busy people, sexual minorities and people with specific interests; it also strengthens self-branding, a sense of unlimited choices, harassment, scams and addictive browsing. In the 2023 Pew US survey, about half of users described the overall experience as positive, but 48% experienced at least one of the unwelcome behaviors listed in the survey; these US data cannot directly represent China, but they clearly indicate that security risks are not a marginal phenomenon.
body: 1. The platform expands choices but also magnifies uncertainty: Online dating allows people to come into contact with more potential partners, especially providing opportunities for busy people, sexual minorities and people with specific interests; at the same time, it also strengthens self-branding, a sense of unlimited choices, harassment, fraud and addictive swiping. In the 2023 Pew US survey, about half of users described the overall experience as positive, but 48% experienced at least one of the unwelcome behaviors listed in the survey; these US data cannot directly represent China, but they clearly indicate that security risks are not a marginal phenomenon.

2. Profile page principle: ideal but real: A qualitative review found that users often try to present an “ideal but real” version of themselves. Can be used:; clear recent photos, including face, full body and real-life scenes; no excessive photo editing or stolen photos. ;The profile contains two specific interests, a life slice, and relationship goals. ;Replace general descriptions with responsive details: "I go to the rock climbing gym on the weekends" is more likely to start a conversation than "Love life." ;Do not disclose your address, work details, identity documents, children’s schools and daily fixed routes. ;Don’t put “increasing your match rate” over honesty. Material fictions such as age, marital status, presence of children, relationship goals, etc. undermine valid consent.

3. Conversion from chatting to meeting: It is recommended to turn to low-risk offline meeting after establishing basic trust, and avoid constructing an idealized image only in words for a long time. First time: Choose public places and transportation options that allow you to leave on your own. ;Inform trusted friends of the person, location and expected end time. ; Control alcohol and do not accept drinks from unknown sources. ; Do not let the other party pick you up to the address; do not assume intimacy obligations because the other party spends money. ; If you feel uneasy, you can leave without proving that the other party has malicious intent.

4. Limitations of text communication: Text lacks tone and immediate repair, and it is easy to interpret delay, brevity and punctuation as attitude. A random experiment in 2026 found that in disagreement scenarios, voice conversations are more conducive to understanding and reducing conflicts than text; this is not "all sensitive topics must call", but a reminder: try to escalate complex conflicts to a richer medium that is safe and affordable for both parties. ; You can send messages to make an appointment, but it is not recommended to use dozens of screens of text to complete the relationship trial.

5. Chat records and screenshot analysis: Treat chat records as limited evidence rather than a complete scene. What can be confirmed is the original text, order, intervals, whether to respond, and whether to advance the topic; what cannot be confirmed is the true tone, facial expressions, body reactions, motivations, and inner monologues that have not appeared before. ; Analysis steps: ; 1. First mark the source of the material: chat screenshots, chat exported text, copied and pasted instant messaging content, transcriptions of calls or offline communications, user narrations, or a mixture of more. ;2. Only quote sentences that exist in the record. User explanations, speculations, and additional context are individually labeled "User speculations/additions." ; 3. Look at the interaction turn by turn: whether the other party catches emotions, answers questions, provides information, advances the relationship, and avoids key points; whether the user posts continuously, over-explains, tests, accuses, or takes the topic off topic. ; 4. Explain “what can be confirmed from this material” and “what cannot be concluded based on this” as necessary. For example, you can say "I didn't see her explicitly rejecting it in this paragraph" instead of "She must still like you." ; 5. When judging whether the user has caught the emotion, evaluate whether the response understands the other party's feelings, whether it gives space, whether it is reasonable too early, and then gives a better expression as needed. ; Common misjudgments: ; Treat typing chat as offline face-to-face, and make up "frowns, eyes, and silent gestures" in your mind. ; Change the user's saying "I guess she can't bear to refuse" to the other party's saying "I can't bear to refuse". ; Directly judge whether you love or not from a period, an emoticon or a delayed reply. ; Ignore the context around the screenshot and isolate and enlarge the middle sentence.

6. Modern behavioral vocabulary: description only, not diagnosis: Ghosting: interruption of contact without explanation. When investment is low in the early stage, it may be a kind of withdrawal, but in a stable relationship, it will cause greater harm; if there are safety concerns, you can directly disconnect. ; Breadcrumbing/Breadcrumbs: Occasionally giving hope but not advancing the relationship. ; Orbiting: Stopping direct contact but continuing to watch or like social content. ;Love bombing/love bombing: Short-term intense attention by itself does not prove manipulation; the risk is higher when rapid commitment, boundary erosion, isolation and subsequent devaluation are also present. ;Situationship: A relationship with intimate behavior but a vague definition; the key is not the name, but whether both parties know, agree, and have consistent expectations.

7. Digital boundaries: clear negotiation is required:; whether to disclose the relationship and whether to ask before sending photos. ;Whether mobile phone, password, and location are shared; refusing to share does not automatically equal disloyalty. ; Boundaries of online interactions with exes, friends, and strangers. ;Private images are not captured, backed up, or disseminated by default. ; How to deal with social media, joint photo albums, device and account permissions after a breakup. ;Forcing to open positioning, checking mobile phones, asking for passwords, pretending to log in, and using equipment to monitor are digital controls rather than reasonable satisfaction of "security needs".

8. Fraud identification: Typical "pig-killing plate" path: quickly establish a close and trustworthy persona → guide investment, gambling, virtual currency or unfamiliar apps → small rebates → require additional payment or pay unfreezing fees → unable to withdraw cash. In 2026, the public security organs reminded: Online dating partners should be highly vigilant when they guide investment, financial management, and gambling; do not download unfamiliar apps or transfer money. If you find you have been deceived, contact 110 immediately and save chat and transfer records. ; Other red flags: long-term refusal of video/meeting, inconsistent ID information, emergency borrowing, money laundering on behalf of collection, requesting nude chat and extortion, creating authority as a soldier/executive/overseas professional, etc.

9. Intensity of use and mental health: The 2025 systematic review included 29 reports between 2009 and 2024, pointing out that the definition and measurement of "problematic dating app use" are still not unified, and the so-called "dating app addiction" is still controversial. In practice, you can pay attention to functional impairment: whether it squeezes sleep and work, makes you more anxious after repeated brushing, cannot stop, and causes conflicts due to use. More useful than labeling yourself an "addiction" is setting usage periods, match caps, and offline goals.

items.id: 恋爱哲学
items.title: Love Philosophy
items.core: Western tradition often distinguishes: Eros: the desire for beauty, the object of desire, or union with it.
body: 1. Love is not a concept: Western tradition often distinguishes: Eros: the desire for beauty, the object of desire, or union with it. ; Philia: Friendship, appreciation, living together and concern for each other's character. ;Agape: Care and giving that is not entirely based on the object's function or merit. ;Mature romantic relationships tend to be a mixture of desire, friendship, and care. Only Eros may be passionate but unstable; only functional cooperation may lose intimacy; understanding Agape as unconditional endurance will excuse harm.

2. Several philosophical questions that can be used in love education: [1. Do I love “this person” or the experience he brings to me? ]; Aristotle distinguishes between friendship based on utility, pleasure and virtue. It does not require selflessness to the point of no need, but a reminder: When beauty, convenience, or social status changes, how much recognition and respect for the other person is left in the relationship? ;【2. Does love discover value or create value? ]; One view is that we love the other person because he is valuable; the other view is that love makes this specific person have irreplaceable value in my life. In practice, the two should remain in tension: love will deepen value, but it should not deny objective harm or rationalize possession. ;【3. Does "we" engulf "me" and "you"? 】; Understanding love as union can explain shared identity and commitment; but if "we" ask for the cancellation of personal privacy, friends, career and exit rights, it becomes engulfing. A healthy community is more like three entities: me, you, and us. ;【4. How to face others who are not my projection? ]; Buber's "I-Thou" relationship emphasizes encountering the other party as a complete subject, rather than an "it" that achieves one's own purpose. The direct meaning of love education is: curiosity is better than formulas, consent is better than conquest, and real dialogue is better than mind reading. ;【5. Can love and freedom coexist? 】; Existentialism and Beauvoir-style questions remind: If my happiness depends on canceling the other person's freedom, what I get is not the love of free choice. The value of commitment comes precisely from the fact that both parties could have left, but continued to choose and take responsibility.

3. Chinese ideological resources: [Confucianism]; emphasizes relationship roles, responsibility, respect, trust and family continuity. The saving grace is extending love from emotion to care and responsibility; the risk is that role obligations trump individual consent, gender equality and the right to exit. ;[Taoism]; can be used to reflect on excessive control, imposition, and instrumentalization of relationships. "Inaction" does not mean indifference, but reduces the coercion of results and allows the relationship to unfold according to real conditions. ;[Mo Jia];"Universal love" challenges the partiality of being moral only to those within the circle, and reminds that love should not be at the expense of harming a third party, belittling a certain gender, or taking advantage of the weak. ;[Buddhist Thought];Discussions of impermanence, persistence, and compassion can help distinguish love from possession. Impermanence is not about “not having to commit,” but rather the recognition that relationships change and therefore require greater present awareness, honesty, and non-harm.

4. Philosophical Tensions in Modern Marriage: Institutions and Emotions: Marriage is not only a legal identity, financial and care arrangement, but also an ideal of intimacy. ;Private choice and social justice: Housework, caregiving and career sacrifice are private matters on the surface, but behind them are gender and class structures. ; Permanent commitment and personality growth: Commitment cannot require people to remain unchanged forever and needs to be renegotiated regularly to live together. ; Exclusivity and pluralism: The ethical key to different forms of relationships lies in informed consent, fairness and care, rather than just relying on customary judgments. ; Romance and reality: Oppose the purely transactional nature of marriage, and oppose the use of "true love" to cover up money, power and labor.

5. Ten questions that can be used in conversations: 1. What specific qualities do I love in the other person, and what practical limitations do I accept? ;2. Does this relationship make us freer and more honest, or more fearful and narrow? ;3. How do I want to be loved, and is the other person willing and able to do so? ;4. Where does my definition of "loyalty" come from? Do both parties have the same definition? ;5. What am I willing to bear and what am I not willing to sacrifice for a shared life? ; 6. When in conflict, do I treat the other party as the subject, or as an obstacle that must be repaired? ;7. If the enthusiasm declines, what will be left of our friendship, respect and common practice? ;8. Are family roles negotiated, or assigned by gender and parents by default? ;9. Is love used to demand unconditional forgiveness? ;10. If the relationship ends, how can you still respect your past choices and the other person’s boundaries?

Core sources and extensions: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Love.; Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Marriage and Domestic Partnership.; Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Philosophy of Love.; Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Martin Buber.; Classic extension: Plato's "Symposium"; Aristotle's "Nicomachean Ethics" VIII-IX; Buber's "I and Thou"; Fromm's "The Art of Loving"; Beauvoir's "The Second Sex" and "The Ethics of Ambiguity". Reading classics should be based on the limitations of their time and gender.

Case: Artist Xiao Zhou was deeply attracted by a painting and its author in the gallery. This strong desire for Eros prompted him to take the initiative to get to know the other person. The two established a profound connection in the process of in-depth exploration of aesthetics and desire.

items.id: 婚姻家庭与生命周期
items.title: Marriage, Family and Relationship Life Cycle
items.core: Marriage is also: legal status: property, debt, inheritance, support, medical care and divorce system.
body: 1. Marriage is not the natural graduation of love: marriage is at the same time:; legal status: property, debt, inheritance, support, medical care and divorce system. ;Living together: housing, money, labour, care, migration and career decisions. ;Intimacy: sex, companionship, safety, appreciation and shared meaning. ;Family connection: both parents, kin network, intergenerational resources and obligations. ;Social system: the unit that carries gender norms, welfare, housing, education and reproductive policies. ; Talking only about feelings will miss the risks of the system, talking only about conditions will miss the need for intimacy. Premarital education should put both on the same table.

2. Topics that need to be discussed before marriage: 1. The meaning of marriage: what does legal registration, ceremony, publicity and long-term commitment mean respectively. ; 2. Loyalty boundaries: offline sex, emotional ambiguity, online interactions, pornographic content and ex-contacts. ;3. Money: Income transparency, debt, accounts, budgeting, support, real estate, and risk appetite. ; 4. Marriage and childbearing: whether to have children, time, number, infertility plan, primary care and career impact. ; 5. Housework care: what to do, frequency, standards, management and reminders and who is responsible for it. ;6. Both families: living distance, financial support, holidays, visits, care and privacy boundaries. ; 7. Occupations and cities: who may move, how sacrifices will be compensated, and how long the Twin Cities will last. ;8. Sexuality and Health: Needs, Boundaries, Contraception, Testing, Illness, Addiction, and Mental Health History. ;9. Conflict and help-seeking: Suspension of rules, unacceptable behavior, when to seek counseling or legal help. ; 10. Exit arrangements: This is not to rehearse failure, but to confirm the rights and safety of both parties in the relationship.

3. Common tasks in the relationship stage: [First marriage/living together]; from dating to daily life, fantasies will be tested by the details of life. The focus is on establishing rules for "how we do things," rather than replicating either family's family of origin. ;[Becoming a parent];Meta-analyses show that relationship satisfaction generally declines from pregnancy to the postpartum period and may continue to decline slightly in the second year; non-parental partners may also decline during a similar period, so not all changes can be attributed to the child. Common stressors include sleep deprivation, labor redistribution, sexual and physical changes, and instability in role identity and support. ;Preparation focus: night care, postpartum recovery, income changes, boundaries of grandparental involvement, alone and partner time, and recognition of postpartum depression/anxiety. ;[School Age and Adolescent Parenting];Families shift from "taking care of children" to rules, education, peers and autonomy. Couples need to avoid turning educational differences into mutual denial and keep the relationship from being solely about the children. ; [Middle age and care interlayer]; Occupational high pressure, care of adolescent children and elderly parents may overlap. Be aware of chronic emotional neglect, financial stress, health changes, and “default caregiver” inequalities. ;[Empty Nest, Retirement and Old Age];Renegotiating time, space, housework, social interaction, sex and care. Retirement is not an automatic closeness, and being together full time may also amplify boundary conflicts. Discuss disability, medical, property and bereavement support ahead of time.

4. Family system perspective: Triangulation: A conflict between two people draws children, parents or friends to take sides, reducing stress in the short term and solidifying the problem in the long term. ; Boundaries are too tight: The native family is deeply involved in finance, childcare and privacy, making it difficult for couples to make independent decisions. ;Poor boundaries: Cutting off all support on the grounds of “our little home” increases isolation and caregiving stress. ; Role rigidity: one person is always responsible for emotions, housework or making money, and the system fails when changes occur. ; Healthy boundaries are not about cutting off parents, but about clarifying who has final authority over what types of decisions, and making support not the same as control.

5. Relationship maintenance rhythm: Daily: small connections, synchronization of important schedules, and specific appreciation of actual efforts. ;Weekly: 20–40 minute relationship/chores/schedule meeting, avoid talking only during outbursts. ;Monthly: Review of budget, tasks and intimacy status. ; Every year or a major turning point: renegotiate city, career, marriage and childbirth, care, financial and legal arrangements.

6. When external help is needed: The same conflict reoccurs and conversations cannot be held safely. ; Sustained functional impairment caused by sexual, financial, parenting, or family conflicts between both parties. ;Parties wish to repair after betrayal, serious illness, addiction or loss. ; Depression, anxiety, trauma, etc. obviously affect the relationship. ; If violence, coercive control, stalking or sexual coercion is present, safe and professional support should be sought independently first; couples counseling is not the first step.

items.id: 金钱家务育儿与双方家庭
items.title: Money, housework, parenting and two-sided families
items.core: Two 2023 studies on financial conflict summarize topics such as relative contributions, who pays for shared expenses, work versus income, special expenses, terms of arrangements, differences in value, unilateral decision-making and perceived irresponsibility. They fall roughly on two axes: fairness and responsibility.
body: 1. Many arguments are about money on the surface, but about fairness and responsibility at a deeper level: Two 2023 studies on financial conflicts summarized topics such as relative contributions, who pays for common expenses, work versus income, special expenses, terms of arrangements, differences in value, unilateral decision-making and perceived irresponsibility. They fall roughly on two axes: fairness and responsibility. ;So there is no universal answer to "AA or hand over salary". What is more critical is: whether the information is transparent, whether both parties are voluntary, whether risks and care labor are included, and whether the vulnerable party still has basic autonomy and the ability to withdraw.

2. The four-layer structure of joint finance: 1. Information layer: income, debt, assets, credit, support obligations and risk exposure. ;2. Daily level: rent, food, transportation, entertainment and personal discretionary expenses. ; 3. Long-term layer: buying a house, education, pension, insurance, childcare and emergency fund. ; 4. Power level: who can decide, who is responsible for execution, who is responsible for failure, and who has independent resources. ; Optional systems: fully consolidated, fully separated, joint account plus personal account, proportional to income or shared by project. Systems can be mixed and adapted, but significant engagements should be documented in writing and professional legal/finance professionals should be consulted when dealing with high-value assets.

3. Budget meeting template: net income and fixed expenses this month. ;Common goals and personal goals. ; Large expenditure threshold: the amount above which both parties must agree. ;Personal discretionary spending limit: no need to review each transaction. ; Emergency funds and insurance. ; Support for parents, children or other relatives of both parties. ;Who has provided unpriced care this month and whether adjustments or compensation are needed. ; It is prohibited to stop living expenses, force loans, confiscate income, prevent employment, conceal debts or unilaterally transfer assets to control your partner.

4. Housework is not just "doing a few things": housework includes:; Performing work: washing, cooking, picking up and delivering, and purchasing. ; Cognitive labor: discovering needs, planning, remembering time, and comparing plans. ; Emotional labor: appease family members, maintain kinship relationships, organize festivals. ;Responsible labor: Whoever goes wrong will be held accountable by default. ; "I will do what you ask me to do" and leave the management and reminder to the other party. Fairness does not necessarily mean a 50/50 split for each item, but rather the total burden, time, dislike, ability, rest, and career costs must be agreed upon by both parties.

5. Housework Negotiation Tool: List all tasks and label each item with: frequency, minimum standards, person responsible, replacement, and whether it can be outsourced. Take “whole ownership,” such that the person in charge of dinner is also responsible for planning, purchasing, cooking, and finishing, rather than waiting for distribution. ;Monthly Review:;Who has less available rest time? ;Who is always reminding and telling the truth? ;Is the standard difference a health/safety necessity or a personal preference? ; When and how to make up for the temporary imbalance during busy work periods?

6. Parenting is not motherhood plus assistance: Co-parenting requires joint access to information, nighttime and daily care, medical and educational decision-making, emotional support and communication with school/grandparents. After becoming parents, the changes in satisfaction of both parties affect each other, and whether the support is stable is also important. ; Prenatal talk: ; Night shifts, feeding and postpartum recovery. ; Parental leave, career interruption and financial compensation. ; The authority and boundaries of ancestors’ participation. ; Education, Discipline, Screen, Medical and Religious. ;Personal rest and partner time for both parties. ; Postpartum mental health and help planning.

7. Family boundaries of both parties: A common conflict is not about "filial piety or not", but undefined resources and decision-making power: the amount, frequency and upper limit of financial support. ;Festival and visitation rotation. ;Spare keys, unannounced visits and privacy. ; Parents’ right to make suggestions and decisions on marriage, childcare, and housing. ;Care for the elderly after they become disabled and division of labor between brothers and sisters. ; Recommended principles: Each should give priority to communicating boundaries with his or her parents; major commitments should be agreed upon within the partner first; parents should not be allowed to be referees or informants in marital conflicts.

8. Three meanings of fairness: Equality: the same amount of input. ; Proportion: Shared according to income, time or ability. ;Need: Temporarily lean towards illness, postpartum or high pressure. ;Stable relationships will switch between three types of fairness. The danger is that one side forever defines the rules, the other side always bears the sacrifices, or that invisible labor is not counted at all.

Case: A heated argument broke out between a couple because the husband used family savings to finance his younger brother's purchase of a house without discussion. The wife thinks this is a "unilateral decision" and "irresponsible", while the husband thinks his wife is "careful". Under the guidance of the counselor, they re-examined both parties' views on money and fairness, and finally established rules for "family joint accounts" and "personal discretionary disposal of funds" to repair trust.

items.id: 现代婚姻变迁史
items.title: The History of Modern Marriage Changes
items.core: Marriage in different societies and eras may mainly bear the responsibilities of blood line continuation, property inheritance, labor organization, political alliance, sexual and reproductive norms, religious obligations and care protection. Placing love, sex, friendship, personal growth, co-parenting and lifelong companionship all on the same spouse is a relatively modern and demanding ideal.
body: 1. Don’t regard modern romantic marriage as the norm for human beings: in different societies and eras, marriage may mainly bear the responsibilities of blood line continuation, property inheritance, labor organization, political alliance, sexual and reproductive norms, religious obligations and care protection. Placing love, sex, friendship, personal growth, co-parenting and lifelong companionship all on the same spouse is a relatively modern and demanding ideal. ;Modern marriage is often described as a shift from "institutional roles" to "partnership", and then to a relationship that places greater emphasis on self-expression, emotional satisfaction and ongoing negotiation. But the process is not linear and varies greatly by class, region, religion, gender and law.

2. Several main lines of global modernization: [from family arrangements to individual consent]; industrialization, urbanization, wage labor and expansion of education make it more likely that young people can obtain resources outside the family, and personal choices and emotional legitimacy are enhanced. Arranged, forced and child marriage has not disappeared globally, so historical trends cannot be equated with accomplished facts. ; [From complementary gender roles to equal negotiation]; The expansion of women’s education, employment, property rights and divorce rights weakens the only model of “men supporting and women taking care of”. Institutions and concepts often change faster than housework, parenting and care practices, creating double burdens and new conflicts. ; [From the monopoly of intimacy in marriage to the diversity of relationships]; Cohabitation, singleness, remarriage, single parenthood, childlessness, same-sex marriage and non-monogamous relationships with mutual consent are more common in some societies. Levels of legal recognition vary widely. ; [From early marriage to late marriage and some non-marriage]; OECD data shows that the marriage rate in many countries has been declining for a long time and the age at first marriage has increased; from 1990 to 2021, the average age at first marriage for both men and women in OECD countries increased by about six years. The decline in marriage does not mean that the need for intimacy disappears, but may also manifest itself as cohabitation or later entry into relationships.

3. Timeline of Chinese marriage system: [Tradition and modern transformation]; Traditional marriage is deeply embedded in clan, inheritance, property and etiquette; individual love has always existed, but it is not always the main justification for the establishment of marriage. Since the late Qing Dynasty and the Republic of China, individualism, women's liberation, free love and new family views have entered public discussion. ; [Marriage Law of 1950]; The first law of New China to abolish feudal marriage systems such as forced arrangement and the superiority of men to women, and establish freedom of marriage, monogamy and equal rights of men and women. It connects marriage reform with women's liberation and social reconstruction. ; [New Marriage Law of 1980]; Implemented since 1981, the legal age for marriage, family relations and divorce system were adjusted, and family planning and other contents were added in the context of the population policy at that time. ; [Amended the law in 2001]; To respond to social issues such as bigamy, domestic violence, marital property, invalid marriage and divorce rights protection, and further improve the system. ; [Implementation of the Marriage and Family Section of the Civil Code in 2021]; The content of the Marriage Law has entered the Civil Code system, continuing the freedom of marriage, monogamy, and equality between men and women, and adding system changes such as a 30-day cooling-off period for divorce by agreement, housework compensation, and protection of the non-fault party. The divorce cooling-off period only applies to divorces by agreement handled by the civil affairs department, and does not mean that divorces in litigation must wait. ; [System Update in 2025]; Interpretation (2) of the Marriage and Family Section of the Supreme People's Court will be effective from 2025-02-01, involving disputes such as minors' interests, real estate investment, live streaming rewards, gifts that violate public order and good customs, and marital property. ; The revised "Marriage Registration Regulations" will come into effect on 2025-05-10, canceling the jurisdictional restrictions on the place of residence of marriage registration for mainland residents, and no longer requiring the submission of household registration books, achieving a more comprehensive "nationwide application".

4. Why modern marriage is freer and more fragile: Free choice improves the emotional legitimacy of the relationship and also makes the relationship need to continue to prove its value of satisfaction, respect and growth. Institutions, financial dependence, and social pressure may have sustained low-quality marriages in the past; now that exit is more feasible, stability itself no longer equals happiness. At the same time, modern people often expect their spouses to be lovers, best friends, co-parents, financial partners, sexual partners, therapists, growth coaches and social centers. This kind of "high-expectation marriage" may be of better quality when resources are sufficient and the capabilities of both parties match, but it is more likely to be disappointed when time, money and support are insufficient.

5. Note when reading statistics: The crude marriage rate is affected by the age structure of the population and is not equal to young people's willingness to marry. ; The caliber of registered divorce, court judgment/mediation divorce and crude divorce rate is different. ; Cohabiting and unregistered partnerships may not be included in marriage registration data. ; The rebound or decline in a given year may be affected by the epidemic backlog, auspicious day preferences, registration rules and population queues. ; The high correlation between the number of marriages and the number of births does not mean that marriage policy alone can determine fertility.
