items.id: 社会发展与家庭变迁
items.title: Social Development and Family Changes
items.core: Don’t interpret late marriage, non-marriage, few children, divorce or living alone as just “conceptual deterioration/progress”. Personal preferences are always embedded in education, employment, housing, care, law, gender norms, demographics and platform technologies.
body: 1. Family changes are the result of a combination of structure and choice: Do not interpret late marriage, non-marriage, few children, divorce or living alone as just "conceptual deterioration/progress". Personal preferences are always embedded in education, employment, housing, care, law, gender norms, demographics and platform technologies.

2. China’s latest background data (as of 2026-07): [Population and Aging]; the National Bureau of Statistics’ 2025 bulletin shows: the national population at the end of the year was 1.40489 million, a decrease of 3.39 million from the previous year; 7.92 million births throughout the year; the population aged 60 and above accounted for 23.0%, and the population aged 65 and above accounted for 15.9%; the urbanization rate of the permanent population was approximately 67.9%. These trends mean that small families face the pressure of childcare, elderly care and cross-regional care at the same time. ;[Family size];The seventh census shows that the average household size in 2020 is 2.62 people, lower than 3.10 people in 2010. Official explanations include more frequent population movements, improved housing and young people living independently after marriage. A smaller household size does not necessarily mean that family ties are weakening. There may be residential separation but the economy and care are still closely connected. ;[Marriage Registration]; In 2024, 6.106 million couples will be legally registered, a decrease of 20.5% from 2023, and the crude marriage rate is 4.3‰. ; In 2025, 6.763 million pairs of marriages will be registered, an increase of 657,000 pairs compared with 2024; 2.743 million pairs of divorces will be registered by the civil affairs department. ;A 2025 rally cannot alone prove a long-term trend reversal. It may be simultaneously related to factors such as the marriageable population, low base in the early stage, zodiac sign/year preference, "national approval" in 2025, and no longer submitting household registration books; the specific cause and effect requires longer time and specialized research.

3. Eight mechanisms that promote family changes: [1. Extended education and a backward pace of life]; the time to receive education increases, stable employment and economic independence are later, and love, marriage and childbirth are synchronized and delayed. The transition from campus to the workplace can also interrupt early relationships. ; [2. Urbanization and mobility]; Population mobility expands the circle of spouse selection, and also results in insufficient distance, housing costs, household registration resources, care distance and social support. Urban anonymity increases personal choice but reduces the matchmaking and supervision of a network of acquaintances. ; [3. Women’s education, employment and renegotiation of gender roles]; Women’s economic autonomy improves their ability to exit unequal marriages and also increases their expectations for partnership-style relationships. If men's family participation and public care do not change simultaneously, dual-income families will experience time poverty and "second-shift labor." ; [4. Housing, employment and economic uncertainty]; The expected costs of weddings, housing, childcare, education and retirement will affect the time to enter marriage and have children. Financial stress can also affect existing relationships through fatigue, conflict, and mental health, not just the “dare to get married.” ; [5. Low fertility and aging]; The reduction in the number of children makes intergenerational resources more concentrated, and may also allow a single adult child to bear more care. Partner selection increasingly involves an assessment of each parent's parental care obligations. ; [6. Rising individualization and emotional expectations]; Marriage has gradually increased its functions of personal happiness, identity and growth from a role that must be completed. People place more emphasis on "emotional value," but this buzzword should be broken down into responsiveness, appreciation, companionship, respect, and shared meaning, rather than requiring partners to infinitely adjust themselves. ;[7. Platform-based dating];App expands the scope of contact and enhances photos, profiles and quick screening. Increased choice may bring opportunities, but also commoditization, self-branding, constant comparison, and security risks. …

4. Common trends and differences in international comparisons: OECD and United Nations data show that many countries have seen a decline in marriage rates, an increase in the age at first marriage, and an increase in cohabitation and multiple family forms. But:;Social acceptance of having children outside of marriage varies widely. ;Whether benefits are based on marriage will change the incentives to get married. ; There are obvious differences in the rights of same-sex marriage, cohabiting partners and protection for unmarried parents. ; Familialist societies may marry later, but they still highly bind childbearing to marriage. ; We cannot take the path of a single Western country as China’s inevitable future.

5. Direct inspiration for love education: extend "personal conditions" to the living system: city, occupation, housing, care and time. ; Treat both families as negotiation objects, rather than automatic enemies or masters. ;Train intimacy skills and institutional literacy at the same time: feelings, money, labor, and law all need to be discussed. ; When discussing gender inequality, focus on the actual division of labor and power, and do not essentialize men and women. ; Respect the choices of singles, never-married, childless and diverse families, and do not put the marriage rate goal above personal well-being.

items.id: 分手背叛与关系修复
items.title: Breakups, Betrayals and Relationship Repair
items.core: Ending a relationship usually doesn't require proof that the other person is a bad person. Core incompatibility, chronic dissatisfaction, depletion of trust, or unwillingness to continue can all be good reasons. Both parties need to mutually agree on the continuation of the relationship, and either party can decide to end it.
body: 1. Breaking up is a relationship decision, not a court decision: ending a relationship usually does not require proof that the other person is a bad person. Core incompatibility, chronic dissatisfaction, depletion of trust, or unwillingness to continue can all be good reasons. Both parties need to mutually agree on the continuation of the relationship, and either party can decide to end it.

2. The basic structure of a decent breakup: When there are no safety risks: 1. Choose a relatively private but safe place and time. ; 2. Use a clear conclusion without creating the illusion of negotiation: "I have decided to end this relationship."; 3. Briefly explain your main reasons, and do not engage in character humiliation or accusations. ; 4. Allow emotions, but do not use the other person’s crying or anger as an excuse to withdraw from the boundary. ;5. Discuss items, housing, finances, pets, social media and follow-up contact. ; 6. Avoid using "maybe in the future" to relieve current guilt, unless there are really clear conditions and wishes. ; If you are worried about violence, door blocking, stalking, threats of self-harm or retaliation, you can end it in a public place, remotely or with the support of a third party, and make a safety plan in advance. Safety takes precedence over "sincerity only comes in person".

3. Recovery from broken love: A large-scale social media language study found that breakup-related cognitive and emotional changes may appear about three months before a public breakup and last for several months afterward; this is not a standard for personal recovery period. Repeatedly monitoring an ex's social media is associated with higher distress, craving, and less growth, but the existing research has mostly been correlational in nature. ;Practical directions: ;Reduce unnecessary contact and social media monitoring, especially if each check worsens the situation. ;Restore sleep, diet, exercise and work structure. ; Connect with trusted friends, but avoid endlessly repeating the same narrative without rebuilding your life. ; Distinguish between "missing" and "suitable for getting back together." ;Write down the relationship facts, satisfactions and damages to prevent remembering only the peaks. ; If severe insomnia, functional decline, thoughts of self-harm, or trauma reactions persist, seek professional help as soon as possible.

4. Evaluation before getting back together: Getting back together doesn’t mean strong emotions are enough. At least check:;Are the issues that caused the breakup in the first place accurately named? ;Is the change a commitment, or is it evidence of behavior that has been in place for some time? ;Have the core values ​​and realistic conditions changed? ;Are both parties free to choose, rather than alone, financially dependent, family pressured or threatened? ; Can new rules be established instead of falling back into old cycles? ;The "honeymoon period" in a violent relationship does not equal repair; occasional tenderness and apology cannot offset patterns of control and violence.

5. What counts as betrayal: Betrayal is a violation of important expectations in a relationship. It is not limited to sexual intercourse, but may also include lying, emotional relationship, technical boundary crossing, leaking secrets, major breach of contract or concealing finances. The definition of "cheating" varies greatly from partner to partner, so it should be discussed up front rather than assumed after the fact.

6. Three stages after discovering betrayal: [Stabilization]; Stop further deception and transgression with third parties (if both parties decide to try to repair it). ;Addressing sexual health, financial and residential security. ; Avoid irreversible revenge or public exposure when extremely excited. ;The injured party does not need to immediately decide to forgive or divorce/break up. ; [Understanding]; Distinguish between explanation and excuse. There is a need to understand how relationship boundaries are violated, how deception is maintained, and what the personal and relationship factors are. Relationship issues can explain the context, but the person committing the betrayal remains responsible for their own choices. ;[Rebuild or End];Repair requires ongoing honesty, appropriate transparency, patience with triggers, acceptance of impact, renegotiated boundaries, and observable change. Small qualitative studies identified high-quality communication, rebuilding safe trust, and forgiveness as common themes, but different partners experience comfort, sex, and trigger processing differently, and the evidence cannot be translated into fixed treatments.

7. Forgiveness, reconciliation and continued relationships are three things: Forgiveness: The process by which an individual reduces revenge or continued resentment. ; Reconciliation: The restoration of a certain relationship between the two parties requires joint participation. ;Continuing a partnership: a realistic choice involving safety, trust and compatibility. ; You can forgive but not get back together, you can not forgive temporarily but still handle things together, or you can leave without forgiveness. No one has the right to force the injured party to forgive in the name of "growth."

Although both parties still loved each other deeply and there was no betrayal, they ended their relationship peacefully and recognized each other's right to withdraw at any time.

items.id: 多元关系与反刻板印象
items.title: Pluralistic relationships and counterstereotyping
items.core: Respect, consent, responsiveness, fairness, trust, and repair are important in most relationships; but different groups also face specific institutional and cultural pressures. Just talking about "love is the same" may ignore discrimination, and talking only about differences may label people.
body: 1. Common mechanisms and special pressures must be seen at the same time: respect, consent, responsiveness, fairness, trust and repair are important for most relationships; but different groups will also face specific institutional and cultural pressures. Just talking about "love is the same" may ignore discrimination, and talking only about differences may label people.

2. Sexual minority partnerships: Same-sex, bisexual, transgender and non-binary couples are not inherently more unstable or free. Additional considerations need to be made: whether, when, and to whom to come out; the safety and respect of one party’s disclosure and one party’s confidentiality. ; Discrimination in the family, workplace, health care, and housing. ;Property, medical, care and inheritance arrangements when the relationship lacks legal recognition. ;The stereotype of bisexuals as “unfaithful/greedy”. ;External projection of gender roles: "Who is male/female?" ; A meta-analysis found that sexual minority stress is negatively related to same-sex couple relationship well-being; this suggests that the problem does not have to come from within the relationship, but may also be external stigma entering the relationship. Internalized stigma and partner marginalization are of particular concern.

3. Consensual non-monogamous relationship: The key difference between non-monogamy and infidelity is whether the parties involved have informed consent. A 2025 meta-analysis that included 35 studies and 24,489 people found no significant differences in overall relationship and sexual satisfaction between monogamous and consensually non-monogamous participants. It does not prove that both forms are equally suitable for everyone, nor does it mean that non-monogamy is free from jealousy, time, and power issues. ;Needs discussion:;Relationship structure and the extent of knowledge of each party. ;Sexual Health and Risk Notices. ;time, resources, disclosure and duty of care. ;New relationship energy, jealousy, privacy and information sharing. ; Is there "forced openness": one party threatens to break up or betrayal to force the other party to agree.

4. Age and life stage: Young people’s relationships are often intertwined with identity formation, education and migration; middle-aged people may have childcare, remarriage and caregiving; older partners need to deal with health, widowhood, property, adult children’s attitudes and digital dating scams. Don’t dismiss the sexual and intimacy needs of older people as non-existent, and don’t dismiss all of young people’s relationships as unserious. ; The obvious age difference itself cannot judge the quality of the relationship, but it is necessary to check: whether the economy, career, housing, experience, social network and decision-making power are highly asymmetric; whether the younger party can freely refuse and withdraw.

5. Disability and chronic diseases: Do not desexualize or infantilize people with disabilities. ; Agree that communication should adapt to differences in language, cognition, senses and actions. ; Differentiate between partner and caregiver roles to prevent mutual exhaustion and power imbalance. ;Discuss pain, fatigue, medications, assistive devices, and possible ways to be intimate. ;Support independent decision-making and do not default to family members’ substitution of parties’ choices.

6. Remarriage, step-parenting and single parenthood: Remarriage is not only the union of two people, but may also reorganize parent-child, ex-partner, financial and ancestral networks. Key point:; Children are not required to immediately treat their stepparents as their biological parents. ; The biological parents are responsible for the main discipline and boundary communication, and the step-family relationship is gradually established. ; Documentation of support, shared expenses, inheritance and housing. ; Collaborate with your ex-partner around the kids without the kids talking or monitoring. ;The new partner does not have to erase past relationships, but needs to have clear current boundaries.

7. Culture, class and region: It is recommended not to assume that everyone has the resources to live alone, have psychological counseling, expensive dating or financial independence. Rural/urban, household registration, education, religion, ethnicity and class will change marriage choices, family involvement and exit costs. Content systems should understand realistic constraints before proposing feasible options.

8. List of anti-stereotype expressions: No need to use: "All men..." "Women are born..." "There is no loyalty problem in same-sex relationships" "Rich people only value value" "It must be complicated to raise children after divorce." ; Change to: "Who specifically did what in your relationship?" "Does this pressure come from individuals, interactions between the two parties, or external institutions?" "Are both parties equally capable of choosing and withdrawing?"

items.id: 中国法律安全与危机转介
items.title: China Law, Security and Crisis Referral
items.core: Updated date: 2026-07-20. The law will change. This document is only for basic reading and does not constitute legal advice on individual cases.
body: 1. First determine whether it is an ordinary relationship issue: the following behaviors should be upgraded to safety issues:; beating, choking, restricting freedom, blocking doors, grabbing mobile phones, smashing or threatening with weapons. ; Forced sexual behavior, sexual behavior while unconscious, threats of private images. ;Continue to track, harass, locate, pretend to log in, or intercept at work/residence. ; Isolating friends and family, restricting work, confiscating income, forcing debt. ; Harming yourself, the other party, children, pets or family members as a means to force reconciliation/obedience. ; Violating breakup boundaries and escalating contact frequency and threats. ; Don’t downplay the danger with “he’s just too in love”, “she’s anxious about attachment”, “both sides are at fault”.

2. China’s Anti-Domestic Violence Legal Basis: The “Anti-Domestic Violence Law” stipulates that domestic violence includes physical, mental and other violations committed by family members through beating, binding, mutilation, restriction of personal freedom, regular verbal abuse, intimidation, etc. The same applies to violence committed between people living together other than family members. ; If a party suffers from domestic violence or faces real danger, he or she may apply to the People's Court for a personal safety protection order. Protection orders may include: Prohibition of domestic violence. ; It is prohibited to harass, follow, or contact applicants and relevant close relatives. ; Order the applicant to move out of his residence. ; Other measures to protect personal safety. ; In principle, the court should make a ruling within 72 hours after accepting the case; in emergency cases, within 24 hours. Local courts or professional legal services should be consulted for specific jurisdiction, materials and enforcement.

3. Preservation of evidence: Preserve without increasing the risk:; alarm and alarm records, warning letters, and inquiry transcripts. ;Medical records, photos of injuries, diagnosis and expense receipts. ;Chats, recordings, emails that threaten, apologize, control or stalk. ;Access control, surveillance, positioning and witness information. ; Financial transfers, forced loans, and account control records. ; Neighborhood committees, village committees, women's federations, schools or units intervene in records. ; Back up to a device or trusted contact that the other party cannot access. Do not deliberately provoke the other party or return to a dangerous scene to collect evidence. ; The opinions of the Supreme People's Court and other departments in 2022 emphasize the privacy and sudden nature of domestic violence, and require relevant departments to assist in collecting and fixing evidence. The 2025 Supreme Court typical case also confirmed that situations such as threatening self-harm with a knife to cause fear may constitute psychological violence; the conclusion of the individual case is still determined by the court in accordance with the law.

4. Immediate safety plan: Leave first when real danger occurs and contact 110; if there is a medical emergency, contact 120. ; Inform at least one trustworthy person and agree on a secret code for help. ; Prepare identity documents, cash/bank cards, medications, keys, charging equipment and necessary clothing. ;Learn about nearby police stations, hospitals, court proceedings and available shelter resources. ; Check shared location, cloud album, family account, smart home and device login. ; If you are bringing children or pets, consider safe evacuation in advance; do not disclose your plans to anyone who may tell the perpetrator. ; The availability of women's federations, legal aid, asylum and hotline services varies across regions, and should be verified through official channels of local government/women's federations/judicial administrative agencies. National numbers and service coverage may also be adjusted.

5. Threats of self-harm or harm to others: Take the threat seriously, but do not bear the responsibility of "you must continue to be in love to save him/her" alone:; When there is immediate danger, specific plans, tools, or loss of contact, contact 110/120 and notify his/her trusted family members or local personnel who can intervene. ; Do not promise confidentiality and do not go to potentially dangerous locations alone. ;Clearly express: "I will contact someone who can guarantee safety, but I will not trade continuing the relationship with you for not harming yourself.";Keep a record of the threat;If the threat is used for control, include it in the security assessment.

6. Reminder on the basics of matrimonial property and divorce: The marriage and family section of the Civil Code involves marriage, spousal relations, property, debt, divorce, child support and relief. Several common misunderstandings:; all debts within a marriage are not automatically joint debts; there are specific rules for the identification of common expressions of intention, family daily needs and debts beyond the scope. ; Husband and wife can make a written agreement on property before marriage and during the marriage relationship. ;The cooling-off period for divorce by agreement is not equal to the cooling-off period for divorce through litigation. ; Disputes such as housework, care contributions, real estate investment, gifts, live broadcast rewards, etc. need to be judged based on current laws and judicial interpretations. ; For major assets, minors, cross-border status, company equity or domestic violence, you should consult a licensed lawyer as early as possible and do not rely on social platform templates.

7. Marriage scams: Be highly vigilant about online dating investments, gambling, virtual currencies, unfamiliar apps, collection and transfer, emergency loans and nude chat blackmail. If you find you have been defrauded: stop making any further payments, save chat and transfer information, contact your bank/payment platform and call the police as soon as possible. Don’t believe that “you can withdraw money by paying the freezing fee”.

Core legal and official sources: National People's Congress website, "Anti-Domestic Violence Law of the People's Republic of China"; Seven departments including the Supreme People's Court, Opinions on Strengthening the Implementation of the Personal Safety Protection Order System.; Supreme People's Court, Typical Anti-Domestic Violence Cases in China in 2025.; Supreme People's Court, Full Text of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China.; Supreme People's Court, Marriage and Family Interpretation (II) Press Conference.; Jiangmen Municipal Public Security Bureau, 2026 Online Dating Investment Scam Alert.

Case: After Xiao Li committed domestic violence, he threatened his wife to withdraw the report. The wife consulted a lawyer and learned that a personal safety protection order could be applied for online. The court issued an injunction in accordance with the law, and the police dealt with it in accordance with the law. In the end, the perpetrator was detained and the victim received legal protection.

items.title: Practical Exercises and Conversation Cards
items.core: These exercises are used for self-reflection, teaching, and low-stakes relationship negotiation. If there is violence, coercion or coercive control, do not practice with two people and use a safety plan first.
body: Exercise 1: Facts - Explanations - Feelings - Actions: | Project | Example |; Let me know in advance." | The goal is not to deny intuition, but to avoid masquerading as fact.

Exercise 2: Ranking of relationship values: Both parties select the top five from the following items and explain the definition of behavior: loyalty, freedom, stability, romance, growth, family, career, sex, financial security, faith, social interaction, adventure, parenting, health, fairness. ; Don’t just compare words for the same, ask: “How do you know loyalty is happening?”

Exercise 3: Green Yellow Red Light: Green Light: Actions that make me feel safe, respected, and connected. ;Yellow light: Behavior that requires slowing down, asking questions, or negotiating. ;Red light: I will not agree to the behavior and need to stop/leave after it happens. ;Respectively used for: chat frequency, social publicity, physical contact, sex, money, both families, mobile phone privacy and conflict.

Exercise 4: Post-Date Review: Answer each item with facts:; 1. Can I express myself naturally instead of acting out all the time? ;2. Is the other party curious and really listening? ;3. When boundaries or small differences arise, how does the other party react? ;4. Does my interest in the other person come from real understanding, or from scarcity/appearance/fantasy? ;5. What is the degree of reciprocity? ;6. Are there any identity, money, sex or safety red flags? ;7. Do I want to see you again? Did the other party also take action?

Exercise 5: Weekly Relationship Meeting (30 minutes): 5 minutes: One thing to say thank you for this week. ;10 minutes: schedules, chores, money and care. ; 10 minutes: one relationship issue; one at a time. ; 5 minutes: Decide who to do, when, and review next time. ; It is prohibited to settle old scores, humiliate, threaten or force all issues to be resolved immediately during meetings.

Exercise 6: Listening rotation: 6 minutes per person:;A speaks for 2 minutes, talking about only one issue. ;B Use 1 minute to repeat without refuting. ;A Correction 1 minute. ;B State something understandable and a curious question. ;Swap roles. ;Enter the plan last. Acknowledging the other person's perspective does not mean agreeing.

Exercise 7: Conflict Pause Protocol: Pre-filled:;Signs that I am overwhelmed: Heartbeat, louder voices, blank mind, wanting to run away. ;Pause statement:______. ; Common pause duration: ______. ; Not to do during the suspension period: post long articles, drink alcohol, contact third parties to provoke, and drive chases. ;Return mode and maximum notification interval: ______.

Exercise 8: Fix List: What I did: ______. ;What impact did it have on you:______. ; My responsibilities: ______. ; What I really regret is: ______. ; Fixes I can do: ______. ; New behavior the next time it is triggered: ______. ;How to check if a change occurred: ______.

Exercise 9: Ten questions before marriage: 1. Do you want children? What if it is difficult to have children? ;2. How to decide when city and occupation conflict? ;3. How to deal with debts, savings, accounts and large expenses? ;4. How to calculate and divide housework and care? ;5. What are the boundaries between parental support and intervention? ;6. How are loyalty and online transgression defined? ;7. How to communicate sexual needs, contraception and health information? ;8. What behaviors are never acceptable in a conflict? ;9. When does psychological, medical, legal or financial help intervene? ;10. How to protect each other and the children if the relationship ends?

Exercise 10: Monthly Review of Relationship Health: Score each from 0–10 and discuss the differences: safety, respect, responsiveness, trust, commitment, sexual satisfaction, conflict repair, fairness, autonomy, and a shared future. ;The score is not a diagnosis. What is more important than the total score is: which item continues to decline, the gap between the two sides' scores is huge, and whether there is a safety red line.

Exercise 11: Digital cleansing after a breakup: Exit shared devices, location, and family accounts. ;Change password and turn on two-step verification. ; Handles shared albums, private images, and cloud backups. ;Cancel automatic payments and shared subscriptions. ; Decide to mute, unfollow or block the scope. ; Common items are handed over with a written list; when there is a safety risk, it will be handled by a third party.

Exercise 12: Advice Quality Self-Check: Before posting any relationship advice, ask:;Does both parties respect consent and the right to withdraw? ;Do you treat group stereotypes as personal facts? ; Is correlation regarded as cause and effect or an inevitable result of commitment? ;Is it possible to help controllers control more effectively? ;Are risks to violence, legal, health or minors ignored? ;Are specific, observable, and reversible actions given?

Case: College students use 'I messages' to practice expressing needs in communication classes, such as 'I feel anxious when I am late and want to be informed in advance'. Through role-playing, both parties learned non-violent communication, and feedback after class showed that relationship tension dropped significantly.

items.id: 经典社交体系的机制、证据与风险边界
items.title: Mechanism, evidence and risk boundary of the classic social system
items.core: 1. Positioning and evidence level 2. Blueprint: Inner state and self-worth
body: Navigation: 1. Positioning and evidence level; 2. Blueprint: Inner state and self-worth; 3. Cold reading: where does the sense of accuracy come from; 4. Mystery: structure, material and expression; 5. Natural flow and structured method; 6. Retainable capabilities and forbidden realization; 7. Analysis checklist; 8. Source entrance

1. Positioning and evidence level: This document breaks down Blueprint, cold reading, Mystery Method and natural flow into "original concept - observable mechanism - risk - ethical translation". It does not regard the course proposition as a relational scientific law, nor does it preserve the original course text, verbatim draft or conventional sentence library. ;Use four levels: ;Strong or direct research evidence: such as the Barnum/Forer effect, confirmation bias, PUA discourse and inequality research. ;Theoretical or teaching framework: can help raise questions and review, such as inner state, structure/material/expression. ; Experience strategies: on-site materials, light structure, dialogue threads, etc.; The effect depends on people, relationships and scenes. ;Course self-statement: such as "attraction loop", "energy", "scientific formula"; cannot be upgraded to determine cause and effect. ; Prioritize observable results when judging effectiveness: whether it is clearer, truer, reciprocal, exitable, and able to stop based on feedback, rather than whether it "completes the process" or makes the other party comply.

2. Blueprint: Inner state and self-worth: [Available mechanisms]; 1. Scenario confidence and relatively stable self-evaluation: familiarity with the environment, appearance or past success will affect current performance; the result of one interaction should not be equated to the overall value. ; 2. External confirmation and self-monitoring: Constantly checking "whether the other person likes me" and "whether I am attractive enough now" will crowd out the attention of the scene and the other person. ; 3. State accommodation: Tension, stuckness and embarrassment can exist; continuing to do a small but appropriate action is more executable than waiting for the perfect state. ; 4. Identity is malleable: "I am not a proactive person" is a temporary rule, not destiny. You can try behaviors that are different from your old identity but that don’t hurt others. ; 5. Process goal: rewrite success as “clearly express, propose next step, respect feedback and review” to reduce the catastrophic outcome of a single time. ; 6. Provide content instead of asking for proof: share true opinions, interests, concerns or arrangements, while allowing the other party not to answer. ;[Must be calibrated];"Core self-confidence" does not mean ignoring rejection or thinking that you are always right. ; "No reaction" should be translated into emotional stability, and should not be translated into denial of harm, rigidity of argument, or cold violence. ; "Self-entertainment" is joint entertainment only when the other party is also willing to participate; if the other party continues to withdraw, stop it. ;"Authenticity" does not exempt empathy, privacy, honesty of material facts, and consent. "Providing value" does not mean ranking people according to high or low value, nor does it mean showing off in exchange for obedience. ; Available questions: "If you don't need this interaction to prove your value, what is the small action you most want to do now to be clear and respectful of feedback?"

3. Cold reading: Where does the sense of accuracy come from: Cold reading is not mind reading. It usually combines the following mechanisms:; | Mechanism | How to generate a sense of accuracy | Romantic contextual risks |; | Barnum/Forer statements | Generalized descriptions treated as personalized insights | Fictional "I know you very well" |; Continuously revise based on expressions, wording, denials and supplements | Treat ambiguous feedback as a sure signal |; | Demographics/Warm Reading | Use high-probability trouble guessing in age, occupation, and culture | Stereotypes and overconfidence |; + Invite correction; for example: "You mentioned twice in a row that you were afraid of disturbing the other party. I'm not sure. It sounds like you may be worried that taking the initiative will appear to be a loss of value. Am I right?"; Maintain three boundaries:; 1. State the uncertainty clearly, without using a diagnostic tone. ;2. Acknowledge that the information comes from the other party or visible materials, and do not pretend to be magical insights. ; 3. If you guess wrong, just update it directly. You don’t need to change your guess to prove that you were “actually right all along.” …

4. Mystery: Structure, material and expression: [A usable debugging framework]; Structure (Structure): Whether the current relationship stage matches the task. When the other person is upset, take over first and don't jump directly to flirting or inviting. ;Material: Whether the content comes from the scene, real information from both parties and the tone of the user, rather than irrelevant conventions. ; Expression (Delivery): Whether the length, intensity, rhythm, timing and medium are appropriate, whether they are sent in succession or do not allow room for response. ; First determine which layer the fault is on, and only change the most important layer. ; [Change M3 to a non-funnel stage consciousness]; | Original stage function | Ethical task | Stop or downgrade signal |; Two-way questioning and moderate self-disclosure | One-sided interrogation or fake common ground |; | Build trust | Rely on time, fulfillment, boundaries and stable behavior | Quick commitment, request for confidentiality or isolation |; The original system's so-called "last-minute resistance" must be rewritten as a space for stopping, acknowledging, and withdrawing; techniques for overcoming rejection must not be provided. ; [Term translation boundary]; IOI → Observe the reciprocal trend over a period of time, without reading the mind...

5. Natural flow and structured method: Natural flow is not "say what comes to mind", nor is it completely unstructured. It typically emphasizes on-the-spot attention, authentic expression, conversational threads, self-disclosure, state accommodation, and feedback calibration. ; A more robust combination is: ; Light structure to judge the current task; → Use on-site and real information to generate content; → Only advance a small step at a time; → Use observable feedback to decide to continue, downgrade or stop; structure can scaffold novices and help review; excessive structure will bring a sense of backlog, treat people as process targets, and ignore feedback. Natural expression is closer to the individual; lack of stage awareness may lead to long-term chatting, missed clarifications, or continuing after rejection. You don’t have to choose one or the other.

6. Retainable capabilities and prohibited realization: [retainable]; state accommodation and reduction of self-monitoring;; on-site collection, observation-expression-invitation;; specific self-disclosure, callbacks and common context;; true expression of interest and low-pressure specific invitation;; structure/material/expression debugging;; two-way screening, trend judgment and review;; low-intensity, exitable, continuous feedback interaction. ; [Forbidden to achieve]; Neg, humiliation, teasing about inferiority points;; Hot and cold, rewards and punishments, jealousy plots, fake future;; Obedience testing, gradual erosion of boundaries;; Falsification of time, identity, social proof or common ground;; Cold reading pretending to be mind reading, information investigation without consent;; Gaslighting, isolation, stalking, threats or retaliation;; Interpreting silence, freezing, drunken state or refusal as consent;; Ignoring feedback in the name of "naturalness", "confidence" and "framework". ; When encountering these requests, explain the mechanism and real risks, and then transform the capabilities that users really need into clear expressions, true demonstrations, boundaries, joint participation, or decent stops.

7. Analysis Checklist: 1. Does the current claim belong to research evidence, teaching framework, empirical strategy or course self-description? ;2. Is the judgment based on visible behavior, generalized sentences, stereotypes or mind reading? ;3. Is the current failure mainly in structure, material or expression? ;4. Is this step real, correctable, rejectable, and exitable? ;5. Is the other party actively participating, or is he just polite, frozen, or passively obedient? ;6. Does the user regard the results as adaptation information or as a trial of self-worth? ;7. Are there alternative actions that are less stressful and provide the same information?

8. Source entrance: Roe & Roxburgh, An overview of cold reading strategies. ; Hyman (1981), The Psychic Reading. ; Johnson et al. (1985), The Barnum Effect Revisited. ; Hambling-Jones & Merrison (2012), Inequity in the pursuit of intimacy. ; Dayter & Rüdiger (2022), The Language of Pick-Up Artists. ; Macmillan, The Mystery Method publishing information. ;Course materials are only used to confirm concepts and versions, and are not used as evidence of effectiveness; original courses, verbatim drafts, and research materials do not belong to runtime Skills.

Case: When a boy was pursuing a girl, he mechanically copied the "push-pull technique" on the Internet and deliberately acted hot and cold towards the girl's advances. At first, the girls felt confused and uneasy. Later, they accidentally saw relevant popular science articles and realized that this was a means of manipulation. She decisively stopped responding and reminded her friends of the boy's behavior pattern. The boy finally gave up because his methods failed.

items.title: Practical Communication and Network Social Strategies: Introduction and Usage Grading
items.core: Consider this directory as a source of words and strategies, not as a psychological law guaranteed to be effective. As long as an expression can help users advance communication, ease the atmosphere, express attraction, maintain boundaries or quickly screen, alternatives can be entered; at the same time, applicable conditions, expected effects, exposure risks and long-term costs are explained.
body: Positioning: Treat this directory as rhetoric and strategy material, not as a psychological law guaranteed to be effective. As long as an expression can help users advance communication, ease the atmosphere, express attraction, maintain boundaries or quickly screen, alternatives can be entered; at the same time, applicable conditions, expected effects, exposure risks and long-term costs are explained. ;Don’t copy mechanically. First confirm the facts, the relationship between the two parties and the user's daily tone, and then rewrite the sentence to make it natural. If users provide chat screenshots or original words, priority will be given to their word length, punctuation and intimacy.

Usage Grading: [A: Can be directly used as a suggestion framework]; First identify and acknowledge the emotion, and then ask the other person if they need listening, companionship, or advice. ; In conflicts, focus on specific behaviors and current issues, and avoid personality attacks, old scores and emotional blackmail. ;Keep compliments specific, real, and describe the positive impact of the other person's behavior. ; Express clear boundaries when rejecting, and do not turn euphemism into vague promises. ; Provide support while retaining the autonomy of both parties, and do not interpret emotional value as unilateral flattery. ; The apology should adopt "acknowledgement of impact + brief explanation + remedial action", and do not dilute responsibility with long self-defense. ;[B: Strategic use];[Universal sentence library];Use ready-made sentences as scaffolding for when users cannot express themselves temporarily. Choose 1–3 sentences and change them to the user's voice. For absolute promises such as "I understand you completely", "Always" and "Definitely", first confirm whether the user is really willing to commit. ; [Tea Art, Coquettishness and Showing Weakness]; Used for ambiguity, flirting, reducing confrontation, giving the other party space to express themselves or expressing "I care about you". Suitable for scenarios where both parties enjoy the interaction and there are no major interest decisions. If you hide your true opinions for a long time, you may end up trying to please someone, lose the initiative, or cause the other party to misjudge their needs. ; Commonly used structures: ; Slight display of weakness + small request that the other party can fulfill; ; Specific affirmation + a little playful exaggeration; ; Express loss but do not accuse + give the other party a chance to repair; ; Take advantage of the situation first + then lead the topic to a meeting or specific actions. ; [Blank space, rhythm and moderate push and pull]; By not over-explaining, leaving part of the arrangement to the other party, and stopping the current round of additions after a clear invitation, observe whether the other party actively invests. If the other party does not clearly refuse, you can make another specific invitation at a different time or scenario based on new information after a reasonable interval; if there is no alternative arrangement twice and there is a continued lack of investment, then downgrade. …

Format of solutions for users: Choose from one to three options according to the complexity of the problem:; 1. Robust version: real, natural, with low long-term risk. ; 2. Flirting version/strategic version: more emotional tension, using humor, blank space, coquettishness, follow-the-scene affirmation or rhythm control. ; 3. Strong version: Emphasizes boundaries, initiative and rapid screening. ; Each wording technique should be accompanied by: sending time, expected effect, key cost, and the next step if the other party is active, vague or does not respond. If the user only wants one sentence, first provide a finished product that can be copied and sent, and then explain it in one or two sentences.

Topic guides in this directory: Conflict and Repair: Universal Argument Techniques: A Guide to Rational Conflict Handling.md; Emotional Responses: Providing Emotional Value to Others: A Guide to Warm and Effective Responses.md; Compliments: Universal Compliment Skills: A Practical Guide to Sincere Recognition.md; Answering: Clever Answering Techniques: Let Communication A more fluid practical guide.md; Turn passive into active: Chatting from passive to active: A practical guide to guide interaction.md; Rejection and boundaries: Rejecting others with high emotional intelligence: A practical guide to respecting boundaries with dignity.md; Investment imbalance and withdrawal: Relationship investment imbalance: Reciprocity judgment, downgrading investment and exit decision-making.md; Embarrassing rescue Field: Resolving Embarrassment: A Practical Guide to Easily Save the Situation.md; Clear Expression: Improving Expression Logic: A Practical Guide from Chaos to Clarity.md; Confidence and Aura: Improving Aura: A Guide to Building a Sense of Power from the Inside Out.md; Social Connections: Effectively Expanding Networks: A Practical Guide from Establishment to Maintenance.md, Being Isolated How to break the situation: A practical guide from self-adjustment to establishing a connection.md; Easy and entertaining reply: Nonsense literature reply guide: Easily cope with various scenarios.md; Sense of scene, relaxed dialogue, easy flirting and advance and retreat calibration: Sense of scene, sense of relaxation and social calibration: From picking up the conversation to advancing the relationship.md; Blueprint Inner state, natural flow, open assumptions and structured interaction: Natural flow, inner state and structured interaction: Ethical competency translation.md; Instant reply, three-level speaking skills, follow-up branches and simulated drills: Practical conversation organizer: Reply from one sentence to subsequent branches.md; Active expression of liking, first meeting, dating experience and natural physical contact: Active expression, first meeting and natural contact.md; The workplace topic guide is only read when the love issue does involve colleague relationships, requests for assistance or power structures.
Assess the other party’s emotional state and relationship stage before using chat skills, choose low-risk expressions, and observe feedback and make timely adjustments
Clearly mark the applicable boundaries of each strategy, for example, humor to resolve embarrassment is only suitable for minor mistakes rather than principled conflicts
For long-term relationships, give priority to sincere communication, use skills as auxiliary tools rather than core means, and regularly reflect on the motivation for use

Case: Xiao Wang used Internet chat skills in social interactions to comfort his lovelorn colleagues, but it backfired because the other party was in a traumatic stage. Later, he changed to listening and accompanying, and explained the potential risks of the original words, which ultimately prevented the relationship from deteriorating.

items.core: ChatLab is responsible for importing, retrieving, counting and returning numbered chat evidence; the dog-headed strategist is responsible for emotional acceptance, fact/speculation separation, relationship judgment and action suggestions. Adaptation does not give Kotou Strategist the ability to directly read or export application databases such as WeChat and QQ.
body: Positioning: ChatLab is responsible for importing, retrieving, counting and returning numbered chat evidence; Doghead Strategist is responsible for emotional acceptance, fact/speculation separation, relationship judgment and action suggestions. Adaptation does not give Kotou Strategist the ability to directly read or export application databases such as WeChat and QQ. ;The upstream contract may change, please refer to the chatlab manifest before running: ;ChatLab external Agent description; chatlab-analyze-cn; chatlab-import-cn

Lock the speaker first: establish and display a fixed mapping before analysis, such as "User=member 17/blue on the right, object A=member 42/white on the left". Do not explain the relationship without confirmation: ChatLab or exported files give priority to sender/member ID, account and session metadata; never judge based on left and right position, tone, gender or "who is more like the user". The left, right and color will vary depending on the application, export method and screenshot taker. ; When screenshots or metadata are missing, only ask a minimal question, asking the user to confirm which side or which nickname is him or her; for one-year records and cross-platform records, take another 2-3 strips of time to check with the anchor points of the short excerpts, and pause the analysis if there is a conflict. ;Cross-file, cross-year and block queries use the same mapping; only reconfirm when the format or account number changes, and cannot be silently flipped due to content, title or pronouns.

Already imported into ChatLab: first check the current command contract and candidate sessions:; chatlab --help; chatlab manifest; chatlab sessions list --format json; let users disambiguate when there are multiple sessions, members with the same name, or "me" is unknown. Use the narrowest private query first, and limit the object and time:; chatlab messages between --member me --member <member> --session <session-id> --last 90d --format agent; chatlab messages search "<keyword>" --session <session-id> --format agent; chatlab messages context --id <message-id> --session <session-id> --window 10 --format agent; when the results are insufficient, check statistics or context, and finally use read-only SQL. Don't use --raw, modify the database, leak full chats, or page without borders for "more comprehensive" purposes.

The exported file provided by the user: first confirm an accurate absolute path; do not guess when there are multiple candidate files. When ChatLab CLI is not installed, only the official installation method is provided, and unauthorized installation is not allowed. ; Read-only preview first: ; chatlab import "/absolute/path/to/chat-export.json" --dry-run --json; Report the recognition format, target session, number of new and repeated messages to the user, without quoting the message text. When the user has explicitly requested the import and the preview result is safe, the same path can be used to officially import; if the user only requires preview, it will stop. Check chatlab formats when the format is not recognized, don't pretend to support it. ;ChatLab can only process export files that have been obtained by the user. When the user said "Help me export WeChat chat", it was clearly stated that the current adaptation can only analyze exported files, and does not call third-party decryption tools or bypass application permissions.

Relationship Trends and K-Lines: Relationship Candlestick Lab can be used as an optional exploration layer. Only aggregation by time, key turning point, event attribution and representative message number are absorbed; K-line price, MACD, RSI, KDJ, mean regression and fixed baseline are not verified relationship measurements and cannot be used to judge love, loyalty or breakup probability, nor can they be written into stable files. When users want to see trends, they should first display explainable active frequency, reply interval, invitation redemption, conflict and repair events, and explicitly mark the subjectivity of model scoring.

Answer and memory boundaries: The beginning of the answer indicates the session and time range of the actual query. Quote evidence numbers such as [#1021] and write separately:; 1. Observable facts: number of initiatives, cashing out, time interval, clear original words. ;2. Reasonable explanation: possible relationship meanings and other explanations. ; 3. Key unknowns: offline interactions, unspoken intentions, and events outside the application. ;4. Recommendation: Low-cost verification of actions, observation windows and stopping conditions. ;Original chats, long summaries and statistics tables do not enter long-term memory. After the first consent, only a brief summary, date and evidence number of key events are allowed to be written into event; the character and intention derived from ChatLab or the model can only be written into hypothesis and cannot be upgraded to object facts.

Case: User suspects his partner is cheating, but only has scattered chat feelings. He first imported three months of WeChat chat records into ChatLab and retrieved specific evidence and timestamps of frequent late-night chats between the other party and a person of the opposite sex. He then handed the numbered evidence to the dog-headed strategist. The strategist analyzed the possibility of emotional transfer based on the evidence and gave action suggestions of calm questioning rather than direct showdown.

items.title: Universal Quarreling Skills: A Guide to Rational Conflict Handling
items.core: Dismantling 4 common misunderstandings in quarreling (with examples): "You didn't do it last time, and it's like this again!" (Get out of the current problem and expand the conflict)
body: 1. Underlying logic (establish the foundation for conflict handling): [1. Cognitive basis: understand the nature of quarrels]; dismantle 4 common quarrel misunderstandings (with examples); turn over old scores: "You didn't do it last time, and you will do it again this time!" (detached from the current problem, expanding the conflict); personal attack: "You are selfish/useless!" (denying personality, rather than targeting specific behaviors); emotional crushing: overpowering the other party, interrupting speech (using momentum to suppress, rather than rational communication); default opposition: "You don't want to solve the problem at all. !" (impose negative motivations and close communication channels); clarify the core goals of the three types of quarrels (refuse to "quarrel for the sake of quarreling"); express needs: such as "I hope you can tell me in advance that you will be home late" (rather than "you always lose contact"); resolve conflicts: such as "let's discuss how to allocate housework next weekend" (rather than "you never do housework"); draw boundaries: such as "I don't like having my phone checked, this is my privacy" (rather than "why are you checking me"); [2. Mentality building: avoid conflict of emotional dominance]; maintain "calm priority": "pause" when emotions come up (such as taking 3 deep breaths and saying "I need 1 minute to calm down"); reject the "victim/attacker mentality": don't dwell on "who is wrong", focus on "how to solve it" (such as Don’t say “You made me angry”, say “Let’s see what the problem is together”); keep the “bottom line of communication”: don’t scold family members, don’t expose private matters, and don’t threaten (such as “No matter how angry I am, I won’t say hurtful words to you”)

2. Skills and techniques (master rational coping methods): [1. Listening and breaking down: first understand the other party before responding]; Capture 2 types of "core signals of conflict"; the other party's "needs behind emotions": For example, the other party says "you always work overtime" → the core is "needing companionship" (not accusing "working overtime"); the other party's "specific dissatisfaction points": such as the other party says "you forgot to buy milk" → the core is "the promise was not fulfilled" (not "you have a poor memory"); 2 steps to disassemble the other party's expression (filter emotional interference); 1. Strip "emotional words": remove extreme words such as "you always/never/at all"; 2. Lock in "specific behaviors": such as "you never care about me" → break it down into "you haven't asked me about my health this week"; [2. Expression skills: Make the other party willing to listen to you]; "I" sentence expression (reduce the other party's defense); Wrong: "You always ignore me and play with your phone after get off work" (accusing the other party); Correct: "I want to chat with you after get off work, and I feel a little lonely when I see you playing with your phone all the time" (express your own feelings + specific behaviors); Focus on "a single issue" (not divergent); Wrong : "You forgot to buy milk, you forgot to pick up the kids last time, and things are always unreliable" (replying old accounts + expanding the problem); Correct: "You forgot to buy milk this time, and I can't make breakfast at night. Can we make a shopping list next time?" (Only talk about the current problem + solution); Appropriate "empathic response" (bringing the distance); if the other party complains that "work is so tiring, you still don't understand" → Response: "I know you have been under a lot of pressure at work recently, and it must be very hard. I either don't understand or I didn't express it clearly just now" (acknowledge the emotion first, then explain); [3. Response skills: do not take the "emotional hook" and guide rational communication]; do not be biased by the other party's emotions (such as the other party calling you "selfish"); Error: "You are selfish!" (escalation of mutual scolding)...

3. Actual combat skills (scenario-based application): [1. Intimacy scenes (couples/family)]; Responding to "the other party complained that "you don't stay with me""; Wording skills: "I know you want me to spend more time with you, but I have been working a lot overtime recently, and I have not taken your feelings into consideration. I'm sorry. How about we set a 'dedicated time' on the weekend, and just spend time with you without looking at the phone?"; Logic: Empathize + apologize first, and then give specific solutions (avoiding the confrontational style of "I have nothing to do, I have to go to work" Response); Responding to "My family is resurrecting an old score, 'You didn't help last time.'"; Words: "I couldn't help you last time, so you must have been uncomfortable, and I'll keep it in mind. This time we will divide the work together, you are responsible for XX, and I will be responsible for XX. Let's finish it as soon as possible, okay?"; Logic: Don't refute old accounts, acknowledge the other party's emotions first, and then focus on the current division of labor (to avoid the dispute of "last time was the last time, this time is different"); [2. Workplace scenario (colleagues/clients)]; Responding to "Colleagues blaming 'You didn't connect well with this matter'"; Words: "Walking about whose fault it is now may delay the progress. Let's check the docking records together first to see which step went wrong. If there is any problem on my side, If you didn't do it right, I'll make it up right away. If you need cooperation, please pay attention, let's solve the problem first." Logic: Don't defend "it's not my fault", focus on solving the problem first, and then implicitly "check the records" for fact checking (to avoid escalation of workplace conflicts); Responding to "Customer dissatisfaction, 'Your service is too poor'"; Words: "I understand your current mood. You must be very anxious when encountering this situation. ...
When arguing, focus on the current specific issue and express your appeal with "this incident" at the beginning to avoid introducing irrelevant mistakes from the past
When you find that you want to settle old scores, pause immediately. First, write down the three main points that you care about most, and then return to the conversation.
Establish a ‘problem list’ mechanism and focus on accumulated issues at a fixed time every week to avoid getting mixed up with old accounts when emotions break out

Case: When the husband and wife were arguing over the allocation of housework, the husband found out that his wife forgot to pay the utility bill three months ago. The wife felt attacked, and the conflict escalated from specific issues to personal accusations, which ultimately required the intervention of a third party to resolve the dispute.

items.title: Universal words and skills to praise others: a practical guide for sincere recognition
items.core: Dismantling 4 common misunderstandings about complimenting people ( Example attached) Vacant without details: "You are awesome" "You are so awesome" (without specific direction, the other party cannot feel "you really care about him", and it is easy to feel perfunctory)
body: 1. Underlying logic (understand the essence of "effective praise" and avoid the trap of perfunctory): [1. Cognitive basis: Praise is not "courteous", but "accurately seeing the value of the other person"]; dismantling 4 common misunderstandings about complimenting others (with examples); vague and without details: "You are awesome" and "you are so awesome" (no specific direction, the other party cannot feel that "you really care about him", and it is easy to feel perfunctory); over-exaggeration: "Your plan is simply perfect, no one can do it better than you" (exaggerating things) Realistic, but makes the other party feel untrue and even stressful); only praise the "external/results" and ignore the "internal/process": the other party stays up late to work on the plan and only says "the plan passed, it's awesome" (not seeing the other party's efforts, it seems that they only value the results and don't care about the effort); contrastive praise: "You did much better than XX, the last plan XX made was a mess" (promoting others by belittling others) Be superior to the other party, which neither respects the third person nor embarrasses the person being praised); clarify the core principles of the three types of effective compliments (making the other party truly feel recognized); sincerity first: do not "compliment for the sake of complimenting", only praise the points that you really agree with (for example, the other party is really careful, then praise "careful", do not praise the qualities that you do not have); specific focus: transform "abstract advantages" into "concrete behaviors" (do not Say "you are careful", say "you even corrected the typos in the notes when checking the report, you are too careful"); fit the needs: praise the other person's "points of concern" (for example, if the newcomer cares about "growth", he will praise "you quickly mastered the process when you first joined the job, and your learning ability is really strong"; if the elder cares about "being needed", he will praise "the cooking skills you taught me, my family said they are delicious, thanks to you"); [2. Mentality building: avoid the sense of violation of "deliberate praise"]...

2. Skills and techniques (master the 4 core methods of "accurate praise"): [1. Detail amplification method: start from "specific behavior" to make the praise have a sense of picture (applicable to all scenarios, the most sincere)]; core logic: capture the other party's "small actions and details", bind "abstract advantages" and "specific behavior", let the other party know "you have really observed him"; Operation steps:; 1. Look for specific behaviors (such as the other party making reports, helping colleagues, way of speaking, etc.); 2. Relevant advantages (extract traits from behaviors, such as "careful, patient, reliable, and able to take care of others"); 3. Organizing words: "When you did XX just now, (specific behavior), this is too (advantage)! "; Example comparison:; The other party helped you organize the meeting minutes; Invalid praise: "Thank you, you are so kind" (general, no details); Effective praise: "You helped me organize the meeting minutes, and even the person in charge of each topic and the time point were clearly marked, so careful! It saved me a lot of trouble when I read it later, thank you so much" (specific behavior + advantages + value brought); [2. Process + result double praise method: praise both "efforts" and "results" (applicable to scenarios where the other party has a clear process of hard work)]; Core logic: When the other party invests time/energy in something, not only praise the "good results", but also the "efforts in the process", so that the other party feels that "my efforts are seen"; Applicable situations Scene: The other party stayed up late working on the plan, revised the work repeatedly, persisted in completing difficult tasks, etc.; Example:; The other party stayed up late to revise the plan, and the client finally approved it; Words: "I know you stayed up two nights for this plan, revised three versions, and even considered the details that the client did not mention in advance. It is normal for it to pass in one go! He is both professional and patient, I admire him so much" (Process: Stay up late to revise three versions, consider the details; Result: Customer approved; Advantages: Professional, patient)...

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application: covering 5 types of high-frequency praise scenarios): [1. Workplace scenarios (praise colleagues, praise leaders, praise subordinates)]; Scene 1: Praise a colleague's PPT report; Wording skills: "Your PPT report today is so amazing! Not only is the logic very clear, from background to plan to expected results, every link is linked, but the charts on each page are so intuitive that even the leaders can't help but nod. I will make PPT in the future. Can I learn from you how to make complex data so good? "; Logic: specific behavior (clear logic, intuitive charts, leader nodding) + advantages (professional, able to present) + expression of "want to learn" recognition, not empty; Scenario 2: Praising the leader's decision; Words: "Last time you decided to tilt the budget of XX channel, I was worried about the effect at the time, but I didn't expect that the conversion rate increased by 20% this month. When you look at a problem, you can always grasp the core and predict the potential of the channel in advance. With you, you can really learn how to look at the problem from an overall perspective." Logic: Objective results (conversion rate increased by 20%) + Advantages (grasp the core, have the ability to predict) + Relate to "what you have learned" to show sincerity and not flattery; Scene 3: Praise your subordinates for completing difficult tasks; Words: "This task is tight and demanding. I know you encountered XX problems, and you also took the initiative to work overtime to adjust the plan. In the end, it was not only completed on time, but also exceeded the expected goals." …
Observe the specific details of the other party, such as 'You were very patient when handling customer complaints just now', which can convey sincere concern more than general compliments
Relate the praise to the other party's efforts, for example, 'This plan shows that you have checked a lot of information', affirm the process rather than talent
Avoid comparative compliments, do not say 'You are much better than your colleagues', focus on individual uniqueness to reduce social pressure

Case: A husband wants to compliment his wife on the newly cooked dinner. If he says "You are great", the wife may feel perfunctory. But he specifically said: "Wife, the braised pork you made today is fat and thin, and it melts in your mouth. It is much better than last time. It seems that you have studied it specially, right?" The wife was very happy after hearing this, because she felt that her husband really paid attention to her efforts and results.

items.title: Providing emotional value to others: A warm and effective response guide
items.core: Dismantling 4 common misunderstandings (with examples) Treating "bottomless pandering" as emotional value: The other party complains that "the boss is unfair", and you say "Indeed, your boss is too stupid" (unprincipled agreement may intensify the other party's negative emotions rather than ease them)
body: 1. The underlying logic (understand the nature of emotional value and avoid the trap of “invalid payment”): [1. Cognitive basis: Emotional value is not "pleasing", but "emotional resonance"]; dismantling 4 common misunderstandings (with examples); treating "bottomless pandering" as emotional value: the other party complains that "the boss is unfair", and you say "indeed, your boss is too stupid" (unprincipled agreement may intensify the other party's negative emotions rather than guiding them); treat "preaching advice" as emotional value: the other party says "I failed to lose weight again", and you say "you just don't have perseverance" ", you should run 5 kilometers every day" (ignoring the other person's "frustration" mood, only giving solutions, showing indifference); treat "self-movement" as emotional value: the other party just casually says "a little tired", and you immediately share your "stress reduction method" in a long speech (without asking the other party if they need it, just focus on your own output, burdening the other party); treat "negative emotions" as emotional value: the other party says "I am so anxious", and you say "what is there to be anxious about?" There are many people who have it harder than you" (deny the other person's feelings, making the other person feel "not understood", which in turn aggravates the negative emotions); clarify the core components of the three types of emotional value (real warm support); empathic understanding: can accurately capture the other person's emotions and make the other person feel "you understand me" (for example, the other party says "work overtime until midnight", and you say "working overtime until so late must be tired and sleepy, too hard"); positive feedback: pay attention to the other party , feel, and share, give a positive response, so that the other party feels "seen" (for example, when the other party shares "cooked a meal" and you say, "This dish looks delicious and delicious, you must have put a lot of thought into it, it's amazing"); Moderate companionship: When the other party needs it, don't be absent or perfunctory, even if you just listen quietly (for example, when the other party is sad, don't say "Don't be sad", but say "I'm here, I'll listen to what you want to say")...

2. Skills and techniques (master the implementation method of "effectively providing emotional value"): [1. Empathic response: the core skill of making the other party feel "you understand me" (applicable when the other party has negative emotions)]; 3-step empathy method (first "accept emotions", then "give understanding", and finally "less suggestions"); 1. Listen and capture emotions: do not interrupt the other party, pay attention to the other party's tone and expression (for example, the other party says "the project is messed up" and the tone is low, indicating that he is "frustrated and self-blaming" at the moment); 2. Confirm the emotion + repeat the feeling: respond with "You must be very XX now" and "It sounds like you are XX" (such as "The project is messed up, you must be very depressed now, and you are also a little self-blame, right?"); 3. Moderate sharing or leaving blank: If you have a similar experience, you can share it briefly ("I have had a situation where the project was not completed well before, and it was very uncomfortable at the time"); if not, leave it blank and let the other party continue ("Do you want to talk about the situation at that time?"); Example comparison:; The other party said "I had a fight with a friend and felt uncomfortable"; Invalid response : "Don't feel uncomfortable, it's normal to quarrel with friends, it will be fine in a few days" (negative emotion + preaching); Empathic response: "It must be very uncomfortable to quarrel with friends, especially when you think about how good you were before, it makes you feel even worse, right? Do you want to tell me why you quarreled?" (confirming emotions + understanding + guiding expression); [2. Positive feedback: techniques to make the other party "seen and recognized" (applicable when the other party shares achievements, contributions, and interests)]; 2 keys: "specific" + "relevant to the other party" (don't generally praise "you are awesome", but praise "the specific thing you did + your characteristics reflected in this thing"); example comparison:; the other party shared "I made a cake for my family today, and it was not burnt for the first time"; invalid feedback: "Wow, that's amazing!" (general, the other party can't feel "you really pay attention")...

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application: covering 5 types of high-frequency scenarios that require emotional value): [1. When the other party is frustrated (failed at work, failed in the exam, plans were ruined)]; Scenario 1: The other party said, "I didn't do a good job and was criticized by the leader, so it's useless."; Wording skills: "It must be particularly uncomfortable to be criticized by the leader, and you will feel that you have not done a good job and blame yourself, right? In fact, who There are times when things are not done well. I was criticized for XX before, and I felt just as uncomfortable as you. If you want to talk about what you didn’t do well this time, I’ll listen. If you want to think about how to improve, we can think about it together." Logic: Empathize with the "uncomfortable" first. ", self-blame" emotions, share your own similar experiences to get closer, and then give the other party the choice of "telling it out" or "finding a solution", without forcing it, showing understanding; Scene 2: The other party said, "I failed to pass the postgraduate entrance examination re-examination, and I have been preparing for so long, but my efforts were in vain"; Speech skills: "I have prepared so much If you fail to pass after a long time, you must be very aggrieved and a little unwilling. You may even feel that your previous efforts have been in vain. This feeling is too uncomfortable. In fact, you have been very perseverant in preparing for so long, and the accumulation during this period will be helpful for other things in the future.
First retell the other party’s factual description to confirm understanding, such as ‘You said the plan was rejected three times’, and then respond to emotions instead of rushing to give suggestions
Distinguish between emotional comfort and factual judgment, use ‘This is really frustrating’ to replace subjective criticisms such as ‘The leader is too bad’
When the topic turns to persistent complaints, gently guide to the solution direction, such as ‘How do you plan to communicate next’

Case: When a colleague complained that the leader was biased, Xiaolin first agreed with ‘It’s really unfair’, and then found that the other party was more emotional. Instead, use "You must be feeling aggrieved. Do you need my help sorting out the problem?" to guide them to analyze rationally instead of getting stuck in emotions.
