items.title: Active expression, first meeting and contact with nature
items.core: This guide is used to turn "I like" into actions that the other party can see and respond to freely: proactive contact, specific invitations, action lists for the first meeting, true expressions of affection, and natural, low-intensity, exitable physical interactions. It is an experience-level social calibration and does not promise that certain words, activities or "suspension bridge effects" will necessarily create attraction.
body: Positioning: This guide is used to turn "I like" into actions that the other party can see and respond to freely: proactive contact, specific invitations, action lists for the first meeting, true expressions of affection, and natural, low-intensity, exitable physical interactions. It is an experience-level social calibration and does not promise that certain words, activities or "suspension bridge effects" will necessarily create attraction.

1. Active gear: one step forward by default: being active does not mean asking more questions, but giving clear information and specific choices earlier. All genders can be active, and any user can select high-active mode. ;| Position | Suitable actions | Calibration method |;| Low initiative | Respond to the other party, express appreciation, accept a clear invitation | The user needs to slow down, or there is little current reciprocity information |;| Regular initiative | Take the initiative to contact, propose specific time and activities, directly express the desire to continue to know more | Ordinary early date default profile |; |; When the user is a male and the target is a female, and is in a common heterosexual dating environment in China, and there is no clear rejection or discomfort, the default suggestion can be raised one level, for example, from "Wait for her to find you" to "You make a specific invitation." This is a situational calibration of common interaction expectations, not a law of "men must chase, women only need to be chased"; the other party's personal preference, the actual investment of both parties, and the user's own style take precedence. Moving up a level also doesn’t mean skipping feedback or automatically upgrading physical contact.

2. Make liking obvious: Use four observable actions instead of "waiting for the other person to realize": 1. Specific appreciation: Explain clearly which detail you remember and why it impresses you, instead of just saying "you are good-looking" and "you are good". ; 2. Take the initiative to contact: When you see something related to the other party, think of a common topic, or simply want to meet, initiate it naturally, without having to calculate who will make the first move so as not to suffer a loss. ; 3. Specific invitation: Give the activity and approximate time, such as "Would you like to go see that exhibition on Saturday afternoon?" instead of saying "I have time to make an appointment" indefinitely. ; 4. Say clearly that you like it: When the relationship and situation are appropriate, directly say "I like getting along with you" and "I really have a crush on you" without requiring the other party to give the same commitment on the spot. ; Don’t regard being deliberately cold, suddenly losing contact, pretending to have other suitors, or suppressing your true feelings as attraction techniques. The sense of rhythm is that you don’t fire continuously in this round, you don’t ask for immediate answers, and you can still be candid and proactive. ; High-concentration praise can be used, but it must be based on real evidence. After the first meeting, you can choose two sincere expressions from the external or on-site status, specific behaviors, and feelings about getting along. Don't pile up a lot of empty adjectives in a row. If the user really thinks so, you can say:;Honestly, you are the most special person I have ever met. It's not just polite, it's your [specific behavior/expression] that makes me feel that you are very different from the people I knew before. ; If "the most special" is not the user's true feelings, reduce it to "there is something special about you" or directly express specific appreciation, and do not make up superlative comments to promote the relationship.

3. Things that need to be done during the first meeting: Do not expand it into a lengthy before/during/after tutorial; give suggestions based on this action list:; Choose a public place that is easy for both parties to reach, where you can talk, and can end at any time, and agree on a rough time. ;Be tidy and punctual, prepare a main activity and an optional extension, and don’t have to fill your schedule. ; Answer the conversation from the scene in front of you and the details that appeared in the chat; you are not only curious about the other party, but also share your own experience and attitude. ; Give specific appreciation at least once, so that the interest is not just polite. ; Based on the other person’s preferences for horror, confinement, movement, noise, and crowds, consider novel or moderately exciting shared experiences such as escape rooms, amusement parks, horror movies, and live performances; if you are obviously repelled, change activities. ; Think of the so-called "suspension bridge effect" as just a popular experience design tip: Shared novelty, excitement, and recall may make a date more enjoyable, but it does not prove or guarantee that the other person likes the user because of it. ;Only attempt low-intensity, exitable approaches or interactions when feedback allows; Do not consider whether physical contact occurs as a dating KPI. ;Tell your true feelings at the end. If you really like someone, express your good feelings that night or sooner and ask to meet again. There is no need to deliberately stay cold for a few days. ; After the first meeting, you can rewrite this original skeleton according to the real details: ; I thought today was just an ordinary meeting, but you turned out to be more interesting than in the chat. Especially the way you talked about [specific details] really made me remember it. Can I still ask you out after that?

4. Natural, low-intensity, withdrawable physical contact: Physical contact is not a ladder of actions that need to be completed in sequence. Combined with the familiarity of the relationship, the atmosphere of the scene, and the distance between the two parties, appropriately create contact opportunities that are natural, low-intensity, and easy for the other party to respond or withdraw, and then focus on the true response without presupposing the next step. ; When the other party takes the initiative to approach, respond naturally, stay relaxed or continue the interaction, you can maintain the current rhythm; when there is continuous positive feedback, make small advances. ; When the other party responds slowly, does not answer back, or cannot see clearly the intention at the moment, end the ongoing contact and return to normal communication without repeated testing in the same round. ; When the other person distances himself, visibly avoids, freezes, pulls away, or expresses discomfort, stop immediately and leave space. ; Shyness does not mean rejection, nor does it automatically mean willingness; you can take the initiative to lead, but you must also see willingness signals such as approaching, responding, continuing interaction, or verbal agreement. ;The more intimate the contact, the greater the need for a clear and consistent positive response. Accepting it once does not mean accepting it by default in the future. ; There is no need to write every action as a mechanical question and answer, nor to deliberately create "accidents" for the sake of contact. A good initiative is to create an opportunity that both parties can naturally catch and adjust based on feedback. ;[Feedback branch];| Feedback | Observable performance | Next step |;| Positive | Approach actively, respond naturally, stay relaxed, extend interaction or verbally say yes | Can maintain or advance slightly, still can exit |; Immediately stop contact and create space without explaining, convincing or testing again |

5. Taking the initiative again after a vague response: no continuous questioning in the same round. Being "busy recently", "not available this week" or not giving a replacement time in time is not enough to request a permanent stop without a clear rejection: wait until there is reasonable new information or interval, then you can change the time or change the scene and make another specific invitation. ;The time didn't match last time. I'm going to [an activity more in line with their preferences] next Wednesday night. Do you want to come with me? ; If the overall trend is still only polite and vague, with no alternative arrangements, no initiative, no extension, and no fulfillment, then adjust investment again. If the other party clearly says that they don’t want to meet, develop, or have any further contact, or express discomfort, then stop the current direction.

Case: The user likes a colleague but doesn’t know how to get closer. He did not express his feelings directly or have a long-term ambiguity. Instead, he first established contact through work topics, and then issued a specific invitation: "A new handicraft store like the one you mentioned opened this weekend. I have reserved two seats. Would you like to go and try it out at 3 o'clock on Saturday afternoon? If it is not convenient, you can choose another day." This kind of low-pressure and withdrawable invitation makes it easier for the other party to agree.

items.id: 关系投入失衡：互惠判断、降级投入与退出决策
items.title: Relationship investment calibration: advance and repair first, then exit when necessary
items.core: This guideline first determines whether the investment difference can be improved through promotion, communication or repair; losses are not calculated first when the relationship is early and when the evidence is insufficient. Only when there is a persistent imbalance, clear rejection or danger, will you turn to adjust your investment or exit.
body: Positioning and evidence boundaries: This guideline first determines whether investment differences can be improved through advancement, communication, or repair; losses are not calculated first when the relationship is early and when evidence is insufficient. Only when there is a persistent imbalance, clear rejection or danger, will you turn to adjust your investment or exit. Responsiveness, commitment, respect, and repair are relationship processes worth observing, but research cannot read the mind of a specific person, and there is no threshold that applies to all relationships: "No return for a few hours = no love" or "Less than the investment ratio is when you should leave." The following steps are a decision-making scaffold, not a diagnostic scale.

1. First, divide it into four areas: | Area | Behavioral evidence | Default action |; For a long time, only users take the initiative; the other party accepts benefits but avoids clear responses; repeatedly misses appointments and does not repair | stop adding more money, reduce investment and set stop conditions |; | clear rejection or danger | has clearly refused, blocked, asked not to contact; or there are threats, stalking, extortion, violence, self-harm threats | stop advancing; start a safety plan when danger |; "busy" can explain a period of low contact, but it cannot automatically offset repeated breaches of appointments, cross-border or long-term non-negotiation. On the contrary, less information does not mean indifference: someone will express their investment by meeting, cashing in, taking care of, and making joint arrangements.

2. Create a one-page factual account instead of an emotional account: look back at the most recent representative interactions and record the events rather than just the reply intervals:; Initiation: Who proposed to meet, call or advance the relationship? Is there an alternative plan if the other party is unable to attend? ; Fulfillment: Are important commitments fulfilled? When failure is achieved, are they explained in advance and remedied? ;Response: After the user expresses his needs, does the other party understand, respect, and care instead of punishing or ridiculing? ;Repair: After a misunderstanding or conflict, is there someone who takes responsibility and implements changes? ; Boundaries and autonomy: Can you say "no", keep your friends and your life, and not give in in exchange for short-term attention? ; Divide each item into "happened", "my explanation" and "don't know yet". Don’t presume to escalate politeness, likes, sexual encounters, gifts, or occasional enthusiasm into evidence of commitment.

3. Action ladder: [1. Advance or clarify first when there is no clear rejection]; when there is insufficient evidence, first choose an action that can generate new information, such as a specific invitation, a true expression, or a repair proposal; only use the following clarification when continued unilateral investment has become a major problem. ;Example: "I enjoy getting along with you, and I also find that I am the one initiating most of them recently. I want to confirm: Do you still want to continue to get to know each other? If so, we can set a comfortable contact and meeting rhythm together; if not, you can also tell me directly."; Clarification is not an interrogation, does not pile up evidence, and does not force immediate commitment. If the other party has clearly refused, do not use "last question" to move forward. ; [2. Use event windows for observation, not universal days]; Bind the window to natural events, such as "whether the next appointment will be honored?" "whether the other party will take the initiative to contact you after finishing the exam" and "whether the next round of shift scheduling can provide executable arrangements." Observe only a small number of behaviors determined in advance and avoid reinterpreting an expression every day. ; [3. Downgrade investment if there is no improvement]; Downgrading can be: stop unilateral planning and rescue; no longer provide money, emotional labor or availability beyond the relationship stage; give time back to friends, sleep, work and new choices. Its purpose should be to restore resource allocation, not to deliberately intimidate or panic the other party. ; Self-examination: "If the other party doesn't come after me, do I still think this step is beneficial to me?" If the answer is no, it may be using exit packaging manipulation. ; [4. Exit when the stop conditions are met]; The stop conditions should come from behavior, such as: breaking an appointment again without explanation; still avoiding for a long time after a clear clarification; crossing the explained boundary again; the user has continued to have insomnia, debt or loss of normal life due to the relationship and the other party is unwilling to negotiate. …

4. Words that can be directly rewritten: Return the initiative: "I am arranging these times. You will tell me when you clearly want to see me next time. I will live at my own pace first."; Reduce investment: "I find that the current way of interaction consumes me a lot. I will reduce contact and extra investment, not to punish you, but to take care of myself."; To end the relationship: "What I need is that both parties are willing to invest and respond. This relationship does not meet this condition, so I decided to stop here. Thank you for the experience, and please respect my decision not to continue personal contact."; Keep business contact here. From now on, we will only communicate about projects/courses/child arrangements, and try to confirm them through text; I will not respond to other topics."; It is not recommended to send sarcastic summaries, bill-like accusations, or "you will regret it." They often prolong the entanglement and allow the user to continue to hand over emotional control to the other party.

5. Correction terms for different relationships: same-sex/transgender/closet relationships: distinguish avoidance of users from protection against discrimination, family or occupational risks. External pressure is understandable, but it cannot be a license to indefinitely conceal, shame, or deny users choice; negotiate disclosure scope and safety plans together. ; Long-distance relationship: Don’t just count the messages, observe whether they jointly arrange calls, meetings, expenses and future actions to shorten the distance. ; Colleagues or classmates: consider power differences, reputation and collaboration costs; maintain professional, necessary, and traceable communication after withdrawing from private advancement. ; Consensual non-monogamous relationship: Determine investment and boundary crossing based on clear agreement between the parties, do not apply default exclusive rules; check informed consent, time resources, sexual health and right to exit. ; Ex or after a breakup: A strong miss is not evidence of repair, but it does not mean no contact forever. When there is no ban on contact, blacklisting or explicit rejection, and the user clearly wants to get back in touch, a light contact can be designed after the emotions and breakup trigger points have stabilized; first clarify the purpose, changes and stop line when there is no response. Getting back together still requires the reasons for the breakup to be concretely addressed, behavioral changes to be observed, and boundaries to be renegotiated.

Core source: Joel et al. (2020), Predictors of relationship quality in a longitudinal dataset of 43 dyads. Supports attention to relationship processes such as commitment, appreciation, satisfaction, and conflict; individual exit thresholds cannot be derived. ;Tasfiliz et al. The man always responded briefly or refused, but did not explicitly refuse to communicate. The woman once wanted to "stop the loss" and delete the other party. items.title: Resolving embarrassment: a practical guide to easily save the situation
items.core: Dismantling 4 types of common misunderstandings (with examples) Pretending "it didn't happen": After the other party says something wrong, he silently lowers his head and plays with his mobile phone (ignoring the embarrassment, but increasing the tension)
body: 1. Underlying logic (understand the nature of embarrassment and avoid invalid operations): [1. Cognitive basis: Make it clear that the core of embarrassment is "unbalanced communication tension"]; dismantle 4 common misunderstandings (with examples); Pretend "it didn't happen": After the other party said the wrong thing, they silently lowered their heads and played with their mobile phones (ignoring the embarrassment, which made the tension more intense); Over-apology/explanation: After knocking over the water glass, you repeatedly said "I'm sorry, I'm so stupid, why was I so careless" (amplifying the mistake, forcing the other party to "comfort you", aggravating the embarrassment ); Changing the topic abruptly: suddenly saying "By the way, do you know what the weather is like today?" during a cold break (it has nothing to do with the previous topic, it seems deliberately abrupt); teasing others to help out: when the other party forgets the words, saying "Are you so nervous that your mind goes blank?" (implying ridicule, making the other party more embarrassed); clarifying the core causes of the three types of embarrassment (targeted resolution); topic disconnection: the chat suddenly has no connection point (such as "after chatting about the movie, no one answered") → Need to "make up the topic naturally"; Mistakes in words and deeds: oneself/the other party said the wrong thing or did the wrong thing (such as "calling the wrong person's name", "knocking something over") → need to "weaken the sense of mistakes"; atmosphere solidification: the atmosphere is tense due to opposing views, exposure of privacy, etc. (such as "talking about salary and being criticized") → need to "reduce tension"; [2. Mentality construction: avoid "the more you panic, the more embarrassed you become"]; accept that "embarrassment is normal": don't regard embarrassment as a "disaster", tell yourself "everyone has encountered it, and will forget it later" (don't criticize yourself "how did I mess up"); maintain a "relaxation": don't rush to "rescue the situation immediately", it doesn't matter if you take it a little slower (such as laughing at the cold scene and then It's more natural to say "Where were you talking about?" than to talk nonsense in a panic); focus on "the other party's feelings": don't worry about "whether I performed well or not", but think about "how to make the other party not uncomfortable" (if the other party said something wrong, help the other party find a step first, and then resolve it)

2. Skills and techniques (master 4 types of core rescue methods): [1. Self-deprecating icebreaker: Use humor to tease yourself and reduce tension (suitable for when you make a mistake, or when the other person is embarrassed by you)]; Core logic: divert attention by "lowering yourself" so that the other person does not need to be nervous and "do you want to comfort you?"; Operational points:; 1. Only laugh at "specific mistakes" and do not deny yourself (don't say "I'm really useless", say "My hands don't seem to listen to instructions today"); 2. Add a "relaxed tone" (said with a smile, using colloquial words such as "Oh" and "good guy"); Examples:; Calling the other person's name by mistake (calling "Sister Li" instead of "Sister Wang"): "Oh, my brain must not have woken up today. Sister Li, please don't mind. It's mainly because you and Sister Wang are both so temperamental. I forgot about it" (joking that "the brain is not awake", praising the other party "Elegant", both apologetic and not embarrassing); I talked about the wrong topic (when I talked about "a certain star got married", the other party said "they divorced long ago"): "Good guy, my news is too late, it seems that I have to ask you to supplement me with more knowledge points about the entertainment industry, otherwise it will be a joke next time" (joking about "the delayed news", asking the other party to "replenish knowledge points", and continuing the topic); [2. Relevant transfer method: Find the "relevant point of the previous topic" to transition without being blunt (suitable for topic breaks and cold breaks)]; Core logic: Don't change topics in vain, find extension points from "the content we just talked about" to make the connection natural; Operation steps:; 1. Recall the keywords of the previous topic (such as just talking about "climbing on the weekend", keywords: mountain climbing, tiredness, scenery); 2. Find "new angles" from the keywords (such as "tired" → Extend "What should I eat to relieve fatigue after climbing the mountain?"; "Landscape" → Extend "Did you take photos?"); 3. Use "Ask/Share" to open a new topic (to avoid the stiffness of "I want to say something"); Example:...

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application: covering 5 types of high-frequency embarrassing scenes): [1. The embarrassment of one’s own mistakes (saying the wrong thing, doing the wrong thing, forgetting things)]; Scenario 1: Calling the leader by the wrong surname (calling “Mr. Zhang” “Mr. Li”); Speech skills: “Mr. Zhang, don’t mind, I was distracted by the project as soon as I got to work today, and my brain was a little short-circuited. You have such aura, I will definitely remember it next time”; Logic: Ridicule “My own brain is short-circuited”, praise the other party’s “aura”, both ways Apologize and give the leader a step forward without looking humble; Scene 2: Knocking over the soup bowl while eating; Speech: "Hey guys, you must have wanted me to taste this soup so much that I ran out! I quickly wiped it, don't splash it on you, you eat first, don't worry about me"; Logic: Use humor to tease "the soup wants to be tasted", take the initiative to say "wipe it yourself", and prevent others from embarrassing "Do you want to help"; [2. The embarrassment of the other party's mistakes (the other party said the wrong thing, forgot something, did the wrong thing)]; Scene 1: The other party is talking about "a certain movie is good", you say "I think it sucks", and the other party freezes; speaking skills: "Hey, I am too blunt. In fact, everyone has different preferences. Do you think There must be something good about you, for example, is the actor's acting skills particularly good? I may not have noticed it at the time." Logic: Apologize first, "speak directly", acknowledge "different preferences", then ask about "actors' acting skills", guide the other party to continue talking, and do not deny the other party; Scenario 2: The other party forgets the agreement with you (such as making an appointment for dinner, but the other party is late and says "forgot"); words: "It's okay. I often forget things. The last time I met a friend for coffee, I only remembered that my friend was on a business trip. ...
Resolve minor mistakes with humor, such as knocking over a water glass and saying, ‘It seems the table also wants to join the discussion,’ and diverting attention
Immediately admit it and briefly remedy it, for example, ‘Sorry, I misremembered the name, I am Xiao Li, nice to meet you.’
Proactively provide steps for others’ embarrassment, such as, ‘This misunderstanding is quite interesting, let’s continue the topic.’

Case: At a friend’s party, a man accidentally spilled a drink on a woman’s skirt while telling a joke, and the scene became silent for an instant. The man did not pretend that nothing was wrong, but immediately handed over a tissue and said humorously: "Oh, I want to add some 'beer print' to your skirt. It seems that my creativity needs to be practiced." The woman burst into tears and smiled, and the tension instantly eased.

body: Positioning and evidence boundaries: This is an experience-level social strategy guide, not a formula that can guarantee attracting or chasing someone. The content refers to the on-site materials, humor and advance and retreat rhythm that appear repeatedly in Tong Jincheng’s public outdoor interactive content. As well as the display, staged chat, emotional value and actual review in the public course catalog of Fan Gongzi. The public video may be edited, scripted or enlarged by the character, and the course catalog can only prove the teaching theme, but not the effect; therefore, only absorb the abilities that can be observed, practiced, and can be stopped or adjusted according to the feedback of the other party; do not copy the character, false wealth display, gender classification, "winning" narrative or force investment through anxiety and competition.

Eight transferable abilities: [1. Display surface: make real life visible]; display surface is not just photos and appearance, but also includes status, expression, life content, way of treating others, and realistic reducibility; photos should be able to clearly see the person, current status, and true interests, without relying on excessive editing or borrowed luxuries; use specific small things to show life in chat. Use empty boasts. ; Offline neatness, punctuality, attitude towards service staff and arrangement ability are often more informative than "high value" slogans; Effect: Reduce unfamiliarity and give the other party something to respond to; Cost: Excessive management will appear performative and may also attract people who are only interested in packaging; On-site materials: start with joint attention]; start with what is happening: venue, food, activities, weather, mutual friends or details the other person just said. This is more natural than memorizing "75 topics"; observation + a little bit of your own feelings + easy to answer small questions; "The song list in this store is more retro than I thought, I almost sang along to that song. Are you here for the food or the atmosphere? ”; Effect: Specific, low pressure, easy for the other party to pick up.; Cost: Asking without sharing will turn into an interview; overly commenting on strangers may appear offensive.; [3. Catch and throw back: make the conversation like playing ball]; A good conversation usually contains four steps, which do not have to be used every time:; 1. Pick up: respond to what the other person is really saying or emotion.; 2. Release: enlarge the interesting details a bit to add to the picture or emotion.; 3. Give: Add some experience, preference or attitude to make the communication two-way; 4. Throw: Leave a point where the other party can come back easily; The other party says "I'm very busy today":; Just ask: "What are you busy with?" Why are you busy? What time do you get off work? "; Just perform: "I'm busier today, I met..."; Throw it back after catching it: "It sounds like you've been drained of work today. …

Output template when calling: When the user says "according to Tong Jincheng's sense of relaxation" or "learn from Mr. Fan's chat method":; 1. First confirm the ability he really wants: sense of presence, humor, presentation, stage diagnosis, flirting or strong screening. ; 2. Adapt it based on the user's natural tone, relationship stage and feedback from the other party, without restoring the host's mantra or pretending to be himself. ;3. Give words that can be used on the spot, the timing of sending or speaking, the expected effect and a major cost. ; 4. Clarify how to continue the green light, how to reduce the yellow light, and how to stop the red light. ; For same-sex, bisexual, transgender, non-binary or non-monogamous relationships, use the same set of "specific people + relationship agreements + immediate feedback" calibration, without presupposing who takes the initiative, who should be pursued, or who must be strong based on gender.

items.title: Practical Speech Arranger: From One-Sentence Reply to Subsequent Branches
items.core: This guide is responsible for arranging the user's goals, the other party's original words and relationship signals into one sentence that can be sent. It does not replace emotional support, factual judgment or relationship analysis, nor does it require users to memorize sentences. The finished product must match the user's usual length, diction, punctuation, intimacy, and current medium.
body: Positioning: This guide is responsible for arranging the user's goals, the other party's original words, and relationship signals into a sentence that can be sent. It does not replace emotional support, factual judgment or relationship analysis, nor does it require users to memorize sentences. The finished product must match the user's usual length, diction, punctuation, intimacy, and current medium.

Five principles that can be used in the Tong Jincheng and Fan Gongzi projects: 1. Attracting is not flattering: the message must contain the user’s own observations, life and choices, not just asking questions around the other party. ; 2. Giving steps is not deception: Invitations, pressure reduction and clarification all give the other party a decent and rejectable exit, but do not use false excuses to cover up major intentions. ; 3. No test of human nature: no need to worry about sudden loss of contact, imaginary enemies, induction of jealousy or secret inspection and testing; use a clear proposal in exchange for real information. ; 4. Diagnose the stuck point first: first determine whether the stuck point is in the presentation, dialogue, emotional connection, invitation, reciprocity, or a practical obstacle. Do not use stronger words to solve all problems. ; 5. Conclusion first, but remain uncertain: give a clear first choice, and then explain it with the original text and behavior; do not write "maybe not interested" as "definitely not like".

One sentence generation process: [1. Set only one goal for this round]; choose only one main strategy from the following seven strategies, and add a very light auxiliary action if necessary. ;| Main strategy | Use signals | What is only accomplished in this round |;| Undertake | The other party is talking, frustrated, excited or sharing | Let the other party feel that the content and emotions are heard |;| Lower pressure | The other party is busy, tired, cold, evasive, or the user has just asked too many questions | Stop adding and keep the stress-free window |;| Teasing | The other party picks up, asks questions, bickers or actively extends | Add a little tension, and then throw the ball back |;| Nudge | The conversation is smooth but only goes in circles | Take the casual chat forward by a small step without committing directly |; | Make an appointment | Have common interests, time window or have received a soft invitation | Reduce the online focus to specific, low-pressure meetings |; | Clarification | Conflicting information, unclear expectations or an unknown will change the decision | Just ask for one key fact |; |;A sentence that simultaneously comforts, flirts, invites, and demands explanation from the other party usually makes the point disappear. ; [2. Combine three layers as needed]; Logical layer: facts, time, place, options, problems and boundaries. ; Emotional layer: humor, ridicule, pictures, suspense, tone and slight reversal. ; Emotional layer: understanding, appreciation, concern, true feelings and relationship willingness. ; Acceptance and repair are usually based on the emotional level; invitations are based on the logical level, and a little emotional level can be added; teasing is based on the emotional level, and there must be an outlet that the other party can accept. Don’t force yourself to have three layers for each sentence. ; [3. Do five tone calibrations]; 1. Length: The other party will not reply with a short essay by default if it says one sentence. …

Common phrase library: The following sentences are skeletons. When using them, replace the square brackets with real details and align them with the user’s tone. ;[1. Just added contact information]; Robust; I just talked about the [specific details] you mentioned, and I found it quite interesting when I came back. How did you start liking it? ; Can flirt; The most unexpected achievement today is not [activity/location], but meeting someone whose eyes light up when talking about [specific topic]. ; Direct; It’s nice to meet you today. I want to continue to get to know you, starting with [specific topic]. ;[2. The other person said "I'm so tired today"]; Steady; It sounds like today has really exhausted you. Do you want to complain first, or take a quiet break? ; will tease; the world today is not very kind to you. I give you two options: complain for five minutes, or owe me a good mood first. ; Simply; you rest first, no need to talk. Come back to me when you want to say something. ; [3. The other party only responds with "haha" or an expression]; Steady; It seems that this round of laughter is in place, I will go and work on it for a while. ; knows how to tease; only smiles but does not catch the ball, so I will win half of this round. ; Strong; OK, let’s stop this topic first. Come back when you have something you want to talk about. ; If this happens for several rounds in a row, there is no need to repeatedly save the situation with the sentence "good at flirting"; end the round and observe whether the other party takes the initiative and is more informative. ; [4. The other party said, "Why are you looking for me all of a sudden?"]; Steady; I happened to see [specific things] and thought of the [details] you mentioned last time, so I came to ask you how you are doing. ; I know how to flirt; I originally had a very serious reason, but after thinking about it, "I kind of want to find you" is more real. ; Strong; just look for it. If you are busy, talk later. ;【5. Transfer invitation from casual chat】; Steady; The [interest/food] you just mentioned reminds me of a [specific place]. Do you want to go and have a look this Saturday afternoon? ;It’s a bit wasteful to talk about this topic on WeChat. I took you to [place] on Saturday and you continued to convince me in person. …

Speech practice mode: When the user says "Practice with me", "Simulate the other party" or "Practice invitation/confession/repair":; 1. Only use the chat, preferences, boundaries and behaviors provided by the user to build a conservative simulation; do not regard the simulation as a prediction of the other party. ; 2. Choose a scenario: ice-breaking, daily pick-up, flirting, invitation, clarification, conflict repair or closing. ;3. Let the user choose real-time prompts or post-event review; only simulate one reply from the other party in each round, waiting for the user to answer the call. ; 4. Review around natural tone, emotion perception, communication rhythm, relationship promotion, boundaries and goals. ; 5. Point out a specific point that is well done and a point that is most worthy of improvement, and give an alternative expression without using fictitious scores to create a sense of accuracy. ;The words in this guide are skeletons, not promises. The user's real details, tone and feedback are always more important than a "high-level speech".

Case: The user wants to reject a colleague’s request to work overtime on weekends, but is afraid of appearing unsociable. He provided his goal (tactful rejection), his colleague’s actual words (“I’ll help you out if I work hard on the weekend”), and relationship signals (normal relationship). The reply prepared by the military counselor was: "I have an emergency at home this weekend and I'm really sorry. If I have time next week, I can help you share some of the burden." It not only made the rejection clear, but also maintained a friendly attitude.

items.title: Smart answering skills: A practical guide to make communication smoother
items.core: Dismantling 4 types of common answering minefields (with examples) Only answer "literal meaning" and ignore emotions: the other party says "I worked overtime until 10 o'clock today, and I am almost exhausted" → answer "Then you go home and sleep quickly" (not responding to the "tired" emotion, appearing indifferent)
body: 1. Underlying logic (understand that the core of "answering" is not "connecting", but "connecting"): [1. Cognitive basis: get rid of the misunderstanding of "invalid answering"]; dismantle 4 common types of answering minefields (with examples); only answer the "literal meaning" and ignore the emotion: the other party said "I worked overtime until 10 o'clock today, and I am almost exhausted" → answer "Then you go home and sleep quickly" (not responding to the "tired" emotion, appearing indifferent); interrupting the conversation and not giving the other party a chance to finish: the other party said "I encountered a very funny thing today..." → Grabbing the conversation "I encountered it last week! It's even funnier than yours" (interrupting the other party's expression, which seems disrespectful); giving a perfunctory response and ending the topic: the other party said "I'm learning to bake recently and made a cake" → followed by "Oh, it's pretty good" (no extension, no interaction, the topic just goes cold); deviating from the core and talking about irrelevant content: the other party said "my cat has always been picky about food recently" → Answer "I bought a new dress yesterday, it looks very good" (completely divorced from the other party's topic, making the other party feel not taken seriously); clarify the core value of three types of answering (the key role of "smart pick-up"); continue communication: use "response + extension" to continue the conversation (such as the other party saying "likes to grow flowers"→ Answer: "Growing flowers must be healing, right? Are you raising succulents or flowering varieties?"); Empathy: Acknowledge the other person's emotions or feelings and close the distance (for example, the other party said, "I was a little sad if I didn't do well in the exam." → Continue: "I will definitely be disappointed if I didn't do well in the exam. I did the same thing last time, and I was very unwilling at the time."); Resolve embarrassment: Use "fill-in answers" to save the situation or smooth things over (if the other person says the wrong thing and gets stuck → Answer "Actually, what you want to say is XX, right? I almost said it wrong before"); [2. Mentality construction: avoid the "stiffness" of answering]; maintain the perspective of "paying attention to the other party": don't worry about "what should I say", but think about "how the other party wants to be responded to" (don't say "I think...", ask more "were you...")...

2. Skills and techniques (master the 4 core methods of "smart answering"): [1. Emotion-priority method: respond to emotions first, then add content (suitable for the other party’s emotional expression)]; Core logic: When people communicate, they “feel” first and then “reason”, acknowledge emotions first, and then talk about specific things; Operation steps:; 1. Grasp the other person’s emotional words (such as “tired, happy, sad, angry”); 2. Start with “affirming emotions + empathy” (such as “Must be very tired”, “This is too happy”); 3. Then extend the topic (ask for details and talk about related experiences); Example comparison:; The other party said, "I had a conflict with a colleague, and I felt very uncomfortable."; Ineffective answer: "Don't argue with him, it's not worth it" (negative emotions, strong sense of preaching); Clever answer: "It must be very annoying to have a conflict with a colleague, is it because of the division of labor?" (First confirm the "angry" emotion, and then ask for details); [2. Keyword extension method: Grasp the "keywords" in the other party's words to expand the topic (suitable for daily chatting); Core logic: Find "talkable points" (such as time, place, events, feelings) from the other party's words, and ask or share around the keywords; Operation steps:; 1. Extract the keywords in the other party's words (such as the other party said "I went to the park to fly a kite on the weekend" → Keywords: weekend, park, kite flying); 2. Choose a keyword extension (preferably choose ones that the other party may be interested in, such as "flying a kite"); 3. Use "Question" or "Share" to answer the conversation (Question: "Is it difficult to fly a kite? Does it always fall down?"; Share: "I did it when I was a child, and every time I ran for half a day, I couldn't fly high. Did it go smoothly when you flew it?"); Example:; The other party said, "I was watching a suspense drama recently, and I was particularly obsessed with it."; Keywords: suspense drama, drama...

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application: covering 6 types of high-frequency communication scenarios): [1. Daily chatting scenes (friends, colleagues, neighbors)]; The other party said, "I lied at home for two days on the weekend and did nothing."; Words: "Lying for two days at home is so comfortable! I don't even have the chance to lie down on the weekend, and I have to work overtime. Are you too lazy to order takeout at home and just eat snacks?"; Logic: First confirm the comfort of "lying for two days" (emotion first), share the comparison of "working overtime" (to close the distance), and then ask about the details of "eating snacks" (Keyword extension); The other party said, "My child loves to draw lately and scribbles everywhere."; Words: "It's great that a child loves to draw, which shows that he has a rich imagination! Does he like to paint bright colors? Have you collected his paintings as souvenirs?"; Logic: First affirm the advantages of "loving to draw" (empathy), ask about the details of "color" (keyword extension), and then bring up the new angle of "collecting paintings to commemorate" (expand the topic); [2. Scenes when the other party confides (family, close friends, colleagues encounter setbacks)]; The other party said, "I failed the interview again, and I feel so useless."; Words: "Failed in the interview must be particularly shocking. I failed in the interview three times last time, and I felt very depressed at the time. Which aspect of the interview did you not perform well in this interview?"; Logic: First affirm the "striking" emotion (emotion first), share your experience of "interview failure" (empathy), and then ask about the details of the "link" (guide the interview) The other party confided); the other party said, "I had a quarrel with my partner and had a cold war for several days."; Words: "The cold war was the most uncomfortable, and I was so worried that no one could say anything. ...
First capture the emotional keywords in the words, such as ‘tired’ and ‘annoyed’, and use ‘You sound tired’ to confirm the emotion
Use open-ended questions to extend the conversation, such as ‘Is this overtime work to catch up on a project?’ to guide the other party to express their deep needs
Avoid giving immediate solutions, first say ‘Do you need me to complain with you for a while?’, and respect the other person’s current needs

Case: A friend said ‘I am almost exhausted from working overtime until ten o’clock’, Xiao Wang directly responded ‘Hurry up to bed’. The other party felt that they were not understood, and the subsequent conversation ended in silence. If it were changed to 'It's really hard to work for so long, do you want to order takeout?' it would be more in line with emotional needs.

items.id: 废话文学回复指南：轻松应对各类场景
items.title: Guidelines for replying to nonsense literature: Easily deal with various scenarios
items.core: Dismantling 4 types of common misunderstandings (with examples) "I don't know" and "casually" (stiff and indifferent, easy to cause dissatisfaction, not real nonsense literature)
body: 1. Underlying logic (understanding the core of nonsense literature): [1. Cognitive basis: make it clear that the essence of "nonsense" is not "useless"]; dismantle 4 common misunderstandings (with examples); regard "perfunctory" as nonsense literature: "don't know" and "casual" (hard and indifferent, easy to cause dissatisfaction, not real nonsense literature); abuse regardless of the scene: saying "this plan is just a plan" in a work report It’s a plan” (using “nonsense” in a serious situation will appear unprofessional); overly roundabout: “About what you asked about, it involves some situations, and these situations have different angles, so the situation is like this” (too confusing, the other party cannot grasp the key point of the response); malicious ridicule: “You are asking this question. , just like a question" (implies sarcasm and violates the principle of "doing no harm"); clarify three types of core values (the actual role of "nonsense"); resolve embarrassment: use non-aggressive expressions to break the ice (if the other party talks about a topic you don't understand, use "This thing sounds interesting, what exactly is it about?"); avoidance Sensitivity: Do not refuse directly, use vague expressions to avoid questions (for example, when asked about salary, use "whatever you earn is enough to spend, I really don't know the exact amount"); ease the atmosphere: reduce communication tension and avoid confrontation (for example, when the other party is arguing, use "Actually, both sides are reasonable, it depends on which angle you look at it"); [2. Mentality construction: avoid the stiff feeling of "using nonsense"; maintain a "natural sense of relaxation": do not deliberately design sentence structures, speak casually like daily chat (do not say "according to my analysis, this matter is like this", say "harm, this matter is not the case") Is that what happened?"); reject "more serious thinking": when using nonsense, don't worry about "whether the logic is right", the focus is on "whether the atmosphere is right" (for example, the other party is serious and "you didn't say it", and responds with a smile "No, it's just a casual chat")...

2. Skills and techniques (master the core method of "nonsense reply"): [1. Core sentence patterns: 4 types of versatile "nonsense templates"]; Repetition (words are repeated, it seems that there is a response but no new information is added); Template: "A, in fact, it is the appearance/situation of A"; Example: The other party asks "Is this movie good?" → "This movie has the feeling of a good movie. If it doesn't look good, no one will watch it." ; Fuzzy type (use "probably/possibly/maybe", without giving a clear answer); Template: "This matter is probably X, maybe Y, it depends on the situation."; Example: The other party asks "Can you go to the party next week?" → "Next week, I probably can go, but maybe I can't go due to something, I'll tell you later depending on the situation."; Transfer type (leading the question back to the other party/irrelevant point, without answering directly); Template: "You asked this, I also want to ask you/what do you think/it depends on (Go back to the original point without advancing the topic); Template: "Let me tell you, you have to look at the situation first, and when the situation is clear, you will know what to do next"; Example: The other party asked "What is the next step for this project?" → "Let me tell you, let's take a look at the current progress for the next step, and when the progress is clear, we will know what to do next"; [2. Scene adaptation: 3 steps to determine when to use nonsense]; 1. Look at the "topic importance": non-critical and non-urgent topics (such as gossip, casual inquiries) are available, important matters (such as medical treatment when sick, work decisions) are not; 2. Look at the "relationship with the other party": Use it with unfamiliar people (such as colleagues chatting, strangers chatting), but less with close people (such as family members, close friends) (to avoid appearing distant)...

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application): [1. Daily greeting scenes (unfamiliar people/during quiet moments)]; Responding to "the other party asks 'how are you doing lately'"; Conversation skills: "It's been like that recently, good or bad, just like usual, how are you lately?"; Logic: Using "repeat + transfer", not only responded to the greetings, but also brought the topic back to the other party, avoiding the cold moment, without revealing too much of the recent situation; Responding to "Talk about what you don't understand" topic (for example, the other party said, "I've been playing XX game recently"); Words: "XX game, it sounds interesting, it should be a fun game, right? I don't usually play games, have you been playing this for a long time?"; Logic: Use "fuzzy + transfer" to admit that you don't understand but don't be embarrassed, use nonsense to talk, and then ask about the other person's situation, so that the other person has something to say; [2. Sensitive interrogation scenarios (private/pressure questions that you don’t want to answer)]; Coping with “being asked ‘How old are you/Why don’t you have a partner yet?’”; Words: “Well, you are at the age you should be. It’s normal to not have a partner. Fate will come when it’s supposed to come. How is your relationship now?”; Logic: Use “repetition + transfer”, don’t answer sensitive questions directly, use nonsense to resolve stress, and then ask the right question. Method to avoid being questioned; response to "being asked, 'How much did you buy this dress/bag?'"; Words: "Oh, I forgot the exact price. I bought it when I liked it, and I didn't calculate it carefully. The quality of your dress looks very good, how much did it cost?"; Logic: Use "fuzzy + transfer", use the excuse of "forgetting the price" to talk nonsense, then praise the other person and change the subject, without revealing the consumption situation; [3. Perfunctory situations at work (don’t want to take the job/don’t want to discuss in depth)]; Dealing with “Colleagues ask ‘Can you help me make this form’ (you don’t want to help)”…

First, distinguish nonsense literature from indifference and perfunctoryness. Nonsense literature is about interesting repetitions, not indifference. Avoid using "I don't know" and "whatever" to reply bluntly.
Don’t abuse nonsense literature in workplace communication. When faced with issues such as work arrangements and demand confirmation, respond accurately to avoid delaying work progress.
Use nonsense literature to adjust the atmosphere when chatting with friends, such as "What I said last time is similar to what I want to say this time" to increase the interest of the chat.

Case: A colleague asked a colleague where to go for a dinner party on the weekend, and the colleague replied, "Anything is fine." Colleagues felt that he was being perfunctory and indifferent. The originally lively group chat suddenly became deserted, and he was never called again for dinner after that.

items.id: 托人办事的高效话术指南
items.title: Guide to efficient speaking skills for entrusting people to do things
items.core: Dismantling 4 types of common tasks Seeing a misunderstanding in speech skills (with examples), suddenly asked: "Get me a qualification certificate, I will ask for it tomorrow" (no foreshadowing, no explanation of difficulty, giving the other party a sense of oppression)
body: 1. Underlying logic (building a solid foundation for service communication): [1. Cognitive basis: understand the core logic of entrusting people to do things]; dismantle 4 common misunderstandings in speech (with examples); sudden demands: "Get me a qualification certificate, I will ask for it tomorrow" (no foreshadowing, no explanation of difficulty, giving the other party a sense of oppression); moral kidnapping : "We have been in a relationship for so many years, and you still won't help with this little work?" (Use friendship to put pressure and ignore the other party's costs); Vague demand: "Help me find a job" (don't mention the industry, position, and time, so the other party has no way to start); No expectation of return: "You Help me first, and then talk about it later" (only mention your own needs, not showing respect for the other party); clarify three types of core principles (rejecting "one-way requests"); first "examine yourself" before "asking for help": first evaluate whether the demand is reasonable (such as "whether the other party is reasonable in this matter" "Able to do it") before speaking; "respect" first and then "ask": do not assume that the other party "must help" and give the other party room to refuse; "explain clearly" first and then "expect": clearly state the needs, difficulty, and time, so that the other party can make rational judgments; [2. Mentality construction: avoid the "sense of pressure" in communication]; maintain an "equal perspective": neither humble nor arrogant (don't say "please, I'll be finished if you don't help me", nor say "this thing is very simple for you"); accept the "possibility of rejection": be prepared for the other party's rejection in advance Be mentally prepared to avoid embarrassment or complaints after being rejected; weaken "result expectations": when communicating, emphasize more on "please take a look" and "it's okay if it's inconvenient" to reduce the psychological burden on the other party

2. Skills and techniques (master efficient communication methods): [1. Preliminary foreshadowing: lowering the acceptance threshold of the other party]; foreshadowing for type 2 scenarios; acquaintances (friends/relatives): first close the distance, and then transition the needs (such as "Sister, I haven't seen you for a long time, how are you recently?... By the way, I encountered something recently, and I want to ask you to do a little favor"); non-acquaintances (colleagues/friends of friends): first associate common points of connection , and then mention the needs (such as "Brother Zhang, I met you through Sister Li before, and I know that you are very experienced in the XX industry... I have a small question I want to ask you recently, and I also want to ask you to lend a hand."); avoid the "zero foreshadowing minefield": do not send sudden messages/calls to directly ask for needs (especially to unfamiliar people), so as to avoid making the other party feel "interrupted"; [2. Expression of needs: clear and specific, reducing the decision-making cost of the other party]; "3 elements" expression (allowing the other party to make quick judgments); 1. State clearly "what to do": specific needs (such as "help me recommend the operation position of XX company" rather than "help me find a job"); 2. Explain "how long it will take": time node (such as "resume needs to be submitted before this Friday, if you are not in a hurry, you can take the time to read it"); 3. Clarify "what needs to be done": the other party's specific actions (such as "just help me submit my resume to HR, and I will follow up with follow-up interviews"); comparison examples; wrong: "help me take care of my children's schooling" (blurred and borderless, making the other party not sure how to respond); correct: "Brother, I My child will go to elementary school next year and wants to go to XX Elementary School. I heard that you know the teachers at the school. Can you help me ask what materials I need to prepare for registration? I don’t need you to ask for help. Just help me find out the process. I can run it myself and won’t trouble you too much." (Be specific, limit boundaries, and reduce stress); [3. Respond to the other party's concerns: Resolve the hesitation of "helping or not helping"]; the other party said "I've been a little busy recently"...

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application): [1. Acquaintance scene (friend/relative/child friend)]; ask friends to recommend jobs; words: "Yangyang, I want to change my job in operations recently. Seeing that you have been working in XX company for 3 years, can you help me recommend the position in your department? I will sort out my resume. Okay, if it's convenient for you, just hand it over to me. If it's inconvenient, it's okay. I'll vote for something else. I'll treat you to a nice meal later, thank you." Logic: mention the common relationship (the other company) first, and then clearly state the requirements (internal recommendation + resume), Give room for rejection and add a promise of repayment (treating you to a meal); ask relatives to help pick up the child; words: "Auntie, I have an impromptu meeting this Thursday afternoon and can't pick up the child. If you are not busy at home, can you help me go to the kindergarten to pick him up? It only takes half an hour. When I get off work, I will go to your house to pick you up. If you have something to do, I will find a trustee, so I won’t bother you.” Logic: state the time (Thursday afternoon), specific matters (pick up the child + duration), proactively provide an alternative (find a trustee), and do not kidnap the other party; [2. Workplace scenario (colleagues/leaders/business partners)]; ask colleagues to help with the work; words: "Sister, this report here requires data from the XX department. You have a lot of contact with them. Can you help me ask if there is the latest archive? I will send you a reference after sorting it out, so as to save you from looking for it later. If you are busy, I will do it myself. Ask, I won’t delay you”; Logic: Explain the “other party’s advantages” (familiar with XX department), mention “two-way benefits” (send data to the other party for reference), and give room for rejection; ask the leader to help fight for opportunities; Words: “Mr. Wang, I have been studying the direction of the XX project recently and have also written a plan. I know that you are very experienced in this area and can Can you help me see if there is anything that needs to be adjusted in the plan? If you have the opportunity to participate in the project, I would also like to ask you to consider me. I will definitely do a good job and live up to your trust...

Before entrusting someone to do something, lay the groundwork first. Ask the other party if it is convenient and explain the background of the matter. For example, "The project at hand is urgent recently, and I would like to ask you for a favor."

Clearly explain the difficulty of the matter and the time required, and do not compress the other party's time. For example, "This proof requires sorting out information, which will take about two hours."
Take the initiative to express gratitude after doing something. Even if the thing is not completed, say "Sorry to trouble you" to maintain interpersonal relationships.

Case: Xiao Wang asked a colleague to help him get a qualification certificate, and he said, "Help me get a qualification certificate. I will ask for it tomorrow." The colleague was busy with the work at hand and refused directly. Xiao Wang could only stay up late to sort it out by himself.

items.id: 提升表达逻辑性：从混乱到清晰的实用指南
items.title: Improving the logic of expression: a practical guide from chaos to clarity
items.core: Dismantling 4 common expression misunderstandings (with examples) "running account" expressions. : Say whatever comes to mind, without focus (for example, reporting on work: "I first made a report in the morning, then had a meeting, the monitor raised the requirements, and then changed the plan, and I also answered a phone call in the afternoon...", the listener cannot grasp the core...
body: 1. Underlying logic (understand the essence of "logical expression" and avoid invalid misunderstandings): [1. Cognitive basis: Logical expression is not "complex", but "makes information transmission more efficient"]; dismantling of 4 common expression misunderstandings (with examples); "running account" expression: say whatever comes to mind, without focus (for example, reporting on work: "I first made a report in the morning, and then had a meeting, and the supervisor raised the demand during the meeting, and then changed the plan, and even answered a phone call in the afternoon...", the listener can't grasp the core); pile of details: drowning in irrelevant information Key point (for example, "going on a trip on the weekend": "I packed my luggage on Friday night and looked for the charger for a long time, but later I found that I put it in my bag. Then I took the subway to the station. There were many people on the subway, and I met an aunt who asked for directions... Finally, I arrived at the scenic spot, and the scenery was not bad." The key point "travel experience" was covered up by trivial matters); confusion of cause and effect: first talk about the result and then the reason, or the cause and the result do not match (for example, asking for leave: "I want to take leave tomorrow because my mother is going there tomorrow I have to stay with her in the hospital. She fell down last week and her knees hurt..." First talk about the needs and then the reasons, and the details of "the fall" can be simplified to avoid logical gaps); terminology stacking: use professional words to pretend to be "logical" without explanation (for example, telling a layman "We use private domain traffic to stratify users and improve conversions through SOP" without explaining "private domain traffic" and "SOP", the other party will not understand, but will feel confused); clarify the three types of logic The core principles of editing and expressing (let the expression be "organized"); first "set up the framework" and then "fill in the content": like drawing the drawings before building a house, determine "what to say first, what to say next, and what to say last" before expressing; "give conclusions" first and then "state the basis": avoid letting the other party "guess the result", for example, in a report, first say "this project can be successful", and then "why it can be successful"...

2. Skills and techniques (master the 4 core methods of "logical expression"): [1. Structured expression: Use "fixed framework" to keep expressions from going off track (applicable to all scenarios, easiest to use)]; 3 types of high-frequency frameworks (with operation steps + examples); Frame 1: Total score (suitable for daily communication and reporting); Operation steps: ① Summary (give conclusion/core first) → ② Points (divided into 2-3 basis/details, with simple examples for each basis) → ③ Summary (reiterate conclusion/prompt action suggestions); Example: say "go on a trip on the weekend"→ Overall: "I traveled to XX Mountain on the weekend and had a great experience"; Points: "Firstly, the scenery is good, you can see the sea of clouds on the top of the mountain, and I took a lot of photos; Secondly, there are not many people, no need to queue, and it is very relaxing"; Overall: "I would like to go again next time I have the opportunity, and I recommend you to try it"; Framework 2: PREP (suitable for outputting opinions and persuading others, such as proposals and debates); Operation steps: ① P (Point: point of view) → ② R (Reason: reason) → ③ E (Example: example) → ④ P (Point: reiterate point of view); Example: say "It is recommended that the company do short video promotion" → P: "I suggest that the company do short video promotions to increase brand exposure"; R: "Because young people now watch short videos, 80% of our target users are active on short video platforms"; E: "The company next door did it last month, the exposure increased by 50%, and brought more than 100 new customers"; P: "So doing short video promotions is very helpful for us to increase exposure and acquire customers"; Framework 3: Timeline (suitable for telling processes and stories, such as project reviews and sharing experiences); Operation steps: ① Past (previous situations/problems) → ② Present (current actions/progress) → ③ Future (next plans/goals)…

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application: covering 4 types of high-frequency expression scenarios): [1. Workplace reporting scenario (reporting work and projects to leaders/colleagues)]; Scenario 1: Reporting "project progress"; Words: "Leader, let me report to you the progress of project XX: The project can currently be delivered on Friday as originally planned (general conclusion). There are two main basis: First, the core parts arrived last week, the assembly team started work yesterday, and now 60% is completed (sub-basis 1 + details) Second, the test team has prepared the test process in advance, and can start testing immediately after assembly (points based on 2 + details). The only thing to note is that the test may take one more day, but we will work overtime to ensure delivery on Friday (pre-determined questions + solutions), so overall, there is no problem in on-time delivery (reiterating the conclusion)"; Logic: Use the "total score" framework, plus "Parallel linking words" (first and second), predict the question of "test time" in advance, so that the report is clear and closed; Scenario 2: Reporting "work problems"; Words: "Colleague, I have a problem that I want to synchronize with you: XX task may be postponed by 1 day (general conclusion). The reason is that the partner said today that an extra 2 days are needed to review the information, causing us to get the information 1 day late (according to the points) According to + causal connection). However, I have communicated with the partners and asked them to review our information first and strive to provide (the solution) before noon tomorrow, so the final delivery time will be postponed from Wednesday to Thursday, which will not affect the follow-up process (reiterating the conclusion + reassurance)"; Logic: first give the "problem conclusion", then talk about the "reason", and add the "solution", the cause and effect are clear, not just to eliminate the problem; [2. Daily communication scenes (talking about things and sharing experiences with friends and family)]; Scene 1: Sharing "feelings of watching movies"; Words: "The "XX Movie" I watched yesterday was very good (general conclusion)...

Refine the core points before expressing them, and use the "conclusion first" approach. For example, when reporting on work, first say "the plan has been decided and the budget needs to be confirmed."

Use the "total, point, and total" structure to sort out the content. First talk about the core conclusion, then explain the reasons for each point, and finally summarize, avoiding a running account style expression.
Proactively screen key information when expressing and remove irrelevant details. For example, if answering the phone has nothing to do with work, there is no need to mention it in the report.

Case: During the weekly meeting, Xiao Li reported that the event was postponed. He first said that he would change the poster in the morning, urge suppliers at noon, and hold another meeting in the afternoon. The leader interrupted and asked how many days the event would be postponed. After changing it to "Conclusion: two days delay; reason: missing batch of materials; coordination required: customer service rescheduling", everyone immediately understood.

items.title: Improving aura: A guide to building a sense of power from the inside out

body: 1. Underlying logic (understand the nature of aura and avoid the trap of “fake aura”): [1. Cognitive basis: Aura is not "pretending to be strong", but "self-stabilizing"]; dismantling 4 types of common cognitive misunderstandings (with examples); treating "speaking loudly" as aura: shouting refutations in meetings without making your point clear (only relying on the volume to exert pressure can easily make people disgusted); using "cold face to show off" When it comes to aura: showing no expression when communicating with others, saying "whatever" and "it doesn't matter" (seemingly cold, but actually "avoiding communication" and having no real sense of power); when using "pretending to be an expert" as aura: talking up an area that you don't understand and saying "I've known this for a long time" (forcibly holding on to the scene, which will be even more embarrassing when exposed) ); regard “boundless” as an aura: never refuse others’ demands and rely on “good old people” to gain a sense of presence (unprincipled compromises will only make people look down upon); clarify the core components of the three types of aura (the source of the real sense of power); inner anchor: clear self-awareness (knowing “who I am, who I am” I won’t accept anything you want”); External consistency: Uniformity in words, deeds, body posture, and tone (for example, “When saying ‘I can do it,’ my eyes do not dodge and my posture does not stoop”); Boundary sense: Gentle but firm rejection of unreasonable demands (without wronging yourself or offending others); [2. Mentality construction: avoid the rigid feeling of "deliberately pretending to be aura"; accept that "aura is developed through practice": do not pursue "one step to get it right", start practicing from "small scenes" (for example, first look at the clerk when checking out at a convenience store and then challenge to speak in public); reject the obsession of "fear of making mistakes" : Aura is not "not making mistakes", but "not panic after making mistakes" (for example, if you say something wrong in a speech, smile and add "I didn't explain this clearly, let me tell you again", it is more aura than freezing)...

2. Skills and techniques (from the outside to the inside, create a landing aura): [1. External performance: 3 "intuitive aura signals" (making people feel the power at first sight)]; Posture: Use a "stable posture" to convey confidence (the core is "not curling up, not shaking"); Standing posture: feet are shoulder-width apart, the center of gravity is between the feet, shoulders are opened 15 degrees back (no tiptoes, no shaking legs, hands hanging naturally or lightly held in front of the body when standing, no shrugging in pockets) shoulder); sitting posture: back straight, buttocks filling 2/3 of the chair (do not sit slumped, do not cross your legs and swing your feet, lean forward slightly 10 degrees when communicating with others, showing concentration); walking posture: steady pace, moderate stride (no procrastination, do not run in a hurry, raise your head and look straight ahead, do not look down at your mobile phone while walking); eyes: use "gentle stare" instead of "dodge or stare"; communicate with others When: looking between the other person's eyebrows or between the eyes (look at each other for 3-5 seconds, and then move away naturally, do not keep staring to make people nervous, and do not look away to show escape the whole time); when speaking/negotiating: look at the whole place (not just looking at one person, nor staring at the ceiling, so that everyone feels that "you are paying attention to him"); speaking speed and tone: use "slow and steady" instead of "fast and chaotic"; Speed: Speak 10%-20% slower than usual (especially when talking about key information, such as "The core of this plan is XX", slow down the speaking speed and emphasize key words); Tone: Don't say "I can do this~" "Do you think it's feasible?", say "I can do this" "Do you think this is feasible", the tone is firm and not hesitant); [2. Inner construction: 2 "aura foundations" (allowing the sense of strength to emerge from within)]; clear "self-boundary": think clearly in advance "what I can accept and what I cannot accept" (to avoid temporary entanglements and appearing to have no opinion)...

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application: covering 4 types of high-frequency scenes that require aura): [1. Workplace scenarios (speaking in meetings, being dumped, talking about needs)]; Scenario 1: Being questioned during the meeting, "Your plan did not consider XX situation"; Wording skills: "The XX situation you mentioned is indeed something we need to pay attention to, but when making the plan, we have already used last year's operating data. After calculation - the impact rate of similar situations at that time was only 5%, and we added XX countermeasures, which can reduce the risk to less than 3%. Do you think this countermeasure needs to be supplemented? "; Logic: first recognize the other party, then use "data" to provide evidence, and finally ask, it is obvious. Professional, not biased by doubts, and with a stable aura; Scenario 2: A colleague wants to offload the work to you and says, "You are better at this, help me do it."; Words: "I have indeed done similar things, but the XX project I am currently working on has to be handed in tomorrow and I don't have enough energy. If you are in a hurry, I can I will send you my previous template, you can refer to it and modify it, and ask me if you encounter any problems. This is more efficient, what do you think? "; Logic: Don't refuse directly, say "your own reasons", and then give "alternatives", which not only keeps the boundaries, but also does not offend others, and has a gentle and powerful aura; [2. Social scenes (being intruded on privacy, kidnapped by morality, socializing with strangers)]; Scene 1: Being asked, "How much is your salary? Why aren't you married yet?"; Words: "My salary is enough for my daily expenses, and I can still save some, but I haven't calculated the exact amount; I am still going along with the matter of getting married. Of course, you care about me so much, do you have any good suggestions?"; Logic: Don't answer directly about privacy, use "vague response" + "change the topic", which is not embarrassing, but also shows the aura of "Don't even think about prying on me"; Scene 2: Being kidnapped by morality "You are so rich" What's wrong with lending me tens of thousands?"; Words: "My current funds have fixed uses, such as paying off mortgages and doing financial management, so I really can't lend them to you...

To improve your aura, practice clear expression first, sort out your opinions in advance during meetings, and express your ideas clearly in concise language, which is more persuasive than loud refutation.
Remain calm and composed. When encountering disagreements, first listen to the other party's point of view and then rebut with reason and evidence to avoid emotional quarrels.
Pay attention to body language, maintain eye contact when speaking, sit upright and upright, which can naturally enhance your personal aura.

Case: At the department meeting, Xiao Chen raised his voice and said "must add" to fight for the budget, but no one answered. The next day, he brought last month's conversion rate, number of customer service orders, and input-output table, and calmly explained the benefits of adding two people, and the supervisor agreed to the pilot on the spot.
