items.core: Dismantling 4 common expansion misunderstandings (with examples) Treat "adding friends" as a network: Participate in events and add WeChat like crazy, but never interact with each other afterwards (there are hundreds of people in the friend list, no one can help when needed, just "invalid friends")
body: 1. Underlying logic (understand the nature of connections, avoid the trap of "invalid social networking"): [1. Cognitive basis: Connections are not “quantity”, but “value resonance”]; dismantling 4 common expansion misunderstandings (with examples); treating “adding friends” as connections: adding people to WeChat like crazy when participating in events, and never interacting after that (there are hundreds of friends in the list, no one can help when needed, they are just “invalid friends”); only “requesting” but not “paying”: just saying “I need XX resources, can you help me” when we first met? ” (Only mentioning one’s own needs and not providing any value, which is disgusting); only focusing on “high-level connections”: ignoring colleagues and partners on the same channel, and only hanging around industry bosses (the bosses have no time to establish valueless connections, but miss the people around them who can help each other); maintenance relies on “holiday group messaging”: sending template messages of “I wish you all the best” during the holidays (untargeted, appearing perfunctory, and even regarded as harassment); clarify the core composition of the three types of connections (real connections) It’s a “two-way rush”); value matching: you have the value that the other party needs (such as information, skills, resources), and the other party also has the value that you need (avoiding “one-way attachment”); trust basis: establishing a “reliable” impression through long-term interaction (such as doing small things promised, sharing information that is true and useful); scene correlation: having common goals in specific scenarios (such as cooperative projects, industry exchanges, interest communities), rather than “unreasonable connections”; [2. Mentality construction: avoid rejection caused by "utility sense"]; maintain an "equality perspective": neither humble nor arrogant (don't say "please lead me", nor "I help you to give you face", communicate with the attitude of "mutual learning/mutual help"); reject "quick fix obsession": Accepting that connections are "slow variables" (for example, exchanging industry information with the other party for 3 months first, and then discussing resource cooperation is more reliable than making demands as soon as you get to know each other)...

2. Skills and techniques (implementation methods from "establishing connections" to "maintaining relationships"): [1. Precise positioning: first clarify "what connections you want" and then find channels (avoid blind socializing); 2 steps to determine the goal of the connections (do not do "purposeless socializing"); 1. Make a "need list": clarify the types of connections you need (such as "Workplace: I need senior operators in XX industry to help me answer user growth problems" "Life: I need partners who like camping to organize activities together"); 2. Find "matching channels": Choose scenarios based on your goals (workplace: industry conferences, vertical communities, in-company training; life: interest groups, charity activities, friend gatherings); avoidance reminder: do not participate in "universal social bureaus" (such as "elite exchange meetings from all walks of life"). This type of bureau has a large number of people and no common topics, making it difficult to establish effective connections; [2. Establishing connections: 3 "natural icebreakers", no embarrassment (when meeting for the first time/adding friends)]; Scene 1: Offline scenes (industry meetings, meetings with friends); Skills: "Use the scene to talk + ask specific questions" (do not say "Hello, let's get to know each other") , say "I heard you discussing XX topic just now. I happen to be doing something in this area. I would like to ask you how to implement the XX method you mentioned?"); Timing to add friends: After chatting about the problem, say "I had a very fruitful chat with you today. Can you add me on WeChat?" If there is relevant information in the future, I can also share it with you." (Use "share information" to give the other party value expectations, not just "add a friend"); Scenario 2: Online scenes (community interaction, comments in friend circles)...

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application: covering 4 types of high-frequency network expansion scenarios): [1. Workplace scenarios (industry conferences, introductions to colleagues, internal training exchanges)]; Scenario 1: At an industry conference, I want to get to know the guest speaker; Speech: "Teacher XX, the XX case I just listened to you, especially the "three key actions for user retention" you mentioned, exactly solved the problem I am currently encountering. I am in the XX industry operation, can I add a WeChat account? I will sort out the user retention plan I made later, and I would like your help to give me some advice. I will also sort out your sharing notes today and send them to you." Logic: first praise the other person's "specific sharing content" (showing that they listened carefully, not blindly chasing stars), tell them about your identity (let the other person know who you are), Use "share notes + please give opinions" to give value, and adding friends is not obtrusive; Scenario 2: Colleagues introduce seniors from other departments and want to establish connections; Speech skills: "Sister Zhang, I heard Xiao Wang say that you are particularly experienced in the field of XX. I have just taken over the job of XX recently, and I don't understand many things. I just have the opportunity to meet you today. Can you add me on WeChat? I would like to ask you occasionally when I encounter problems in the future, and I will also send you the business process of the XX department that I compiled, which may also be helpful for your cross-department collaboration." Logic: Use "colleague introductions" to get closer, express the need to "ask questions," and use "share business processes" to give value to the other party and show a mutual help mentality; [2. Online scenarios (vertical communities, circle of friends interaction, knowledge platforms)]; Scenario 1: In an operational community, I want to get to know group friends who share useful information...
Actively interact within 24 hours after adding friends, such as sending a message saying "I had a lot of fun today and it's nice to meet you" to establish an initial impression.
Regularly maintain your network and send a valuable message to 3-5 friends every month, such as sharing industry information and greetings about recent developments.

Precisely screen when expanding your network, give priority to making friends with people in the same field and have common interests, avoid blindly adding friends, and improve the quality of your network.

Case: Xiao Wang participated in an industry salon and added 80 WeChat messages in two hours, and only posted advertisements in his circle of friends. Three months later, he wanted to find an internal referral, but most people in the group couldn't remember who he was, and only one person remembered that he helped him change his business card at an event.

items.title: Changing chat from passive to active: A practical guide to guide interaction
items.core: Dismantling 4 common proactive misunderstandings (with facts) Example) Talk-stealing initiative: The other party interrupts before he finishes speaking and says, "I'm telling you, last time I..." (depriving the other party of the right to express, showing off one's self, easily making the other party feel disgusted)
body: 1. Underlying logic (understand the essence of "passive chat" and avoid active misunderstandings): [1. Cognitive basis: Passivity does not mean "nothing to say", but "failure to find an entry point for interaction"]; dismantling of 4 common misunderstandings about initiative (with examples); preemptive initiative: the other party interrupts before he finishes speaking and says, "I'm telling you, last time..." (depriving the other party of the right to express, showing off one's self, and easily disgusting the other party); household check-based initiative: continuously asking "How old are you?" Where are you from? How much is the salary? "(Only focusing on "getting information", not sharing yourself, making the other party feel oppressed); One-way output-based initiative: Talk to yourself about "the movies I like, the things I do", and do not pick up the other party's topic (for example, the other party says "I'm afraid of the dark", and you say "I watched a horror movie yesterday which was super exciting", completely detaching from the other party, leaving the other party unable to get in the conversation); Forcibly changing the subject initiative: The other party talks about "tired from work", and you suddenly say, "By the way, do you know what the weather is like today?" " (It has nothing to do with the previous topic, it is intentional and breaks the rhythm of the chat); clarify the core principles of the three types of active chats (initiative means "two-way interaction", not "one-way dominance"); first "answer" and then "extend": do not deny the other party's topic, find an entry point from the other party's words (for example, when the other party says "I stay at home on weekends", first respond with "it is really comfortable to stay at home", and then extend "I watched a variety show at home last time, do you like watching dramas at home?" Are you playing games?"); "Share" first and then "ask": don't just ask "how are you?", first share your own experience, and then guide the other person to say (for example, instead of saying "do you like traveling", say "I went to a small ancient town last week, the scenery is beautiful with few people, do you usually like to go to lively places or quiet places?")...

2. Skills and techniques (master the 4 core methods of "turning passive into active"): [1. Extension method of answering the conversation: "dig out topics" from the other party's words and let the chat continue naturally (suitable for the other party to raise the topic and you want to take the initiative to answer the conversation)]; Core logic: Grasp the "keywords" in the other party's words (such as time, place, feelings, experiences), affirm the other party first, and then use "share + question" to extend to avoid "just answer but not answer"; Operation steps:; 1. Grasp the keywords: the other party said "I went to the art exhibition yesterday, it was very beautiful" (keywords: art exhibition, good-looking, yesterday); 2. First answer and affirm: "Watching the art exhibition is so stylish, it will definitely make people calm down" (acknowledge the other person's choice and don't let the topic end); 3. Share + ask questions and extend: "I have always wanted to go to the exhibition before but didn't have time. Is this art exhibition going to be oil painting or ink painting?" Is there any work that particularly impressed you? " (Share your own experience of "whether you want to go or not", and then ask two specific questions to let the other party have something to say); Example comparison:; The other party said "I was late for work today, and the money was deducted" (Passive response: "Ah, it's so miserable" → End of topic); Active extension: "It's too distressing to deduct money for being late for work (acknowledge the answer)! I was almost late last time, running all the way to catch the subway, but fortunately I was not late in the end (sharing my own experience). …

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application: covering 4 types of high-frequency chat scenarios): [1. Newly met/unfamiliar scenarios (blind date, chatting with friends, chatting with new colleagues)]; Scene 1: The other party asks "What do you do?" (Passive response: "I do operations" → Topics are easy to break); proactive speaking skills: "I am an Internet operator and am mainly responsible for user growth. I usually plan some small activities to attract new users. Sometimes I work overtime when I am busy, but I feel a sense of accomplishment when I see the activities are effective (share details of my work). What industry do you do? Is there anything you find particularly challenging in your daily work? (Guide the other person to say)"; logic: first answer the other person's questions, then add "work content + feelings" (not just "doing operations"), and then use "what do you do + question challenges" to guide the other person to expand, avoid Avoid the embarrassment of "question and answer"; Scenario 2: A game hosted by a friend, sitting together with a stranger, nothing to talk about; proactive words: "The food in this game today is quite delicious, especially the braised pork, which is very soft and rotten (take the scene and share your feelings). You usually like to eat at home Regular dishes or special dishes from outside? Is there any restaurant that makes you feel like "you never get tired of eating it every time"? (Guide the other party to say)"; Logic: Start with the "on-site environment (dish)", and then extend to "food preferences", so that the other party can talk to you and not be left alone; [2. Friend/acquaintance scene (daily chat, friends whom I haven’t seen for a long time)]; Scene 1: A friend says “I’m so bored lately and have nothing to do” (passive response: “Me too”→ End of topic); Active speaking skills: "Boredom can indeed make people lose energy. I tried to put together a jigsaw puzzle at home last week when I was bored. I put together a 1,000-piece puzzle. It took me two days and I felt quite accomplished after finishing it (share my own story). ...

Listen patiently when the other party is speaking, do not interrupt at will, and wait for the other party to finish speaking before expressing your own opinions, such as "I understand what you mean, I used to...".
Use questions to guide the other person to talk more, such as "What happened next?" "What did you think at the time?" to make the other person feel valued.
When taking the initiative to share relevant experiences, first relate the other person's topic, such as "I have encountered this thing you mentioned before..." to enhance the sense of interaction.

Case: During the lunch break, a colleague said that he would take his parents to see a doctor on the weekend. Xiao Zhang immediately interrupted and talked about his experience of accompanying the doctor. He continued talking for five minutes, and the other party just said yes. Later, he changed the question to "How are the test results?" and the chat continued naturally.

items.title: Natural flow, inner state and structured interaction: Translation of ethical capabilities
items.core: 1. Diagnose a main problem first.
body: Navigation: 1. Diagnose a main problem first; 2. Inner state: not perfect feeling; 3. Natural flow generator; 4. Open hypothesis instead of cold reading; 5. Light structure: not an upgrade funnel; 6. Three-layer debugging of structure/material/expression; 7. Feedback determines next step; 8. Output template

Positioning: Used when the user clearly wants to learn the natural flow, the inner state of Blueprint, Mystery structured interaction or cold reading opening, or when the ordinary interaction is stuck in "nervousness, memorizing manuscripts, distracted chatting, misaligned stages, and inability to read feedback". First use the mechanism, evidence and risk boundaries of the classic social system to determine the retainability, and then use this document to implement it. ;Don’t repeat existing topics: ;Need looser sentences, on-the-spot materials or flirting examples, read the sense of scene, relaxation and social calibration. ; If you need an immediate reply and follow-up branches, read Practical Speech Arranger. ;Involves belittling, pushing and pulling, compliance testing, gaslighting or sexual pressure, read PUA, Manipulate Knowledge and Ethical Substitutes and switch to Safe Substitutes.

1. Diagnose a main problem first: | Phenomenon | Main fault | Priority action |; | Very nervous, check your performance repeatedly | Inner state | Accept the tension, narrow the goal to a clear action |; Structural misalignment | Accept the emotion first, and then see if it is suitable to turn |; | The sentence itself is usable but too long, too strong, or repeated | Expression | Shorten, reduce the intensity, and leave room for response |; | Always want to prove "I understand you very well" | Misuse of cold reading | Change to observation-hypothesis-correction |;

2. Inner state: Not perfect Feeling: Use 60 seconds to reset: 1. Naming: Say "I am nervous now/afraid of rejection" instead of writing it as "I can't socialize". ; 2. Implementation: Find three currently visible or audible details, and shift your attention from self-monitoring back to the scene. ; 3. Narrow down: Select only one process goal, such as saying hello, expressing specific appreciation, or making an invitation. ; 4. Permission: Allow the sentence to be imperfect and allow the other party not to be interested. ;5. Action: Complete the action at a time that does not cause stress, and then read the feedback. ; Inner stability is not about “holding the opponent down”. If the other party refuses, the stable behavior is to accept the information, stop pushing, and retain self-esteem.

3. Natural flow generator: [Observation - Expression - Invitation]; specific observation + a bit of your own feelings/views + an invitation that is easy to accept and reject; for example: "You were obviously a little excited when you talked about that store just now, and I was also attracted. Which one do you recommend the most?"; the observation must come from the scene or what the other party actually said. ; Express and provide the user's own information to avoid household registration checks. ;The invitation can be a question, a shared joke, or a next step, and does not require the other party to cooperate. ;[Thread selection];Identify facts, emotions, values, characters, scenes and future actions from the other party's words, and only select the one with the most emotion or the one closest to the current goal. Don't ask questions one by one. ;The other party said, "I have recently changed projects and worked overtime every day, but I can finally go hiking on the weekends.":; I want to take over the emotion: take over the fatigue of "working overtime every day." ; Want to understand the value: pick up "Why do you still want to climb mountains". ; Want to advance the meeting: Take "weekend arrangements" when there is sufficient reciprocity, and propose specific but low-pressure joint activities. ;[Two-way self-disclosure];Every time you ask one or two questions, add some relevant information about yourself. The depth of disclosure increases with relationship stage; don't use trauma, secrets, or quick commitments to create quick intimacy.

4. Open hypothesis instead of cold reading: only use when there is visible evidence:; Fact: "You said twice in a row that you were afraid of disturbing her."; Hypothesis: "I guess you not only don't know how to post, but you are also afraid of taking the initiative to appear cheap."; Correction: "Am I right? Maybe you just don't want to put pressure on her."; When you guess wrong, say: "I understand, I guessed wrong just now." Then use the other party's correction to update, and do not repackage the error into a hit. ; [Banned version]; Use high-hitting generalized sentences such as "You are cold on the outside but hot on the inside" to create a sense of specialness;; Determine personality conclusions based on age, occupation or gender;; Find information privately from social media or mutual friends, and then pretend to guess it on the spot;; Repeat what the other party just revealed, but claim that you have seen through it;; Determine the other party's heart from an expression or interval in the chat screenshot. ; If the user wants to "make her feel like I see through her in a few words", first point out that false insights will damage trust, and then give specific curiosity or praise based on real details.

5. Light structure: not an upgrade funnel: think of interaction as five round-trip tasks: 1. Establish contact: start it real and confirm whether it is convenient now. ; 2. Form a two-way interaction: both parties are providing content, rather than one party performing or interrogating. ; 3. Understand adaptation: Express specific appreciation, but also understand value, rhythm and boundaries. ;4. Propose next steps: Give specific invitations, contact information, or relationship clarification when there is reciprocity. ; 5. Confirmation and review: Both parties clearly agree on the next step; if there is ambiguity, leave space; if they refuse, stop. ;Tasks can be rolled back, stayed or ended. Deep conversation does not equal physical consent, accepting contact information does not equal accepting an invitation, and a date does not equal relationship commitment.

6. Three-level troubleshooting of structure/material/expression: When receiving a chat or review, ask in order: 1. Structure: Is this sentence suitable for the current mood, medium and relationship stage? ;2. Material: Does it come from original words, scenes or real life? Does it fit the user’s tone of voice? ;3. Expression: Do the length, intensity, timing and frequency give the other party room to respond? ; Only output one main fix: ; Structural problem: change the target, such as changing from invitation to acceptance. ;Material issue: Delete the routine and replace it with real details. ;Express the problem: shorten it by half, drop it by one level, and stop the burst.

7. Feedback determines the next step: | Feedback | Observation | Next step |; | Green light | Take the initiative to extend, ask questions, joke, give specific time or alternative arrangements | Only advance a small step |; |; Feedback depends on the trend. Do not regard a single expression, a one-second reply, a long late-night chat or polite cooperation as a definite like.

8. Output template: Main diagnosis: one of internal state/structure/material/expression/feedback; preferred action: only one thing to do now; can be used directly: a sentence that matches the user's tone or an offline action; basis: a visible fact + a tentative judgment; feedback branch: green light to continue a small step; yellow light to decrease; red light to stop; review: whether it is true, two-way, and exitable; which one to practice next time; do not talk about course history in ordinary output. When users clearly want theoretical sources, explain which ones are teaching frameworks, which ones are supported by research, and which ones are just course descriptions.

Case: Xiao Li interrupts others in every team discussion and talks endlessly. Colleagues are unwilling to be in a group with him. He detects that the main problem is to steal the conversation, and then deliberately controls himself.

items.title: Gaining the Favor of Leadership: A Practical Guide from Value Matching to Trust Building
items.core: Breaking down 4 common misunderstandings (with examples), taking "sweet talk" as the core: saying "you have worked hard to lead" every day, but even making basic mistakes in basic work (appearance of politeness has no actual value, and is easily classified as "not pragmatic")
body: 1. The underlying logic (understand the nature of “favor” and avoid ineffective efforts): [1. Cognitive basis: What leaders favor is not "pleasers" but "people who solve problems"]; dismantling 4 common misunderstandings (with examples); taking "sweet talk" as the core: saying "leader, you have worked hard" every day, but even the basic work is wrong (surface politeness has no actual value, and is easily classified as "not pragmatic"); only doing "hard work" without taking "credit": Working overtime every day but with no results, saying "I have worked very hard" (leaders want "results", not "hard work", hard work cannot replace value); excessive "passivity": not doing things unless the leader arranges, saying "the leader didn't let me do it" (lack of initiative, unable to become a "reliable option" for the leader); avoiding "problems": encountering difficulties It is difficult to hide it without telling it, otherwise it will be out of control when the leader finds out (if the leader is caught in "firefighting", he will be considered "unreliable and irresponsible"); clearly define the three types of core values (the abilities that the leader really values); goal alignment: can accurately grasp the focus of the leader's attention (for example, if the leader focuses on "performance growth", you will focus on "user conversion"; if the leader focuses on "efficiency", You will optimize the "process time-consuming"); Closed-loop execution: Do things from beginning to end, so that leaders can "rest assured" (accept tasks → confirm requirements → process synchronization → result feedback, do not pass the blame, and do not give up halfway); proactive filling: can see the unspoken needs of the leader (such as proactively optimizing process loopholes to help leaders reduce "hidden troubles"); [2. Mentality construction: avoid the conflicting feeling of "eager for quick success"; maintain "long-termism": do not pursue "short-term favor", focus on "long-term value accumulation" (for example, continuing to make reports for 3 months and solving two core problems is more effective than giving an occasional gift); reject "humble feeling": neither humble nor arrogant (do not say "I will listen to you in everything", but "I will give you a plan based on your needs, and you will decide the direction"...

2. Skills and techniques (implementation methods from "satisfying needs" to "creating value"): [1. The first step: accurately aligning needs and knowing "what the leader wants" (not doing "useless work")]; 2 methods of "reading the needs thoroughly"; 1. Starting from the "leader's concerns": observe the key words that leaders often mention (for example, they always say "cost", "time" and "risk" in meetings), and prioritize covering them when doing things (for example, when making plans, proactively add "cost control plan" and "risk response measures"); 2. "Second confirmation" when accepting a task: Do not accept the task vaguely, use the "3-element confirmation method" (goal, time, focus), such as "Leader, let me confirm with you again: The core goal of this task is to improve the conversion rate of XX channel, and it needs to be delivered before this Friday, focusing on user retention. If there are any unclear points, I will sync with you at any time." Tips to avoid pitfalls: Don't "take it for granted". For example, if the leader says "make an activity plan", don't just immerse yourself in it, but first ask "Is the activity aimed at new users or old users? What effect do you want to achieve (acquisition/activation/conversion)"; [2. Step 2: Closed-loop execution, so that leaders “don’t have to worry” (creating a “reliable” impression)]; 3-step “closed-loop process” (covering the entire task cycle); 1. Process synchronization: proactively report the progress without waiting for the leader to ask (for example, “Leader, XX task has reached the XX stage, and I encountered XX small problems, I have solved them with XX methods, and I expect to advance to the next step tomorrow” to avoid “the leader will only tell after questioning”); 2. Result feedback: report in a timely manner after completion, not just "finished", but "result + value + follow-up suggestions" (for example, "Leader, XX report is completed, the key data is: XX channel conversion increased by 15%, follow-up can focus on investment; In addition, XX data is found to be abnormal, I have marked it, do you need further analysis?")...

3. Practical speaking skills (scenario-based application: covering 5 types of high-frequency workplace scenarios): [1. Task scenario (to avoid "understanding bias" and show professionalism)]; Scenario: The leader said "make a promotion plan for XX product before next week"; Speech: "Leader, let me confirm with you: Is this promotion plan aimed at attracting new users or promoting old users? Is there a clear direction for the core goals that need to be achieved (such as adding 1,000 new users/increasing repurchases by 20%) ? In addition, is there a scope for the promotion budget and available channels (such as community/short video/offline)? I will set up a framework based on these and synchronize the first draft ideas with you tomorrow morning. Do you think it is okay? "; Logic: Use "goal + budget + channel" to confirm the core needs, and then give a time to "synchronize ideas" to let the leader know that you have a plan and are not blind; [2. Process synchronization scenario (avoid "leader questioning", appear reliable)]; Scenario: The leader has arranged for you to do "user research", which has been carried out for 3 days; Speech: "Leader, synchronize the progress of the user research with you: 200 questionnaires have been collected so far, and the core feedback is concentrated on 3 points: 1. The product operation is complex (40%); 2. The customer service response is slow (30%); 3. I hope to add XX function (accounting for 20%). There are still 100 questionnaires that have not been collected. It is expected to be completed tomorrow and compiled into a report for you the day after tomorrow.…
Do your job well first, ensure zero mistakes in your work, and prove your ability with actual results. You will be more recognized by the leadership than talking sweetly.

Take the initiative to take on additional work. For example, when the leader mentions that the project is lacking people, he takes the initiative to say "I can help organize the information" to show responsibility.
Report your work progress to your leadership regularly, such as sending a short work summary every week to let your leadership understand your work status and results.

Case: Xiao Liu sends "Thank you for your hard work" to the leader on time every day, but the number of customers and turnover in the weekly report are continuously wrong, and attachments are also missing. During the quarterly review, the leader only remembered that he had an enthusiastic attitude, unstable delivery, and that key tasks were not assigned to him.

items.title: How to break through isolation: A practical guide from adapting to building connections
items.core: Breaking down the 4 common misunderstandings that break the situation (with examples) Blind flattering: If others don’t talk to you, you take the initiative to give gifts, help with work, or even make yourself uncomfortable to accommodate the other person (for example, "They like to drink milk tea, and I buy it for them every day, but they are still not accepted." Flattery will only make the other person despise them more)
body: 1. The underlying logic (understand the essence of isolation and avoid the trap of "ineffective breaking"): [1. Cognitive basis: Isolation is not "your fault", but a "relationship adaptation problem"]; dismantling 4 common misunderstandings (with examples); blindly pleasing: if others don't talk to you, you will take the initiative to give gifts, help with work, and even wrong yourself to accommodate the other person (for example, "They like to drink milk tea, I buy it for them every day, and also "I am not accepted", flattering will only make the other party despise him more); Self-denial: Feeling that "I am isolated because I am not good enough", falling into the internal friction of "I have a bad personality and no one likes me" (for example, "They don't play with me, it must be because I am too introverted", ignoring the objective factors of "not being in the same circle"); Fierce confrontation: Finding out that I am isolated Later, he deliberately said "I don't care about playing with them", or even complained behind their backs (for example, "They are just a bunch of small-minded people, I don't care about them", which intensified the conflict and made myself more isolated); passive waiting: feeling that "as long as I wait, they will always take the initiative to care for me", never taking action, and falling into long-term loneliness (for example, " I'm just sitting here, they might come and talk to me", being passive will only prolong the isolation state); clarify the core causes of the three types of isolation (targeted breaking); misunderstanding isolation: due to poor information and rumors, the other party misunderstands you (for example, "Others think you don't want to play with them, but in fact you are too embarrassed to take the initiative") → Need to "actively clarify"; circle-type isolation: you are incompatible with the values and interests of the current group (for example, "colleagues all like to gossip, you like to talk about work, and you can't fit in") → you need to "find the same circle"; exclusion-type isolation: a few people lead others to deliberately ignore you (for example, "some people think you are better than him, and deliberately prevent everyone from talking to you") → need to "stabilize yourself first, and then choose the opportunity to deal with it"; [2. Mentality construction: avoid "internal friction" that drags down the rhythm of the game]...

2. Skills and techniques (implementation method from "self-adjustment" to "establishing connections"): [1. Step 1: Diagnose the type of isolation and find the right direction to break the situation (do not act blindly)]; Step 2 determine the cause of isolation (avoid "one size fits all" to break the situation); 1. Observe the details: See whether the other party is "deliberately neglectful" or "just unfamiliar" (for example: when you take the initiative to speak, does the other party respond perfunctorily, or does he chat normally? If it is the latter, it is most likely because he is "unfamiliar in the circle" and is not really isolated); 2. Find a "key person" to test: Find a relatively friendly and neutral person in the group (such as a classmate in the new class who took the initiative to help you pick up a pen), and ask lightly: "No one seems to talk to me recently. Is there something I haven't done well?" (If the other person says "No, it means that everyone doesn't know you yet", it means misunderstanding/unfamiliarity; if the other person avoids answering, it may be an exclusion type); [2. Step 2: Low-threshold interaction, breaking the "zero connection" state (suitable for misunderstandings and unfamiliar circles)]; 3 types of "non-awkward" interaction skills (start with small actions, don't force yourself to "socialize"); 1. Use "scenario tools" to strike up conversations: use objects and events around you as topics (for example: in the office, "Your keyboard is very easy to use, where did you buy it?"; in the cafeteria, "This dish looks delicious, have you tried it?"); 2. Do "lightweight help": help the other party solve their small needs without being intentional (for example, if the other party forgets to bring a tissue, you hand one over and say, "I have it here, you can use it"; when the other party moves things, you lend a hand and say, "I will help you get some"); 3. Give "positive feedback": pay attention to the other party's small actions and simply praise (for example, if the other party wears new clothes and says, "The color of your dress is very nice"; when the other party completes the work, say, "Your report is really neat")...

3. Practical tactics (scenario-based application: covering 4 types of high-frequency isolation scenarios): [1. Isolation in the new environment (just joined the job/transferred school, no one talks to you)]; Scene 1: In the office, everyone is chatting together, and no one pays attention to you; Talking skills 1 (using the scene to talk): "The XX drama you just talked about, I wanted to watch it before, is there a character in it that is particularly interesting?" (Used in "Common topics" cut through, not blunt); Word Skills 2 (lightweight help): "Your printer seems to have a paper jam. I have encountered it before, can I help you clear it?" (See the other party has a small trouble, take the initiative to help, and close the distance); Logic: Start with small interactions, do not let the other party feel "disturbed" " feeling and slowly build up a sense of familiarity; Scenario 2: No one sits with you at school; Speech Skill 1 (actively join in): "Is there anyone here? Can I sit here? If no one wants to sit with you, just eat by yourself and watch your favorite articles/videos while eating (without showing "loneliness", it will make people feel that "you are very comfortable", and someone may take the initiative to sit with you); Logic: Don't force yourself to "have someone to accompany you", a comfortable state will make it easier to attract others; [2. Misunderstanding isolation (others think you "don't want to play with them")]; Scenario: A small group of friends haven't talked to you recently, and you later found out that someone said, "You think they are childish and don't want to play with them."; Words: "Hey, recently I noticed that you don't seem to talk to me very much, and later I found out that someone said that I think you are childish - which is actually not the case. I didn't take the initiative to play with you before, because I just got here, and I was a little embarrassed...
Stop blindly trying to please and focus on improving yourself, such as using your free time to learn skills to make yourself more valuable.
Take the initiative to establish connections with neutral people in the group, such as eating together, discussing work, and slowly integrating into the small circle.
Stay confident when you are isolated, don't deny yourself, and give yourself positive psychological hints every day, such as "I just haven't found anyone on the same wavelength yet."

Case: New employee Xiao Zhou found that no one asked her for lunch, so she bought milk tea every day and finished the work for others. At the end of the month, no one took the initiative to ask her out. Later, she delivered the plan on time and put forward two executable suggestions at the meeting, and colleagues began to contact her.

items.title: Long-term memory and relational archives
items.core: Reuse streamlined user, object, and relationship information across tasks after the user explicitly consents to it the first time. Memory serves to reduce repeated interpretations, not a complete chat warehouse, nor a permanent judgment on personality.
body: Goal: Reuse streamlined user, object, and relationship information across tasks after the user explicitly consents to it the first time. Memory serves to reduce repeated interpretations, not a complete chat warehouse, nor a permanent judgment on personality.

First time consent: run first:; python3 scripts/memory_store.py status; If it has not yet been enabled, ask in one sentence:; Is the dog-headed military division allowed to save streamlined relationship files on this machine? It will be updated automatically after you agree. Every time you are prompted for changes, you can view, pause, revoke or delete them at any time. ; Only the user’s explicit consent can be run: ; python3 scripts/memory_store.py enable --confirm; After rejection, this task will no longer be asked. When the host does not have file permissions, the script is unavailable, or the command fails, only the current task context is used and there is no persistence.

Five types of memory: | scope | content | qualified sources |; | user | user’s MBTI, subjective comprehensive score, stable goals, preferences, boundaries and communication habits | user’s explicit statement |; | User narrative; ChatLab or tools can only go to this level |; | hypothesis | Tentative explanations of personality, attachment, intention, etc. that can be corrected | User observations or model inferences must have confidence and evidence |; The name, nickname or code name provided by the user can be directly saved as display_label, and recall and reply will be used first. In order to control the memory size, the entire chat, screenshot and exported file continue to remain in the original file or ChatLab; long-term memory only saves fields and key event summaries of no more than 200 words. ; MBTI and subjective ratings are actively asked when creating a profile for the first time; if the user says they don’t know, they can leave it blank. MBTI is saved as explicitly provided by the user or as reported by the subject; subjective scores are saved as 0–100 and marked as user evaluations. Only the score definition given by the user will be interpreted; if there is no definition, it will be called "subjective comprehensive score" and shall not be renamed as willingness, heartbeat, condition or investment score. The same field is updated when the score changes, and the score is not accumulated each time; the old value is overwritten when the MBTI is corrected by the user.

Automatic update: After consent, each round will first determine whether there are high-value changes that will affect future recommendations. If there are no changes, don’t write. Write the current status as a field update of user, object or relationship; write a one-time transition as event; write mind reading or personality interpretation as hypothesis. The same object, same date, and same event fields are considered subsequent updates of the same event; use stable types for fields, such as planned_activity, conflict, repair, and do not create new fields for the same thing. ;Example:;python3 scripts/memory_store.py apply --json '{"scope":"relationship","subject_id":"obj-a","field":"stage","value":"Both parties have confirmed entering the exclusive appointment","source_type":"user_rep ort","source_ref":"turn:current task","occurred_at":"2026-08-02","confidence":"high"}'; After agreeing for the first time, the clearly given profile information can be written into fields: User use scope=user, field mbti/subjective_score; object uses scope=object, field display_label/mbti/subjective_score. Unknown items are not written. Ratings only accept numbers given by the user himself, and models are not allowed to fill in the numbers on their behalf. …

Read and on-demand disclosure: only read the compression context required by the current object:; python3 scripts/memory_store.py context --subject-id obj-a --max-chars 4000; By default, it can load up to the user stable archive, the current object snapshot, a small number of assumptions, and the last 8 key events. Do not inject all objects or complete history into the current answer, and do not write back recalled memories as new information.

User control: View: show, you can add --subject-id obj-a. ; Undo the latest update: undo; If the operation number is retained in the answer, use undo --op-id .... ;Pause/resume: pause, resume. ;Forget object: Confirm the accurate code number first, and then run forget-object obj-a --confirm; This is a hard deletion and clears the undo history. ;Withdraw consent but retain existing data: revoke --confirm. ;Revoke and delete: revoke --delete --confirm. ;Clear all: Run clear --confirm after the user explicitly confirms. ;The script limits a single piece of content to 200 words, the total memory to 200, 20 events for each object, 5 hypotheses, and only retains the latest 20 undoable operations. When the upper limit is reached, low-value events are merged or deleted first, and the capacity is not expanded to avoid restrictions.

Design source: OpenClaw memory: absorb core archives with searchable event layering, plain text reviewable and on-demand recall. ;claude-mem: absorb progressive disclosure, return the compressed index and evidence number first, and do not stuff the entire history into the context. ; Napkin skill: absorb continuous organization, merge duplicates, delete low-value content and category capping. ;Cyrene-Agent and ZifaMem: Assimilate explicit fact/model inference separation, evidence, confidence, conflicts and alternative states. ; Mem0 and Letta: only absorb multi-layer memory and core/archive ideas; this Skill does not introduce resident services, cloud dependencies or unbounded ADD-only accumulation.

Case: For the first time, the user explicitly agreed to reuse information across tasks, telling the AI ​​that he preferred concise responses and did not like redundant explanations. Subsequent AI answers to questions were simplified.

items.title: Emotionally Intelligent Saying No to Others: A Practical Guide to Honoring Boundaries
items.core: Breaking down the 4 common rejection misunderstandings (with examples): blunt and direct type: "No, I'm not free" "Don't ask me, I won't help" (no foreshadowing, no empathy, like "throwing cold water", it is easy for the other party to feel that "you don't value him")
body: 1. The underlying logic (understand the essence of "high emotional intelligence rejection" and avoid hurtful misunderstandings): [1. Cognitive basis: Rejection with high emotional intelligence is not "complimentary compromise", but "clear protection of boundaries"]; dismantling of 4 common rejection misunderstandings (with examples); blunt and direct type: "No, I don't have time" "Don't ask me, I won't help" (no foreshadowing, no empathy, like "throwing cold water", it is easy for the other party to feel "you don't value him"); excessive guilt type: "I'm sorry, I really can't help you, it's all because of my lack of ability, I'm too incompetent" Used" (amplifying self-denial, but forcing the other party to "comfort you", aggravating the embarrassment of both parties); vague and perfunctory type: "Let me see" and "let's talk about it later" (unclear rejection, making the other party have expectations, and follow-up questions are more difficult to handle, such as "You said last time, can you help me now?"); making false excuses: "I have to work overtime" (actually I am resting, which will hurt trust after being exposed, such as the other party seeing your friends chatting together. (can take photos); clarify the core principles of the three types of high EQ rejections (rejection can still be dignified); "empathize" first and then "reject": recognize the rationality of the other party's needs, and then explain your own difficulties (don't say "I can't help you with your busy schedule", say "I particularly understand that you need help, but I am really in an emergency now, and I really can't get away"); first "clarify" and then "give steps": clearly express "can't help", don't be vague and procrastinate, Then give the other party an alternative (don't say "I may not be free", say "I can't help you today, but you can try to find XX. He has done similar things before and should be able to help"); "protect yourself" first and then "not hurt others": do not compromise yourself, and do not accuse the other party of "shouldn't ask for help" (don't say "why do you always ask me for help", say "I have to prioritize the things at hand now, I can't help you, I'm sorry"); [2. Mentality construction: Avoid the internal friction of “rejection is guilt”]…

2. Skills and techniques (master the 4 core methods of "high emotional intelligence rejection"): [1. Buffering rejection: use "empathy + difficulties" to soften rejection and prevent the other party from embarrassment (suitable for friends, colleagues, relatives and other acquaintance groups)]; Core logic: First catch the other party's "demand emotions", and then objectively explain your own difficulties, so that the other party feels "you understand him, but you just can't help" rather than "you don't want to help"; Operation steps:; 1. Empathy and recognition: Respond to the other party's needs with "I understand you" and "I really need help" (for example, if the other party says "Help me change the plan," first follow with "Changing the plan is very time-consuming, I especially understand that you are anxious"); 2. Explain the difficulty: Objectively talk about your own limitations (don't say "I don't want to help", say "But I have to rush my own project report today, and I have to work all night, and I really don't have the energy to help you change it"); 3. Express apology: Apologize simply, without excessive guilt (say "I'm sorry, I can't help you this time", don't say "It's all my fault, I'm so useless"); Examples: The other party said, "Please help me move over the weekend, there are too many things"; Rejection skills: "Moving does require help from others, and I especially understand that you can't move it alone (empathy). However, I have made an appointment to take my parents to the hospital for a review on the weekend, and I have pushed it back several times, and there is really no way to change the time (difficulty)…

3. Practical tactics (scenario-based application: covering 5 types of high-frequency rejection scenarios): [1. Workplace scenarios (colleagues giving up work, leaders adding extra tasks, cross-department asking for help)]; Scenario 1: Colleague says "I have too much on my hands, please help me make this data form, it's very simple"; Wording: "I especially understand that you are too busy (empathy). But I have to rush for the data report of project XX today, and the boss wants it before get off work. I have to concentrate on this, and I really can't spare the time to help you make the form. grid (difficulty). But I can tell you some tips I used to make data tables, such as using the VLOOKUP function to automatically match data, which can save you half the time (alternative solution). I’m sorry, I can’t help you this time (apology)”; logic: use “buffering + alternative”, empathize first, then talk about your own urgent tasks, and give “technical support” without rejecting it. Colleague relationship; Scene 2: The leader said, "Work overtime tonight and help me sort out this material" (you don't want to work overtime); Words: "Leader, I know that this material needs to be sorted out as soon as possible (empathy). However, I have made an appointment to take my child for a physical examination tonight, and I can't change the scheduled time. I really can't work overtime (difficulty). If the materials are not urgent, I will arrive at the company one hour early tomorrow morning. , I will sort it out for you first; if it is particularly urgent, you can see if you can find Xiao Wang. He has worked with me on similar materials before and is familiar with the process (alternative plan). Do you think this will work? "; Logic: Use "buffer + substitution" to give the leader "time substitution" (arrive early tomorrow) and "candidate substitution" (Xiao Wang), which not only refuses to work overtime, but also reflects "for the sake of work"; [2. Life scenes (friends borrowing money, relatives borrowing cars, friends asking for help)]; Scene 1: A friend says, “Lend me 5,000 yuan, and I’ll pay you back next month’s salary.”; Wording skills: “I especially understand that you need money now (empathy).…
Be empathetic before refusing. For example, if a colleague asks you to help work overtime, you can say, "I know you are very busy recently and need help to catch up."
Give a clear reason for rejection, not vague, such as "I have to pick up my children from school today, and I really can't stay and work overtime."
Provide alternatives, such as "I can help you organize the information tomorrow morning, and you can deal with the urgent parts yourself first" to show sincerity.

Case: Before leaving get off work on Friday, a colleague asked Amin to help change the bidding PPT. Amin directly replied "I'm not free, don't look for me", and the other party was silent on the spot. The next day, she explained that she had already arranged it, recommended a template and could help with proofreading for half an hour on Saturday, and the other party expressed her understanding.
